For [[Prov 11:27|he that seeketh after evil things, shall be oppressed by them|observator est malorum, opprimetur ab eis]]. Now Odolla is interpreted *the testimony of their drawing*. And in Proverbs we read: Son, if thou be evil, thou alone shalt draw up evils[[Prov 9:12||]] [the margin gives Prov. ix, 12, after the Septuagint; the Douay-Rheims, following the Vulgate, has: if a scorner, thou alone shalt bear the evil].

paras.t: Decalvare et tondere super filios deliciarum tuarum : id est, o Ecclesia vel prælate, cujus filii olim spiritualibus gratiis abundabant, et nutriebantur in croceis, pane filiorum vescentes, signa doloris assume, et lugubri habitu vesti te, propter spiritualem ruinam, recidivationem, et subversionem filiorum tuorum, qui nunc in terrenis volutantur, stercora amplexantur, carnalibus vitiis inquinantur, et a diabolo capiuntur ac vinciuntur vinculis vanitatis, elationis et incorrigibilitatis. Quemadmodum enim maximum gaudium boni prælati est, gregis sibi commissi profectus (secundum quod ait Joannes in tertia sua Canonica : Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes) ; ita præcipuus mœror ejusdem esse debet gregis sui perversitas.
paras.en: [[1:16|Make thee bald, and be polled for thy delicate children|Decalvare et tondere super filios deliciarum tuarum]]: that is, O Church, or O prelate, whose sons once abounded in spiritual graces and [[Lam 4:5|were brought up in scarlet|nutriebantur in croceis]], feeding on the children's bread, take up the signs of grief and clothe thyself in mourning garb, because of the spiritual ruin, relapse and overthrow of thy sons, who now wallow in earthly things, [[Lam 4:5|have embraced the dung|stercora amplexantur]], are defiled with carnal vices, and are taken by the devil and bound with the bonds of vanity, pride and incorrigibility. For as the greatest joy of a good prelate is the progress of the flock committed to him (as John says in his third canonical Epistle: [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth.|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes]]), so his chief sorrow ought to be the perversity of his flock.

2.title: Expositio capituli secundi: Væ qui cogitatis inutile.
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable.

paras.t: Væ qui cogitatis inutile. Quidam asserunt loqui Prophetam ad decem tribus ; alii vero, ad duas. Sed ad totum duodecim tribuum populum referri hæc possunt. Væ temporalis captivitatis et æternæ damnationis imminet vobis, nisi pœnitueritis, qui cogitatis inutile, id est nociva, seu aliis infligere nocumenta. Quorumdam enim pœna hic incipit, et in futuro continuatur. Constat autem ex isto, quod in cogitatione consistat peccatum. Propter quod Dominus ait in Isaia : Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis. Et operamini malum in cubilibus vestris, exercendo luxuriæ vitia. Unde in Amos præhabitum est : Væ qui dormitis in lectis eburneis, et lascivitis in stratis vestris. In luce matutina, id est cito, festinanter, et mane in ipso diluculo, dum lux solis incipit emicare, faciunt illud, id est, male cogitata in nocte ad effectum deducunt ; quia contra Deum, id est divinæ voluntati ac jussioni contraria, est manus, id est operatio eorum, vel potestas quam a Deo sortiti sunt, qua abutuntur. Unde apud Job dicitur : Cucurrit impius adversus Deum. Et in Levitico Dominus ait frequenter : Si ambulaveritis ex adverso mihi.
paras.en: [[2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ qui cogitatis inutile]]. Some say that the Prophet is speaking to the ten tribes, others to the two. But these things can be referred to the whole people of the twelve tribes. The woe of temporal captivity and of eternal damnation hangs over you, unless you repent, [[2:1|that devise that which is unprofitable|qui cogitatis inutile]], that is, harmful things, or how to inflict harm on others. For the punishment of some begins here and is continued in the life to come. And it is plain from this that sin consists in thought; for which reason the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]]. [[2:1|And work evil in your beds|Et operamini malum in cubilibus vestris]], by practising the vices of lust. Hence it was said before in Amos: [[Amos 6:1|Woe|Væ]] to you [[Amos 6:4|that sleep upon beds of ivory, and are wanton on your couches|qui dormitis in lectis eburneis, et lascivitis in stratis vestris]]. [[2:1|In the morning light|In luce matutina]], that is, quickly, hastily, and early, at the very break of day, when the light of the sun begins to shine forth, [[2:1|they execute it|faciunt illud]], that is, they carry into effect what they wickedly devised in the night; [[2:1|because|quia]] [[2:1|against God|contra Deum]], that is, contrary to God's will and command, is [[2:1|their hand|est manus]], that is, their working, or the power they have received from God, which they abuse. Hence it is said in Job: [[Job 15:26|He hath run against him|Cucurrit impius adversus Deum]] [Denis's wording: "The wicked man hath run against God"]. And in Leviticus the Lord often says: [[Lev 26:21|If you walk contrary to me|Si ambulaveritis ex adverso mihi]][[Lev 26:40||]].

paras.t: Deinde specificat mala istorum. Et concupierunt agros aliorum. In quo patet avaritia horum, quum Dominus jusserit in Exodo : Non concupisces rem proximi tui, non agrum, non servum, etc. Et violenter tulerunt, id est, per potentiam abstulerunt, tanquam raptores et inferiorum oppressores. Et domos alienas concupiscendo, rapuerunt eas vel contenta in eis. De talibus dicitur in Isaia : Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum agro copulatis. Numquid habitabitis vos soli in medio terræ ? Et calumniabantur virum, id est viros egenos, vel subditos aut quietos, et domum ejus, id est posteritatem, prolem, seu familiam, virum et hereditatem ejus, id est possessiones, nec ætati virili nec juvenili parcentes, et proximos suos persequentes in personis et filiis ac rebus eorum. De hac violentia et crudelitate, præsertim quantum ad decem tribus, dictum est plenius super Osee et Amos. Illos enim præcipue persequebantur ac spoliabant, qui relictis aureis vitulis, pergebant ad templum Jerusalem adorare Dominum. Prophetæ autem, quantum ad materiam, in multis coincidunt, quamvis in forma verborum atque metaphoris distinguantur. Nec mirum, quoniam multi eorum eodem tempore et ad eosdem vaticinabantur.
paras.en: Next he specifies their evils. [[2:2|And they have coveted fields|Et concupierunt agros]] of others. In this their avarice is plain, since the Lord commanded in Exodus: [[Ex 20:17|Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's|Non concupisces rem proximi tui]] goods, nor his field, [[Ex 20:17|nor his servant|non servum]], etc. ["nor his field" is not in Exodus 20:17 but in Deut 5:21]. [[2:2|and taken them by violence|Et violenter tulerunt]], that is, they took them away by force, like robbers and oppressors of those beneath them. [[2:2|and houses|Et domos]] of others, coveting them, [[2:2|they have forcibly taken away|rapuerunt]], them or what was in them. Of such it is said in Isaias: [[Is 5:8|Woe to you that join house to house and lay field to field|Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum agro copulatis]]. [[Is 5:8|shall you alone dwell in the midst of the earth?|Numquid habitabitis vos soli in medio terræ]] [[2:2|and oppressed a man|Et calumniabantur virum]], that is, men who are needy, or subjects, or quiet men, [[2:2|and his house|et domum ejus]], that is, their posterity, offspring, or household, [[2:2|a man and his inheritance|virum et hereditatem ejus]], that is, their possessions, sparing neither manhood nor youth, and persecuting their neighbours in their persons, their sons and their goods. Of this violence and cruelty, above all as regards the ten tribes, more has been said on Osee[[Osee 4:1||]][[Osee 9:1||]][[Osee 12:1||]] and Amos[[Amos 8:1||]]. For they chiefly persecuted and despoiled those who, leaving the golden calves, went to the temple at Jerusalem to worship the Lord[[Osee 5:1||]][[Osee 6:9||]]. Now the Prophets agree in many things as to their matter, though they differ in the form of their words and in their metaphors. Nor is this surprising, since many of them prophesied at the same time and to the same people.

paras.t: Idcirco, id est propter hæc mala culpæ, hæc dicit Dominus : Ecce ego cogito super familiam istam, id est tribus Israel, malum, id est justam punitionem seu ultionem : quæ non est mala in se, sed patientibus nocet seu dura est, et mala apparet ; unde non auferetis colla vestra, id est, illud non effugietis, sed portare cogemini, eique subdemini, quemadmodum collum subjicitur oneri. Solent enim circa collum pondera deferenda locari : ideo nomine colli totum, videlicet homo puniendus, signatur. Et non ambulabitis superbi, id est collo erecto in signum interioris tumoris, sed inimicis eritis subditi ac depressi. Cordis namque superbia in incessu solet lucere. Quoniam tempus captivitatis vobis instantis, pessimum est, id est plenum adversitatibus et vindicta : quamvis tempus in se ipso malum non sit, sed secundum ea quæ in ipso fiunt, dicitur bonum vel malum, melius sive deterius. Hæc autem impleta sunt tempore captivitatis decem tribuum ab Assyriis, et duarum a Chaldæis : imo et a Romanis, quia tempore Christi prædicta peccata in populo Judæorum fuerunt. Et post Christi ascensionem bona primitivæ Ecclesiæ partim diripuerunt, atque ex Judaismo in Christum credentes multipliciter calumniabantur, secundum quod dicit Apostolus : Rapinam bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis.
paras.en: [[2:3|Therefore|Idcirco]], that is, on account of these evils of guilt, [[2:3|thus saith the Lord: Behold I devise|hæc dicit Dominus : Ecce ego cogito]] [[2:3|against this family|super familiam istam]], that is, the tribes of Israel, [[2:3|an evil|malum]], that is, a just punishment or vengeance, which is not evil in itself, but harms those who suffer it, or is hard, and seems evil; [[2:3|from which you shall not withdraw your necks|unde non auferetis colla vestra]], that is, you shall not escape it, but shall be forced to bear it and shall be put under it, as the neck is put under a burden. For loads that are to be carried are commonly placed about the neck; and so by the name of the neck the whole is signified, namely the man who is to be punished. [[2:3|and you shall not walk haughtily|Et non ambulabitis superbi]], that is, with neck held high in sign of inward swelling pride, but you shall be subject to your enemies and brought low; for pride of heart commonly shows itself in the gait. [[2:3|for this is a very evil time|Quoniam tempus captivitatis vobis instantis, pessimum est]], namely the time of the captivity that threatens you, that is, full of adversities and vengeance: though time is not evil in itself, but is called good or evil, better or worse, according to the things that are done in it. Now these things were fulfilled at the time of the captivity of the ten tribes by the Assyrians, and of the two by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 15:29||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]][[4 Kings 24:14||]][[4 Kings 25:11||]]; indeed also by the Romans, since in Christ's time the sins foretold were in the people of the Jews. And after Christ's ascension they plundered in part the goods of the primitive Church, and oppressed in many ways those from Judaism who believed in Christ, according to what the Apostle says: You [[Heb 10:34|took with joy the being stripped of your own goods|Rapinam bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis]].

paras.t: In die illa captivitatis vestræ, sumetur super vos parabola : id est, de vobis seu vestra calamitate accipietur atque dicetur ab adversariis vestris proverbium quoddam derisorium. Unde per Jeremiam Dominus ait frequenter : Ponam locum istum in sibilum et in parabolam omnibus transeuntibus per eum. Et cantabitur ab æmulis vestris canticum cum suavitate, id est dulci melodia, dicentium, id est carmen vestrum seu de vobis compositum, qui dicitis : Depopulatione, id est cum magna direptione et oppressione, vastati sumus ab hostibus. Itaque miseriæ vestræ vertentur illis in canticum. De talibus enim rebus solent carmina fieri. Pars populi mei commutata est. Hoc Hieronymus exponit de templi destructione, eritque sensus : Pars populi mei, id est templum meum, quod solum in populo Judæorum habebam, commutata est, id est ad ruinam mutatum, seu demolitum a Chaldæis. Alii ita exponunt : Pars populi mei, id est decem tribuum, commutata est, id est dejecta. Antequam enim Salmanasar rex Assyriorum decem tribus vastavit, jam partim captæ occisæque erant a Theglathphalasar et Phul regibus Assyriorum. Quomodo recedet a me, id est a terra mea vastator illius (et sic verba istorum dicuntur in persona Dei), quum revertatur, qui regiones nostras dividat, id est, extraneis tradat ac mensuret ad possidendum ? Salmanasar enim rex Assyriorum vastavit decem tribus, et tunc Osee rex Israel fecit pacem cum eo solvendo tributum. Postea vero conatus est rebellare, quærendo a rege Ægypti auxilium. Quo audito, Salmanasar rediit, et decem tribuum regnum destruxit, atque in terra illa alienas constituit gentes, ut legitur quarto Regum. Simile est de Nabuchodonosor, quantum ad duas tribus. Capto enim Joachin, constituit Sedeciam in regem. Quem quum audisset velle rebellare, reversus est, et duarum tribuum demolitus est regnum, et in suam potestatem regionem illam redegit. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: [[2:4|In that day|In die illa]] of your captivity [[2:4|a parable shall be taken up upon you|sumetur super vos parabola]]: that is, a mocking proverb shall be taken up and spoken by your adversaries about you, or about your calamity. Hence the Lord often says through Jeremias: I will make this place a hissing and a byword to all that pass by it[[Jer 19:8||]][[Jer 25:9||]][[Jer 25:18||]] [Denis gives the sense of several such threats in Jeremias, not the words of one]. [[2:4|and a song shall be sung with melody|Et cantabitur ab æmulis vestris canticum cum suavitate]] by your rivals, that is, with sweet melody, [[2:4|by them that say|dicentium]], that is, your song, or one made about you, who say: [[2:4|spoiled|Depopulatione]] [Latin *depopulatione*, "with spoliation"], that is, with great plundering and oppression, [[2:4|We are laid waste|vastati sumus]] by our enemies. And so your miseries shall be turned into a song for them; for songs are commonly made about such things. [[2:4|the portion of my people is changed|Pars populi mei commutata est]]. Jerome explains this of the destruction of the temple, and the sense will be: [[2:4|the portion of my people|Pars populi mei]], that is, my temple, which alone I had among the people of the Jews, [[2:4|is changed|commutata est]], that is, changed to ruin, or demolished by the Chaldeans. Others explain it thus: [[2:4|the portion of my people|Pars populi mei]], that is, of the ten tribes, [[2:4|is changed|commutata est]], that is, cast down. For before Salmanasar king of the Assyrians laid waste the ten tribes, they had already in part been taken and slain by Theglathphalasar[[4 Kings 15:29||]] and Phul[[4 Kings 15:19||]], kings of the Assyrians. [[2:4|how shall he depart from me|Quomodo recedet a me]], that is, from my land, he who lays it waste (and so these men's words are spoken in the person of God), [[2:4|whereas he is returning that will divide our land?|quum revertatur, qui regiones nostras dividat]] that is, will hand it over to strangers and measure it out to them to possess? For Salmanasar king of the Assyrians laid waste the ten tribes, and then Osee king of Israel made peace with him by paying tribute[[4 Kings 17:3||]]. But afterwards he tried to rebel, seeking help from the king of Egypt[[4 Kings 17:4||]]. Hearing this, Salmanasar came back and destroyed the kingdom of the ten tribes[[4 Kings 17:6||]], and settled foreign nations in that land[[4 Kings 17:24||]], as we read in the fourth book of Kings. It is the same with Nabuchodonosor as regards the two tribes. For when Joachin was taken[[4 Kings 24:12||]], he made Sedecias king[[4 Kings 24:17||]][[2 Par 36:10||]]. When he heard that Sedecias meant to rebel, he came back, demolished the kingdom of the two tribes[[4 Kings 25:1||]], and brought that country under his own power. Therefore it is added:

paras.t: Propter hoc non erit tibi, o familia Israel, super quam cogito malum, mittens funiculum sortis, id est dans tibi partem hereditatis, in cœtu Domini, id est in terra promissionis, in qua sancti Domini habitaverunt, et quam Josue sorte divisit filiis Israel. Vel sic : Non erit mittens funiculum sortis in cœtu Domini, id est, nullus de populo Judæorum, qui erant exercitus Dei, mittet tibi mensuram hereditatis per sortem : quoniam terra promissionis aliis dabitur. Decem enim tribus usque in præsens privatæ sunt terra paterna. Et duæ tribus sub Chaldæis septuaginta annis fuerunt translatæ, a Romanis vero finaliter sunt expulsæ.
paras.en: [[2:5|Therefore thou shalt have none|Propter hoc non erit tibi]], O family of Israel, against which I devise evil, [[2:5|that shall cast the cord of a lot|mittens funiculum sortis]], that is, giving thee a share of inheritance, [[2:5|in the assembly of the Lord|in cœtu Domini]], that is, in the land of promise, in which the holy ones of the Lord dwelt, and which Josue divided by lot among the children of Israel. Or thus: [[2:5|none that shall cast the cord of a lot in the assembly of the Lord|Non erit mittens funiculum sortis in cœtu Domini]], that is, no one of the people of the Jews, who were the army of God, shall cast for thee the measure of an inheritance by lot, since the land of promise shall be given to others. For the ten tribes have been deprived of their fathers' land to this day; and the two tribes were carried away under the Chaldeans for seventy years, and were finally driven out by the Romans.

paras.t: Consequenter reprimitur vana spes seu præsumptio Judæorum. Ne loquamini loquentes, id est, nolite loqui verba ista sequentia : Non stillabit super istos malum, id est, super tribus Israel partem ac populum Dei non irruet pœna quam minantur Prophetæ, non comprehendet istos confusio, id est ignominiosa captivitas, et sub hostibus dejectio, dicit domus Jacob, id est familia Judæorum. Numquid abbreviatus est spiritus Domini ? Ista sunt verba quibus sibi inanem spem mutuo tribuebant, præsumendo de misericordia Dei, nec tamen cessando a vitiis, sicque peccantes in spem. Et est sensus : Numquid abbreviatus est spiritus Domini ? id est, bonitas seu voluntas Dei, aliis larga ac benefactiva, non est utique minorata. De quo spiritu scriptum est in libro Sapientiæ : O quam bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus in omnibus ! aut tales sunt cogitationes ejus, ut scilicet cogitet super nos mala, et vetera vitia ulciscatur, tanquam severus et iracundus, qui omnibus clemens est, et maxime populo suo peculiari ?
paras.en: Next the vain hope or presumption of the Jews is checked. [[2:6|Speak ye not, saying|Ne loquamini loquentes]], that is, do not speak these following words: [[2:6|It shall not drop upon these|Non stillabit super istos]] evil, that is, the punishment the Prophets threaten shall not fall upon the tribes of Israel, the portion and people of God; [[2:6|confusion shall not take them|non comprehendet istos confusio]], that is, shameful captivity and being cast down under enemies, [[2:7|The house of Jacob saith|dicit domus Jacob]], that is, the household of the Jews. [[2:7|Is the Spirit of the Lord straitened|Numquid abbreviatus est spiritus Domini]]? These are the words by which they gave one another an empty hope, presuming on the mercy of God, yet not ceasing from their vices, and so sinning against hope [that is, by presumption, the sin opposed to hope by excess]. And the sense is: [[2:7|Is the Spirit of the Lord straitened|Numquid abbreviatus est spiritus Domini]]? That is, the goodness or will of God, which is bountiful and beneficent to others, is surely not lessened. Of which Spirit it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 12:1|O how good and sweet is thy Spirit, O Lord, in all things!|O quam bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus in omnibus]] [[2:7|or are these his thoughts?|aut tales sunt cogitationes ejus]] namely, that he should devise evils against us and avenge old vices, as one stern and wrathful, he who is merciful to all, and most of all to his own peculiar people?

paras.t: Huic præsumptioni Deus respondet : Nonne verba mea bona sunt, id est pia et consolatoria bonique promissiva, cum eo qui recte graditur, id est justo seu pœnitenti qui in semitis justitiæ ambulat, non autem impœnitentibus et præsumptuosis ? quasi dicat : Bonus sum bonis, et severus iniquis non pœnitentibus. Secundum quod dicit Apostolus ad Romanos : Vide bonitatem et severitatem Dei : severitatem quidem in eis qui ceciderunt ; in te autem bonitatem, si tamen permanseris in bonitate. Quod itaque Deus non parcit, non contingit ex abbreviatione spiritus ejus, sed ex duritia præsumptioneque nostra, juxta illud Isaiæ : Ecce non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat, neque aggravata auris ejus, ut non exaudiat ; sed iniquitates vestræ diviserunt inter Deum vestrum et vos, et peccata vestra absconderunt faciem ejus a vobis.
paras.en: To this presumption God answers: [[2:7|Are not my words good|Nonne verba mea bona sunt]], that is, kind and consoling and promising good, [[2:7|to him that walketh uprightly|cum eo qui recte graditur]], that is, to the just man or the penitent who walks in the paths of justice, but not to the impenitent and presumptuous? As if he said: I am good to the good, and stern to the wicked who do not repent. According to what the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 11:22|See then the goodness and the severity of God: towards them indeed that are fallen, the severity; but towards thee, the goodness of God, if thou abide in goodness|Vide bonitatem et severitatem Dei : severitatem quidem in eis qui ceciderunt ; in te autem bonitatem, si tamen permanseris in bonitate]]. That God does not spare, then, does not come from any straitening of his Spirit, but from our hardness and presumption, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 59:1|Behold the hand of the Lord is not shortened that it cannot save, neither is his ear heavy that it cannot hear|Ecce non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat, neque aggravata auris ejus, ut non exaudiat]]. [[Is 59:2|But your iniquities have divided between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you|sed iniquitates vestræ diviserunt inter Deum vestrum et vos, et peccata vestra absconderunt faciem ejus a vobis]].

paras.t: Et econtrario populus meus in adversarium consurrexit : id est, quum verba mea sint bona rectis, tamen vice versa populus Israel, qui debuit mihi per caritatem servire et amicabiliter consentire, factus est mihi resistens et inobediens, atque in adversarium commutatus, idola colens, et alia mala exercens. Unde Symmachus transtulit : Populus meus quasi inimicus restitit. Desuper tunicam pallium sustulistis, id est, vestimenta inferiorum seu impotentium violenter rapuistis. Et eos qui transibant simpliciter, id est innocentes et simplices, convertistis in bellum, eos impie impugnando, et ad resistentiam concitando, vel contra alios excitando. Potest quoque per pallium, Dei auxilium accipi ; et per bellum, inobedientia seu rebellio contra Deum. Sacerdotes ergo et principes, per hoc quod quosdam bonos ac simplices a cultu Dei ad idololatriam aliaque piacula induxerunt, privaverunt eos auxilio Dei, et contra Deum incitaverunt quasi in bellum. Sic exponit Hieronymus.
paras.en: [[2:8|But my people, on the contrary, are risen up as an enemy|Et econtrario populus meus in adversarium consurrexit]]: that is, though my words are good to the upright, yet on the contrary the people of Israel, who ought to have served me in charity and agreed with me as friends, has become resistant and disobedient to me, and changed into an adversary, worshipping idols and doing other evils. Hence Symmachus translated: My people has stood against me as an enemy. [[2:8|you have taken away the cloak off from the coat|Desuper tunicam pallium sustulistis]], that is, you have violently seized the garments of those beneath you, or of the powerless. [[2:8|and them that passed harmless|Et eos qui transibant simpliciter]], that is, the innocent and simple, [[2:8|you have turned to war|convertistis in bellum]], wickedly attacking them and stirring them to resistance, or stirring them up against others. By the *cloak* may also be understood the help of God, and by *war* disobedience or rebellion against God. The priests and princes, then, by leading some good and simple men away from the worship of God into idolatry and other crimes, deprived them of God's help and stirred them against God as if to war. So Jerome explains it.

paras.t: Mulieres populi mei ejecistis, id est captivas ire fecistis vel expulistis, de domo deliciarum suarum, id est a propriis habitaculis, in quibus cum viris et liberis suis lætanter vixerunt ; a parvulis earum tulistis laudem meam in perpetuum, avertendo filios earum a cultu divino, vel occidendo, vel in captivitatem mittendo, ita ut dicant : Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini in terra aliena ?
paras.en: [[2:9|You have cast out the women of my people|Mulieres populi mei ejecistis]], that is, you have made them go captive, or driven them out, [[2:9|from their houses, in which they took delight|de domo deliciarum suarum]], that is, from their own dwellings, in which they lived happily with their husbands and children; [[2:9|you have taken my praise forever from their children|a parvulis earum tulistis laudem meam in perpetuum]], by turning their sons away from the worship of God, or by killing them, or by sending them into captivity, so that they say: [[Ps 136:4|How shall we sing the song of the Lord in a strange land?|Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini in terra aliena]]

paras.t: Surgite, et ite, id est, propter tanta facinora surgentes coacte, in captivitatem transibitis, quia non habetis hic requiem, id est, in propria terra non meremini quietam habere mansionem. Propter immunditiam ejus, id est culpam terræ seu plebis hujus, corrumpetur putredine pessima, id est captivitate et vastitate gravissima per Chaldæos sive Romanos.
paras.en: [[2:10|Arise ye, and depart|Surgite, et ite]], that is, for such great crimes you shall rise up under compulsion and pass into captivity, [[2:10|for there is no rest here for you|quia non habetis hic requiem]], that is, you do not deserve to have a quiet dwelling in your own land. [[2:10|For that uncleanness of the land|Propter immunditiam ejus]], that is, for the guilt of this land or people, [[2:10|it shall be corrupted with a grievous corruption|corrumpetur putredine pessima]], that is, by a most grievous captivity and devastation by the Chaldeans or the Romans.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta ostendit se ista non dicere congratulando de imminentibus Judæorum periculis, sed vehementissime condolendo. Utinam non essem vir habens spiritum. Hoc dupliciter accipi potest. Hieronymus enim exponit sic : Utinam verus propheta non essem, sed pseudo, et Spiritu Sancto carerem, et mendacium potius loquerer, id est, falsa essent quæ futura prædico, quatenus multitudo Judæorum converteretur, et crederet in Filium Dei. Secundo exponitur sic : Utinam non essem vir habens spiritum, id est gratiam prophetiæ, et mendacium potius loquerer, id est non eveniret quod dico.
paras.en: Then the Prophet shows that he says these things not as one rejoicing over the dangers hanging over the Jews, but as one grieving with them most deeply. [[2:11|Would God I were not a man that hath the spirit|Utinam non essem vir habens spiritum]]. This can be taken in two ways. For Jerome explains it thus: Would God I were not a true prophet but a false one, and were without the Holy Spirit, [[2:11|and that I rather spoke a lie|et mendacium potius loquerer]], that is, that the things I foretell were false, so that the multitude of the Jews might be converted and believe in the Son of God. Secondly it is explained thus: [[2:11|Would God I were not a man that hath the spirit|Utinam non essem vir habens spiritum]], that is, the grace of prophecy, [[2:11|and that I rather spoke a lie|et mendacium potius loquerer]], that is, that what I say might not come to pass.

paras.t: Sed primæ expositioni potest opponi, quod homo non debet eatenus affici et compati aliis, ut velit caritate et gratia gratum faciente privari et pseudo consistere, quum dicat Salvator : Quid proficit homo, si lucretur universum mundum, se ipsum autem perdat ? Ordo quippe caritatis cadit sub præcepto. Secundæ quoque expositioni obviare videtur, quod homo non debeat veniale peccatum committere, ut liberet alium a mortali, vel quocumque tormento, quum peccatum sit infinitæ fugibilitatis. — Et respondendum, quod verba hujus sanctissimi Michææ, secundum expositionem primam accipi possunt per hyperbolen seu excessum, quomodo ait Apostolus : Optabam anathema esse a Christo pro fratribus meis Judæis ; et Moyses, Aut dimitte populo hanc noxam, aut dele me de libro quem scripsisti. Talia nempe per excessum dixerunt, quoniam aliter plene exprimere non valebant caritatis suæ fraternæ fervorem. Porro, juxta secundam expositionem, mendacium sumitur materialiter, non formaliter, scilicet pro sermone qui aliunde ab effectu rationabiliter impeditur, et tamen sine intentione fallendi implendus asseritur.
paras.en: But against the first explanation it can be objected that a man ought not to be so moved with compassion for others as to wish to be deprived of charity and of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God] and to be a false prophet, since the Saviour says: [[Luke 9:25|what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world and lose himself|Quid proficit homo, si lucretur universum mundum, se ipsum autem perdat]] For the order of charity [that is, the due order in which charity loves God, oneself and one's neighbour] falls under precept. Against the second explanation, too, there seems to stand this: that a man ought not to commit a venial sin to free another from a mortal one, or from any torment whatever, since sin is to be shunned without limit. And the answer must be that the words of this most holy Micheas, according to the first explanation, can be taken by hyperbole or overstatement, as when the Apostle says: [[Rom 9:3|I wished myself to be an anathema from Christ, for my brethren|Optabam anathema esse a Christo pro fratribus meis]], the Jews; and Moses: Either [[Ex 32:31|forgive them this trespass|dimitte populo hanc noxam]], or [[Ex 32:32|strike me out of the book that thou hast written|dele me de libro quem scripsisti]]. For they said such things by overstatement, because they could not otherwise fully express the fervour of their brotherly charity. Further, according to the second explanation, a *lie* is taken materially, not formally [that is, for words that turn out untrue, not for an intent to deceive]: namely, for a saying whose fulfilment is reasonably hindered from some other quarter, and which was nonetheless asserted, without intent to deceive, as something to be fulfilled.

paras.t: Considerandum est in his, quantus erat in sancto hoc vate zelus salutis fraternæ, caritatisque fervor, qui maluit absolute gratia prophetiæ, quæ est gratia gratis data, et sine peccato potest amitti, carere et mendax quodammodo apparere, quam populum suum perire. Non talis videtur fuisse Jonas, qui petivit animæ suæ ut moreretur, quoniam prophetia ejus non implebatur : quamvis inter Prophetas non oporteat facere comparationem in talibus, quum spirituum ponderator sit Dominus ; comparationes quoque odibiles sint.
paras.en: Here we must consider how great was the zeal for his brethren's salvation, and the fervour of charity, in this holy seer, who would rather be wholly without the grace of prophecy, which is a grace freely given [*gratia gratis data*, a gift given for the good of others, not one that makes its bearer holy] and can be lost without sin, and in a manner appear a liar, than that his people should perish. Jonas does not seem to have been such, who [[Jon 4:8|desired for his soul that he might die|petivit animæ suæ ut moreretur]][[Jon 4:3||]], because his prophecy was not fulfilled; though among the Prophets one ought not to make comparisons in such things, since [[Prov 16:2|the Lord is the weigher of spirits|spirituum ponderator sit Dominus]], and comparisons are odious as well.

paras.t: Sed quia Propheta agnovit vaticinium suum certissime adimplendum, tanquam ad prædestinationis pertinens prophetiam, subjungit : Stillabo, id est, verba futuræ punitionis per modum pluviæ fundam, dicamque tibi in vinum et in ebrietatem, id est, illa tibi per modum poculi propinabo tam copiose, quod afflictionibus inebriaberis ; et erit super quem stillatur, id est, qui effectum comminationis meæ patietur, ita quod stillatio verborum meorum cadet in eos de quibus subjungitur : populus iste, id est plebs Judæorum. Solet autem pœna abundans, potus vocari, et nomine calicis designari.
paras.en: But because the Prophet knew that his prophecy would most certainly be fulfilled, as belonging to the prophecy of predestination [that is, a prophecy of what God has decreed absolutely, as distinct from a threat that depends on men's conduct], he adds: [[2:11|I will let drop|Stillabo]], that is, I will pour out the words of the punishment to come like rain, and speak them [[2:11|to thee of wine, and of drunkenness|tibi in vinum et in ebrietatem]], that is, I will pledge them to thee like a cup, so abundantly that thou shalt be drunk with afflictions; [[2:11|and it shall be|et erit]] [[2:11|upon whom it shall drop|super quem stillatur]], that is, he who shall suffer the effect of my threat, so that the dropping of my words shall fall on those of whom it is added: [[2:11|this people|populus iste]], that is, the people of the Jews. Now abundant punishment is commonly called a drink and signified by the name of a cup.

paras.t: Præterea, post austeritatem instantis periculi, describit Propheta consolationem beneficii exhibendi, loquens in persona Dei : Congregatione congregabo Jacob totum te ; in unum conducam reliquias Israel, etc. Locus iste multipliciter explanatur. Quidam enim exponunt hæc de reditu Judæorum a Babylonica captivitate : ex qua licet omnes Judæi reversi non sint, majores tamen et principaliores redierunt cum aliis plurimis ; et universis data fuit a Cyro rege Persarum licentia redeundi. Videtur quoque expositio ista non dissona, si superiora de Babylonica captivitate elucidentur.
paras.en: Further, after the harshness of the danger at hand, the Prophet describes the consolation of the benefit to be shown, speaking in the person of God: [[2:12|I will assemble and gather together all of thee, O Jacob|Congregatione congregabo Jacob totum te]]: [[2:12|I will bring together the remnant of Israel|in unum conducam reliquias Israel]], etc. This passage is explained in many ways. Some explain it of the return of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity: for though not all the Jews returned from it, yet the greater and more important of them came back with very many others, and leave to return was given to all by Cyrus king of the Persians[[1 Esd 1:2||]][[1 Esd 1:3||]]. And this explanation does not seem out of keeping, if what goes before is explained of the Babylonian captivity.

paras.t: Alii vero exponunt de Judæorum generali conversione in fine sæculi, ut sit sensus : Congregatione, id est spirituali unione in fide catholica, individua caritate, speque divina, congregabo Jacob totum te, id est omnes duodecim tribus. Tunc enim omnes credent in Christum per prædicationem Eliæ, Christo testante : Elias quum venerit, restituet omnia. In unum conducam reliquias Israel pariter, id est electos Judæos qui tunc superstites erunt, ut omnium sit cor unum et anima una : quod et post Babylonicam captivitatem aliquo modo impletum est, juxta illud Jeremiæ, Dabo eis cor unum et animam unam. Ponam illum quasi gregem in ovili Ecclesiæ, id est, in militanti Ecclesia eos constituam sub imperio Christi, sub cujus directione obedienter procedent, sicut grex ovium sub virga pastoris. Tunc enim perfecte fiet unum ovile, et unus pastor. Quasi pecus in medio caularum, id est, in domibus et pascuis dominici ovilis collocabuntur, sicut jumenta in stabulis. Tumultuabuntur, id est, in maxima multitudine erunt, atque communi laude in Dei venerationem erumpent. Per hanc igitur tumultuationem non designatur commotio veræ quieti contraria, sed credentium inæstimabilis copia. Propter quod subditur : a multitudine hominum, præ nimia pluralitate fidelium.
paras.en: Others explain it of the general conversion of the Jews at the end of the world, so that the sense is: [[2:12|I will assemble|Congregatione]], that is, by spiritual union in the catholic faith, in undivided charity and in divine hope, [[2:12|and gather together all of thee, O Jacob|congregabo Jacob totum te]], that is, all the twelve tribes. For then all will believe in Christ through the preaching of Elias, as Christ testifies: [[Mark 9:11|Elias, when he shall come|Elias quum venerit]], [[Mark 9:11|shall restore all things|restituet omnia]]. [[2:12|I will bring together the remnant of Israel|In unum conducam reliquias Israel pariter]], that is, the elect Jews who shall then be living, so that all may have [[Acts 4:32|one heart and one soul|cor unum et anima una]]: which was in some way fulfilled after the Babylonian captivity too, according to that of Jeremias: [[Jer 32:39|And I will give them one heart|Dabo eis cor unum]], and one soul [the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have "and one way"]. [[2:12|I will put them together as a flock in the fold|Ponam illum quasi gregem in ovili]] of the Church, that is, I will set them in the Church militant under the rule of Christ, under whose guidance they will go forward obediently, like a flock of sheep under the shepherd's rod. For then there shall perfectly be [[John 10:16|one fold and one shepherd|unum ovile, et unus pastor]]. [[2:12|as sheep in the midst of the sheepcotes|Quasi pecus in medio caularum]], that is, they shall be placed in the houses and pastures of the Lord's fold, like beasts in their stalls. [[2:12|they shall make a tumult|Tumultuabuntur]], that is, they shall be in the greatest multitude, and shall break out in common praise to the honour of God. By this tumult, then, is signified not a commotion contrary to true quiet, but a countless number of believers. Therefore it is added: [[2:12|by reason of the multitude of men|a multitudine hominum]], because of the very great number of the faithful.

paras.t: Ascendet enim, id est, Christus, de quo ista dicuntur, sicut patebit, in cordibus illorum erit, eosque docebit ac ducet, pandens iter ante eos : id est, viam salutis illis ostendet ad dirigendum pedes eorum in viam pacis, ut impleatur in illis illud in Psalmo : Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus, ingressus Dei mei, regis mei, qui est in sancto. Dividet, et transibunt portam, id est rectam et arctam januam ducentem ad vitam : de qua scriptum est, Intrate per angustam portam ; et denuo, Quam angusta porta et arcta via quæ ducit ad vitam, et pauci inveniunt eam ! Vel porta est fides Ecclesiæ, vel Baptismus, seu Christus, qui ait : Ego sum ostium. Qui autem non intrat per ostium in ovile ovium, sed ascendit aliunde, ille fur est et latro. Et egredientur per eam, transeundo de via ad patriam, de fide ad speciem, de merito ad præmium. Christus etiam protestatur : Si quis per me intraverit, ingredietur et egredietur, et pascua inveniet. Et transibit rex eorum coram eis : id est, Christus ductor erit eorum per gratiosam illustrationem, sicut ait Psalmista : Deduc me, Domine, in via tua. Unde in Exodo Moyses loquitur Domino : Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, non educas nos de loco isto : in quo enim scire poterimus invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum ? Et Dominus in capite eorum, id est in principio tanquam dux sui exercitus. Ipse quoque disseruit : Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio illorum sum.
paras.en: [[2:13|For he shall go up|Ascendet enim]], that is, Christ, of whom these things are said, as will be plain, shall be in their hearts and shall teach and lead them, [[2:13|that shall open the way before them|pandens iter ante eos]]: that is, he shall show them the way of salvation, to direct their feet [[Luke 1:79|into the way of peace|in viam pacis]], so that there may be fulfilled in them that of the Psalm: [[Ps 67:25|They have seen thy goings, O God, the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.|Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus, ingressus Dei mei, regis mei, qui est in sancto]] [[2:13|they shall divide and pass through the gate|Dividet, et transibunt portam]] [Denis reads *Dividet*, "he shall divide", where the Vulgate has *divident*, "they shall divide"], that is, the right and strait door that leads to life, of which it is written: [[Matt 7:13|Enter ye in at the narrow gate|Intrate per angustam portam]]; and again: [[Matt 7:14|How narrow is the gate, and strait is the way that leadeth to life: and few there are that find it!|Quam angusta porta et arcta via quæ ducit ad vitam, et pauci inveniunt eam]] Or the gate is the faith of the Church, or Baptism, or Christ, who says: [[John 10:9|I am the door|Ego sum ostium]]. [[John 10:1|He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold but climbeth up another way, the same is a thief and a robber|Qui autem non intrat per ostium in ovile ovium, sed ascendit aliunde, ille fur est et latro]]. [[2:13|and shall come in by it|Et egredientur per eam]] [Denis reads *egredientur*, "they shall go out", where the Vulgate has *ingredientur*, "they shall go in"; his gloss follows his reading], passing from the way to the fatherland, from faith to sight, from merit to reward. Christ too declares: [[John 10:9|By me, if any man enter in|Si quis per me intraverit]], [[John 10:9|he shall go in and go out, and shall find pastures|ingredietur et egredietur, et pascua inveniet]]. [[2:13|and their king shall pass before them|Et transibit rex eorum coram eis]]: that is, Christ shall be their guide by the enlightening of his grace, as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 85:11|Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way|Deduc me, Domine, in via tua]]. Hence in Exodus Moses speaks to the Lord: [[Ex 33:15|If thou thyself dost not go before, bring us not out of this place|Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, non educas nos de loco isto]]: [[Ex 33:16|For how shall we be able to know, I and thy people, that we have found grace in thy sight, unless thou walk with us|in quo enim scire poterimus invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum]]? [[2:13|and the Lord at the head of them|Et Dominus in capite eorum]], that is, at the front, as the leader of his army. He himself also declared: [[Matt 18:20|where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio illorum sum]].

paras.t: Præterea, secundum Hieronymum, passus iste exponi potest pro tempore primi adventus Christi : qui tunc per se et Apostolos, electos Judæorum infra ecclesiasticam unitatem collegit, et reliquias Israel per gratiam salvas fecit. Soli autem electi Judæi, qui fidem et mores Patriarcharum sequuntur, reputantur in semine : non enim qui filii carnis, hi filii. Illis quoque Christus præmemorata beneficia præstitit, et fideles valde auxit merito et numero, ut patet in Actibus. — Postremo, quidam exponit hæc de congregatione electorum Judæorum in limbo inferni, in quo quasi in ovili custodiebantur a Deo, donec Christus venit pandens illis iter ad regnum cœleste, in quod eos præcessit ac introduxit. Verum expositio ista videtur impertinentior aliis, nec ad præcedentia aut consequentia condependentiam habet.
paras.en: Further, according to Jerome, this passage can be explained of the time of Christ's first coming: who then, by himself and by the Apostles, gathered the elect of the Jews into the unity of the Church, and by grace saved the remnant of Israel[[Rom 9:27||]][[Rom 11:5||]]. For only the elect Jews, who follow the faith and the ways of the Patriarchs, [[Rom 9:8|are accounted for the seed|reputantur in semine]]: for [[Rom 9:8|not they that are the children of the flesh|non enim qui filii carnis]], these are the children. To them also Christ granted the benefits recounted above, and greatly increased the faithful in merit and in number, as is plain in the Acts[[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 2:47||]][[Acts 4:4||]][[Acts 4:32||]]. Lastly, someone explains these things of the gathering of the elect Jews in the limbo of hell, in which they were kept by God as in a fold, until Christ came, opening for them the way to the heavenly kingdom, into which he went before them and brought them in. But this explanation seems less fitting than the others, and has no connection with what goes before or what follows.

paras.t: Insuper moralitas hujus capituli patet ex præinductis frequenter. Quod enim in exordio scriptum est, Væ qui cogitatis inutile, et operamini malum in cubilibus vestris, referendum est ad Christianos qui mala cogitant cum rationis consensu ; et ex deliberatione, non ex subita passione agunt inique, mala intra se proponentes, et vias callidas fallendi, seu cogitata exsequendi excogitantes, seu carnis libidini insistentes : quibus æternum væ imminet. In luce matutina faciunt illud, quorum pedes festinant ad mala ; et totum diem infructuose, illicite et criminaliter expendentes, quum e contrario deberent totum tempus in pœnitentiæ exercitiis occupare. Unde de singulis talium scriptum est in libro Job : Dedit illi Deus locum pœnitentiæ, et ille abutitur eo in superbiam.
paras.en: Moreover, the moral sense of this chapter is plain from what has often been brought forward before. For what is written at the beginning, [[2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable, and work evil in your beds|Væ qui cogitatis inutile, et operamini malum in cubilibus vestris]], is to be referred to Christians who think evil with the consent of reason, and act wickedly from deliberation, not from sudden passion, proposing evils within themselves and devising cunning ways of deceiving, or of carrying out what they have thought, or giving themselves to the lust of the flesh: over whom an eternal woe hangs. [[2:1|in the morning light they execute it|In luce matutina faciunt illud]], they whose feet hasten to evil[[Is 59:7||]], and who spend the whole day fruitlessly, unlawfully and criminally, when on the contrary they ought to fill all their time with the exercises of penance. Hence it is written of each of these in the book of Job: [[Job 24:23|God hath given him place for penance, and he abuseth it unto pride|Dedit illi Deus locum pœnitentiæ, et ille abutitur eo in superbiam]].

paras.t: Et concupierunt agros, etc., et calumniabantur virum. Hæc contra avaros, violentos et injuriatores dicuntur, quorum gravissima erit damnatio, quia directe agunt contra caritatem atque justitiam ; et judicium sine misericordia fiet his qui non faciunt misericordiam : quanto magis his qui inferunt crudelitatem, nocumentum, seu violentiam ?
paras.en: [[2:2|And they have coveted fields|Et concupierunt agros]], etc., [[2:2|and oppressed a man|et calumniabantur virum]]. These things are said against the avaricious, the violent and those who do wrong to others, whose damnation will be most grievous, because they act directly against charity and justice; and there shall be [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|judicium sine misericordia fiet his qui non faciunt misericordiam]]: how much more to those who inflict cruelty, harm or violence?

paras.t: Super talem pessimam familiam cogitat Deus malum tartareæ ultionis, quod nunquam evadent. Super hos quoque sumetur parabola, quia lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam. Et qui tribulant nos diaboli, exsultabunt, si moti fuerimus recedendo a Deo, et pœnas inferi incidendo. Propter quod orat vir sanctus : Neque irrideant me inimici mei. Et Ecclesiasticus ait : Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu et consilio illorum, et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum, et gaudeat inimicus meus. Et cantabitur canticum cum suavitate. Tunc enim Sancti jucundissime canent : Laqueus contritus est, et nos liberati sumus. Depopulatione vastati sumus. Hoc competit his qui invisibilium hostium tentationibus victi sunt, et funibus vitiorum constricti. Pars populi mei commutata est : quia nunc multi Christianorum summo et invariabili bono relicto, mutantur et convertuntur ad ista terrena et vana, ac pereunt.
paras.en: Against such a most wicked family God devises the evil of the vengeance of hell, which they shall never escape. Upon these too [[2:4|a parable shall be taken up|sumetur parabola]], for [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]]. And the devils who trouble us will rejoice if we are moved, by falling away from God and falling into the pains of hell[[Ps 12:5||]]. Therefore the holy man prays: [[Ps 24:3|Neither let my enemies laugh at me|Neque irrideant me inimici mei]]. And Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 23:1|O Lord, father, and sovereign ruler of my life, leave me not to their counsel|Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu et consilio illorum]] [Denis has "to their thought and counsel"], [[Ecclus 23:3|and I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me?|et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum, et gaudeat inimicus meus]] [[2:4|and a song shall be sung with melody|Et cantabitur canticum cum suavitate]]: for then the Saints shall sing most joyfully: [[Ps 123:7|The snare is broken, and we are delivered|Laqueus contritus est, et nos liberati sumus]]. [[2:4|We are laid waste and spoiled|Depopulatione vastati sumus]]: this fits those who have been overcome by the temptations of invisible enemies and bound with the cords of vices. [[2:4|the portion of my people is changed|Pars populi mei commutata est]]: for now many Christians, forsaking the highest and unchangeable good, are changed and turned to these earthly and vain things, and perish.

paras.t: Propter hoc non erit tibi mittens funiculum sortis in cœtu Domini : id est, tibi qui talis es, non erit sors inter electos, nec Christi eris coheres, neque in cœtu Sanctorum erit tibi participatio bonorum Domini in terra viventium.
paras.en: [[2:5|Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast the cord of a lot in the assembly of the Lord|Propter hoc non erit tibi mittens funiculum sortis in cœtu Domini]]: that is, thou who art such shalt have no lot among the elect, nor shalt thou be co-heir of Christ, nor shalt thou have any share, in the assembly of the Saints, in the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

paras.t: Ne loquamini : Non stillabit super istos, etc. Hoc dicitur contra eos qui peccant in spe, et de misericordia Dei periculose confidunt, imo non vere confidunt, sed stulte præsumunt. Quibus advertendum est quod Dominus ait in Psalmo : Hæc fecisti, et tacui. Existimasti inique quod ero tui similis : arguam te, et statuam contra faciem tuam. Unde Ecclesiasticus inducit : Non adjicias peccatum super peccatum, et dicas, Miseratio Domini magna est : misericordia enim et ira ab illo cito proximant, et in peccatores respicit ira illius.
paras.en: [[2:6|Speak ye not|Ne loquamini]]: [[2:6|It shall not drop upon these|Non stillabit super istos]], etc. This is said against those who sin against hope and trust dangerously in the mercy of God; or rather, they do not truly trust, but foolishly presume. They must take heed of what the Lord says in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:21|These things hast thou done, and I was silent. Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.|Hæc fecisti, et tacui. Existimasti inique quod ero tui similis : arguam te, et statuam contra faciem tuam]] Hence Ecclesiasticus puts it: [[Ecclus 5:5|add not sin upon sin|Non adjicias peccatum super peccatum]], [[Ecclus 5:6|And say not: The mercy of the Lord is great|et dicas, Miseratio Domini magna est]]: [[Ecclus 5:7|For mercy and wrath quickly come from him, and his wrath looketh upon sinners.|misericordia enim et ira ab illo cito proximant, et in peccatores respicit ira illius]]

paras.t: Et econtrario populus meus in adversarium consurrexit. Hoc dicit Christus adversus ingratos atque rebelles : quibus quum ipse tanta largitus sit atque spoponderit bona, illi econtra reddunt mala pro bonis. Et nedum propria corda, sed alios quoque a Deo avertunt, et divinæ legis jussionibus contraire non metuunt. Unde a parvulis quos in vitiis fovent ac instruunt, tollunt laudem Altissimi. Surgite, ite, quia non habetis hic requiem. Isti enim modo non pertinent ad mysticam unitatem fidelium. Et de eis ait Scriptura : Tollatur impius, ne videat gloriam Dei. Ibunt ergo in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[2:8|But my people, on the contrary, are risen up as an enemy|Et econtrario populus meus in adversarium consurrexit]]. Christ says this against the ungrateful and rebellious: to whom, though he has bestowed and promised such great good things, they on the contrary render [[Ps 34:12|evil for good|mala pro bonis]]. And they turn not only their own hearts away from God, but others' too, and do not fear to go against the commands of the divine law. Hence [[2:9|from their children|a parvulis]], whom they foster and train in vices, they take away the praise of the Most High. [[2:10|Arise ye, and depart, for there is no rest here for you|Surgite, ite, quia non habetis hic requiem]]: for such men do not now belong to the mystical unity of the faithful. And of them the Scripture says: Let the wicked be taken away, so that [[Is 26:10|he shall not see the glory of the Lord|ne videat gloriam Dei]] [the margin gives Is. xxvi, 10, according to the Septuagint; the Vulgate there reads "Let us have pity on the wicked"]. They [[Matt 25:46|shall go|Ibunt]] therefore [[Matt 25:41|into everlasting fire|in ignem æternum]].

paras.t: Utinam non essem vir habens spiritum, etc. Exemplo hujus beatissimi vatis discere debent prælati, prædicatores, doctores, omnesque fideles, subditis et proximis suis errantibus, seu afflictis atque tentatis cordialiter condolere, succurrere, semperque adstare, et omne bonum terrenum saluti illorum postponere, quia et ordo caritatis id exigit. Et secundum Joannem, debemus pro fratribus animas ponere.
paras.en: [[2:11|Would God I were not a man that hath the spirit|Utinam non essem vir habens spiritum]], etc. By the example of this most blessed seer, prelates, preachers, doctors and all the faithful ought to learn to grieve from the heart with their subjects and neighbours who go astray, or are afflicted and tempted, to help them and always to stand by them, and to put every earthly good after their salvation, for the order of charity also requires this. And according to John, [[1 John 3:16|we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren|debemus pro fratribus animas ponere]].

paras.t: Congregatione congregabo Jacob totum te, id est omnes Christianos electos vitia conculcantes : quos colligam in regno cœlorum in ovili triumphantis Ecclesiæ, sicut promisi dicendo : Vado parare vobis locum ; et iterum veniam et assumam vos ad me ipsum. Itemque : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam. Triticum enim Christus congregabit in horreum suum, paleas vero comburet igne inexstinguibili.
paras.en: [[2:12|I will assemble and gather together all of thee, O Jacob|Congregatione congregabo Jacob totum te]], that is, all the elect Christians who trample vices underfoot: whom I will gather in the kingdom of heaven, in the fold of the Church triumphant, as I promised, saying: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado parare vobis locum]]; [[John 14:3|I will come again and will take you to myself|et iterum veniam et assumam vos ad me ipsum]]. And again: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam]]. For Christ will [[Matt 3:12|gather his wheat into the barn|Triticum enim Christus congregabit in horreum suum]], [[Matt 3:12|but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire|paleas vero comburet igne inexstinguibili]].

3.title: Expositio capituli tertii: Et dixi: Audite, principes Jacob.
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: And I said: Hear, O ye princes of Jacob.

paras.t: PROPHETA præsenti capitulo arguit eminentiores populi Israel de diversis excessibus. Et dixi : Audite, principes Jacob, et duces domus Israel, id est, reges, sacerdotes, principes, et judices totius Israeliticæ plebis, seu duodecim tribuum : Numquid vestrum est scire judicium ? id est, indigni estis doceri a Deo, ad sciendum judicium discretionis inter bonum et malum, verum et falsum ; vel judicium retributionis, quo quisque recipit quod meretur. Et tamen tenemini ratione officii vestri ad hoc, sed propter peccata vestra privamini veritatis notitia, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: In the present chapter the Prophet rebukes the more eminent of the people of Israel for divers excesses. [[3:1|And I said: Hear, O ye princes of Jacob, and ye chiefs of the house of Israel|Et dixi : Audite, principes Jacob, et duces domus Israel]], that is, the kings, priests, princes and judges of the whole Israelite people, or of the twelve tribes: [[3:1|Is it not your part to know judgment|Numquid vestrum est scire judicium]]? [Denis reads the question without *non*: "Is it your part to know judgment?", expecting the answer no] That is, you are unworthy to be taught by God so as to know the judgment of discernment between good and evil, true and false; or the judgment of retribution, by which each receives what he deserves. And yet you are bound to this by reason of your office; but for your sins you are deprived of the knowledge of the truth, as is added next.

paras.t: Qui odio habetis bonum, id est virtutes et veritatem, seu bonos ac justos, et diligitis malum prædictis bonis oppositum. Quamvis enim appetitus objectum sit bonum, videlicet verum sive apparens, multi tamen virtutes et veritatem seu justos odiunt per accidens, prout eorum affectionem impediunt a consecutione eorum quæ appetunt. Unde qui male agit, odit lucem; et qui cupit delectari illicite, odit justitiam corripientem ac punientem. Qui violenter tollitis pelles eorum desuper eis, id est, bona inferiorum diripitis, eosque depauperatis atque nudatis rebus ac vestibus, quibus velut pelle tegebantur, et carnem eorum desuper ossibus eorum, id est, etiam necessaria victui subripitis eis, ut macerentur.
paras.en: [[3:2|You that hate good|Qui odio habetis bonum]], that is, virtues and truth, or the good and just, [[3:2|and love evil|et diligitis malum]], the opposite of the goods just named. For although the object of the appetite is good, whether true or apparent, yet many hate virtues and truth, or just men, accidentally [that is, not for what they are in themselves, but because of something joined to them], inasmuch as these hinder their affection from gaining what they desire. Hence [[John 3:20|every one that doth evil hateth the light|qui male agit, odit lucem]]; and he who longs for unlawful pleasure hates the justice that rebukes and punishes. [[3:2|that violently pluck off their skins from them|Qui violenter tollitis pelles eorum desuper eis]], that is, you plunder the goods of those beneath you, and impoverish them and strip them of the goods and clothing with which they were covered as with a skin, [[3:2|and their flesh from their bones|et carnem eorum desuper ossibus eorum]], that is, you filch from them even what they need to live, so that they waste away.

paras.t: Qui comederunt carnem populi mei, id est, labores et possessiones eorum consumunt, juxta illud in Psalmo : Qui devorant plebem meam sicut escam panis; et pellem eorum desuper excoriaverunt. Et ossa eorum confregerunt et conciderunt sicut in lebete, id est in olla, et quasi carnem in medio ollæ, id est, igne tribulationis et persecutionis subditos quodammodo excoquebant, quemadmodum carnes in olla coquuntur.
paras.en: [[3:3|Who have eaten the flesh of my people|Qui comederunt carnem populi mei]], that is, they consume their labours and possessions, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 13:4|who devour my people as they eat bread|Qui devorant plebem meam sicut escam panis]][[Ps 52:5||]]; [[3:3|and have flayed their skin off them|et pellem eorum desuper excoriaverunt]]. [[3:3|and have broken, and chopped their bones as for the kettle|Et ossa eorum confregerunt et conciderunt sicut in lebete]], that is, in a pot, [[3:3|and as flesh in the midst of the pot|et quasi carnem in medio ollæ]], that is, with the fire of tribulation and persecution they in a manner boiled their subjects, as meat is boiled in a pot.

paras.t: Per hæc autem nil aliud designatur, nisi quod superiores multipliciter atque crudeliter nimis vexaverunt subjectos, spoliando, contristando, cædendo, lædendo vel occidendo. — Hoc quoque spiritualiter peregerunt, subditos subvertendo, seu bonis gratiæ destituendo, dum vel minis vel blandimentis, aut alio modo mihi ignoto, eos ad peccata inducunt. Sicque tollunt ab eis cutem, id est virtutes circa exterioris hominis decorem spectantes; carnem quoque, id est virtutes interiorum affectionum inordinationem frenantes, quæ sunt magis intrinsecæ homini quam prædictæ; et ossa, id est virtutes intellectuales et theologicales, ac dona, quæ sunt firmissima animæ munimenta ac arma, quibus et ceteræ virtutes sustentantur, quemadmodum ossibus caro. Itaque prædicta gratiarum charismata subditis condonata, pessimi præsidentes devoraverunt ac confregerunt, imo in nihilum redegerunt, dum directe vel indirecte ad culpam mortalem induxerunt subjectos. — Moraliter quoque hæc referuntur ad crudeles Christianorum principes, et immisericordes atque avaros prælatos Ecclesiæ, qui in spiritualibus ac temporalibus nocent subjectis, et opprimunt subditos. Qui potius sunt peremptores quam pastores : in quibus passiones ac vitia rationis lucem obtenebrant, ita quod verum non contuetur judicium, sed in judicando sequitur passionatos affectionem motus, amorem, cupiditatem, vel odium.
paras.en: By these things nothing else is signified but that the rulers harassed their subjects in many ways and all too cruelly: by despoiling, grieving, beating, wounding or killing them. — This they also did spiritually, by overthrowing their subjects, or stripping them of the goods of grace, when by threats or by blandishments, or in some other way unknown to me, they lead them into sins. And so they take from them the skin, that is, the virtues that concern the comeliness of the outward man; the flesh too, that is, the virtues that curb the disorder of the inward affections, which are more inward to man than the former; and the bones, that is, the intellectual and theological virtues, and the gifts, which are the soul's strongest defences and arms, by which the other virtues also are held up, as flesh is by the bones. So these most wicked rulers devoured and broke, nay, brought to nothing, the aforesaid gifts of grace bestowed on their subjects, when directly or indirectly they led those subjects into mortal sin. — Morally, too, these things are referred to cruel princes of Christians and to unmerciful and avaricious prelates of the Church, who harm those under them in things spiritual and temporal, and oppress their subjects. These are slayers rather than shepherds [Latin *peremptores … pastores*]: in them passions and vices darken the light of reason, so that it does not behold true judgment, but in judging follows the impassioned movements of the affection, love, covetousness or hatred[[Rom 14:5||]] [the margin gives Rom. xiv, 5 here; the fit is uncertain].

paras.t: Tunc, puta in die afflictionis et captivitatis Judæorum ab Assyriis vel Chaldæis, clamabunt ad Dominum, non ex caritate, sed necessitate servilique timore; et non exaudiet eos, quum nihil sit Deo acceptum, gratum aut meritorium, nisi ex caritate emanet. Et abscondet faciem suam, id est piam et gratiosam opem sive præsentiam, ab eis in tempore illo, sicut nequiter egerunt, id est malitiose fecerunt, in adinventionibus suis, id est peccatis, quæ ex prævia quadam deliberatione, non ex impellente passione, fecerunt. Unde per Isaiam Dominus loquitur : Quum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos a vobis; et quum multiplicaveritis orationem, non exaudiam : manus enim vestræ sanguine plenæ sunt. Quod de omnibus generaliter accipi potest qui tempore angustiæ invocant Dominum ex necessitate, non pura intentione, quem in prosperis contempserunt, quemadmodum in Proverbiis testatur : Tunc invocabunt me, et non exaudiam; mane consurgent ad me, et non invenient me, eo quod exosam habuerint disciplinam. Qui vult ergo exaudiri, agat quod instruit Isaias : Quærite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum prope est.
paras.en: [[3:4|Then|Tunc]], namely in the day of the affliction and captivity of the Jews by the Assyrians or Chaldeans, [[3:4|shall they cry to the Lord|clamabunt ad Dominum]], not out of charity, but out of necessity and servile fear [that is, fear of punishment only, not the filial fear that springs from love]; [[3:4|and he will not hear them|et non exaudiet eos]], since nothing is acceptable, pleasing or meritorious to God unless it flows from charity[[1 Cor 13:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor. xiii, 1–3]. [[3:4|and he will hide his face|Et abscondet faciem suam]], that is, his loving and gracious help or presence, [[3:4|from them at that time|ab eis in tempore illo]], [[3:4|as they have behaved wickedly|sicut nequiter egerunt]], that is, have done maliciously, [[3:4|in their devices|in adinventionibus suis]], that is, in their sins, which they committed from a certain forethought, not under the drive of passion. Hence the Lord speaks by Isaias: [[Is 1:15|when you stretch forth your hands, I will turn away my eyes from you: and when you multiply prayer, I will not hear: for your hands are full of blood|Quum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos a vobis; et quum multiplicaveritis orationem, non exaudiam : manus enim vestræ sanguine plenæ sunt]]. This may be taken generally of all who in time of distress call upon the Lord out of necessity, not with a pure intention, whom they despised in prosperity, as he testifies in Proverbs: [[Prov 1:28|Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning, and shall not find me|Tunc invocabunt me, et non exaudiam; mane consurgent ad me, et non invenient me]], [[Prov 1:29|Because they have hated instruction|eo quod exosam habuerint disciplinam]]. Whoever, then, wishes to be heard, let him do what Isaias teaches: [[Is 55:6|Seek ye the Lord, while he may be found: call upon him, while he is near.|Quærite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum prope est]]

paras.t: Insuper Propheta loquitur contra pseudoprophetas seu mendaces doctores. Hæc dicit Dominus super prophetas qui seducunt populum meum, pacem et prospera promittendo ex parte Dei, quum propria mente talia confinxerint ad acquirendum ab hominibus temporale emolumentum ; qui mordent dentibus suis, id est, irrationabiliter loquuntur, dura annuntiando his qui eis nihil præstant, et sanctis vatibus detrahendo, et prædicant pacem dandam a Deo, ut lucrum obtineant, dicentes : Pax, pax; et non est pax. De talibus Dominus ait per Jeremiam : Ipsi currebant, et ego non misi eos. Et si quis non dederit in ore eorum quidpiam, id est aliquid cibi aut potus, vel similis rei, sanctificant, id est, quasi divino oraculo nuntiant, et prophetica auctoritate affirmant, super eum prælium esse venturum, id est, quod hostibus suis tradetur. Tales namque dicebant contemptores veri Dei ac Prophetarum, magnamque mereri vindictam.
paras.en: Further, the Prophet speaks against the false prophets, or lying teachers. [[3:5|Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err|Hæc dicit Dominus super prophetas qui seducunt populum meum]], by promising peace and prosperity on God's behalf, though they had made such things up in their own mind to gain temporal profit from men; [[3:5|that bite with their teeth|qui mordent dentibus suis]], that is, speak unreasonably, announcing harsh things to those who give them nothing, and disparaging the holy seers, [[3:5|and preach peace|et prædicant pacem]] to be given by God, in order to get gain, saying: [[Jer 6:14|Peace, peace: and there was no peace|Pax, pax; et non est pax]][[Jer 8:11||]]. Of such the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 23:21|they ran|Ipsi currebant]], and [[Jer 29:9|I have not sent them|ego non misi eos]]. [[3:5|and if a man give not something into their mouth|Et si quis non dederit in ore eorum quidpiam]], that is, something to eat or drink, or some such thing, [[3:5|they prepare|sanctificant]] [literally "they sanctify", that is, proclaim as holy], that is, they announce as if by a divine oracle, and affirm with prophetic authority, that [[3:5|war against him|super eum prælium]] is to come, that is, that he will be handed over to his enemies. For they used to say that such men were despisers of the true God and of the Prophets, and deserved great vengeance.

paras.t: Propterea nox, id est caligo erroris, vobis pro visione erit, id est, non veram illuminationem, o pseudo, habebitis, sed animæ cæcitatem; et tenebræ adversitatis seu justæ punitionis, vobis pro divinatione erunt, id est pro vaticinatione vestra conficta, quæ non est prophetia, sed divinatio, id est usurpata futurorum prænuntiatio. Itaque propter culpam confictæ prophetationis sustinebitis ultionem divinam. Et occumbet sol intelligentiæ, id est divinæ veritatis notitia : de quo fertur in Psalmo, Supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem; super prophetas mendaces, ita quod veritas deerit eis. Vel sol materialis atque sensibilis eis occumbit, dum claritas diurna non est eis in consolationem, eo quod debitis pœnis afficiantur. Et obtenebrabitur super eos dies, id est, omnia convertentur eis in materiam adversitatis, tempusque lucis tenebris adversitatis implebitur, quum Deus peccata eorum ulcisci inceperit.
paras.en: [[3:6|Therefore night|Propterea nox]], that is, the gloom of error, [[3:6|shall be to you instead of vision|vobis pro visione erit]], that is, you shall have, O false ones, not true enlightenment but blindness of soul; [[3:6|and darkness|et tenebræ]] of adversity, or of just punishment, [[3:6|to you instead of divination|vobis pro divinatione erunt]], that is, instead of your feigned prophesying, which is not prophecy but divination, that is, a usurped foretelling of things to come. And so, for the guilt of your feigned prophesying, you shall undergo the vengeance of God. [[3:6|and the sun shall go down|Et occumbet sol]] of understanding, that is, the knowledge of divine truth, of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 57:9|fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun|Supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem]]; [[3:6|upon the prophets|super prophetas]] who lie, so that truth will fail them. Or the material and sensible sun goes down for them, while the light of day is no comfort to them, because they are afflicted with the punishments they deserve. [[3:6|and the day shall be darkened over them|Et obtenebrabitur super eos dies]], that is, all things will be turned for them into matter of adversity, and the time of light will be filled with the darkness of adversity, when God begins to avenge their sins.

paras.t: Et confundentur, qui vident visiones tales, falsas ac deceptorias. Quum enim mendosi fuerint inventi, et pœnis addicti, confusionibus suffundentur. Et confundentur divini, qui sibi usurpant prænuntiare futura contingentia proprio spiritu, vel diabolica revelatione. Qui dicuntur divini, quia quod Domini est proprium, scilicet futura prædicere (juxta illud in Isaia : Quæ futura sunt annuntiate, et sciemus quia dii estis vos), sibi usurpant. Et operient vultus suos omnes, id est, præ rubore optabunt latere, quia non est responsum Dei, id est, Deus eis veritatem non revelavit, neque revelat.
paras.en: [[3:7|And they shall be confounded that see visions|Et confundentur, qui vident visiones]] of that kind, false and deceitful. For when they have been found out as liars and given over to punishment, they will be covered with confusion. [[3:7|and the diviners shall be confounded|Et confundentur divini]], who take it upon themselves to foretell future contingent things [that is, things that may or may not come to pass, and so cannot be known in their causes] by their own spirit, or by the devil's revelation. They are called *divini* [diviners: the word also means "divine ones"] because they usurp what is proper to the Lord, namely to foretell things to come (according to that in Isaias: [[Is 41:23|Shew the things that are to come hereafter, and we shall know that ye are gods|Quæ futura sunt annuntiate, et sciemus quia dii estis vos]]). [[3:7|and they shall all cover their faces|Et operient vultus suos omnes]], that is, for shame they will wish to hide, [[3:7|because there is no answer of God|quia non est responsum Dei]], that is, God has not revealed the truth to them, nor does he reveal it.

paras.t: Hæc autem moraliter contra illos dicuntur, qui in Ecclesia Christi divitibus adulantur, et hominibus placentia prædicant, ex avaritia, ambitione, aut simili temporalis commodi affectione. Quibus convenit illud in Isaia : Et erunt, qui beatificant populum istum, seducentes; et qui beatificantur, præcipitati.
paras.en: — Morally, these things are said against those who in the Church of Christ flatter the rich and preach what pleases men, out of avarice, ambition, or some like love of temporal advantage. To them fits that saying in Isaias: [[Is 9:16|And they that call this people blessed, shall cause them to err: and they that are called blessed, shall be thrown down, headlong.|Et erunt, qui beatificant populum istum, seducentes; et qui beatificantur, præcipitati]]

paras.t: Verumtamen ego repletus sum fortitudine spiritus Domini, id est constantia data a Spiritu Sancto, et dono Spiritus quod fortitudo vocatur, estque unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti. Sum quoque repletus judicio discretionis ac rectæ sententiationis : quod est actus prudentiæ, tanquam habitus actum elicientis; et justitiæ, tanquam habitus in judicando regulantis; et virtute, id est efficacia in loquendo, vel sanctitate in operando, quam decet prædicatori inesse, ne et ipse reprehensibilis sit. Ut annuntiem Jacob, id est Judæis, scelus suum, id est idololatriam; et Israel, id est, eidem populo annuntiem, peccatum suum, sine timore corripiendo iniquos de quocumque peccato, ita ut eos qui corpus occidunt non timeam, sed pro veritatis defensione mori paratus sim. Simile est quod de se loquitur Jeremias : Misit Dominus manum suam, et tetigit os meum, et dixit: Ecce dedi verba mea in ore tuo ; ecce constitui te super gentes et regna. Christus quoque in Evangelio suis promisit : Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri. Qui itaque taliter confortatur et informatur a Deo, verba ignea profert, quibus audientium corda moventur ac immutantur. Multi vero proprio sensu loquuntur : et nec sibi nec aliis prodest.
paras.en: [[3:8|But yet I am filled with the strength of the spirit of the Lord|Verumtamen ego repletus sum fortitudine spiritus Domini]], that is, with the constancy given by the Holy Ghost, and with the gift of the Spirit which is called fortitude [*fortitudo*, the word of the text, means both "strength" and the gift of fortitude], and is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]]. I am filled also [[3:8|with judgment|judicio]] of discernment and of right sentence: which is an act of prudence, as of the habit that elicits the act, and of justice, as of the habit that rules in judging [a habit here is a settled quality of the soul from which its acts proceed]; [[3:8|and power|et virtute]] [*virtus* is both "power" and "virtue"], that is, effectiveness in speaking, or holiness in working, which befits a preacher, lest he too be blameworthy. [[3:8|to declare unto Jacob|Ut annuntiem Jacob]], that is, to the Jews, [[3:8|his wickedness|scelus suum]], that is, idolatry; [[3:8|and to Israel|et Israel]], that is, that I may declare to the same people, [[3:8|his sin|peccatum suum]], rebuking the wicked without fear for any sin whatever, so that I fear not [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui corpus occidunt]], but am ready to die in defence of the truth. Like this is what Jeremias says of himself: [[Jer 1:9|the Lord put forth his hand, and touched my mouth|Misit Dominus manum suam, et tetigit os meum]], and he said: [[Jer 1:9|Behold I have given my words in thy mouth|Ecce dedi verba mea in ore tuo]]; [[Jer 1:10|Lo, I have set thee this day over the nations, and over kingdoms|ecce constitui te super gentes et regna]]. Christ also promised his own in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:15|For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay.|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]] Whoever, then, is so strengthened and formed by God, utters fiery words, by which the hearts of the hearers are moved and changed. But many speak from their own sense, and profit neither themselves nor others.

paras.t: Audite hæc, principes domus Jacob, id est familiæ regni Juda, seu duarum tribuum, et judices domus Israel, id est ejusdem populi vel decem tribuum. Potius tamen ista dici videntur ad duas tribus, quia mox subditur : Qui ædificatis Sion in sanguinibus. Qui abominamini judicium, id est, æquitatem et discretionem abhorretis, vel juste judicari seu corripi spernitis, detestantes judicia Prophetarum ; et omnia recta, id est justas causas, pervertitis, judicando injuste. Hinc scriptum est apud Jeremiam : Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus? Et tenentes legem nescierunt me, et pastores prævaricati sunt in me. Et apud Isaiam : Pupillo non judicant, et causa viduæ non ingreditur ad eos.
paras.en: [[3:9|Hear this, ye princes of the house of Jacob|Audite hæc, principes domus Jacob]], that is, of the household of the kingdom of Juda, or of the two tribes, [[3:9|and ye judges of the house of Israel|et judices domus Israel]], that is, of the same people, or of the ten tribes. Yet these words seem rather to be addressed to the two tribes, since it is added straight after: [[3:10|You that build up Sion with blood|Qui ædificatis Sion in sanguinibus]]. [[3:9|you that abhor judgment|Qui abominamini judicium]], that is, you shrink from equity and discernment, or you scorn to be justly judged or rebuked, loathing the judgments of the Prophets; and [[3:9|all that is right|omnia recta]], that is, just causes, you [[3:9|pervert|pervertitis]] by judging unjustly. Hence it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:8|The priests did not say: Where is the Lord? and they that held the law knew me not, and the pastors transgressed against me|Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus? Et tenentes legem nescierunt me, et pastores prævaricati sunt in me]]. And in Isaias: [[Is 1:23|They judge not for the fatherless: and the widow's cause cometh not in to them|Pupillo non judicant, et causa viduæ non ingreditur ad eos]].
