paras.t: Qui ædificatis Sion, id est domus vestras in Jerusalem, in sanguinibus, id est de rapinis pauperum, cæde insontium, occisione sanctorum, quorum substantiam diripientes, construitis habitacula vestra; et Jerusalem, id est urbem ipsam, ædificatis in iniquitate, id est de rebus illicite acquisitis, quas a subditis extorquetis, et exinde ruinas urbis reparatis.
paras.en: [[3:10|You that build up Sion|Qui ædificatis Sion]], that is, your houses in Jerusalem, [[3:10|with blood|in sanguinibus]], that is, out of the plunder of the poor, the slaughter of the innocent, the killing of the saints, whose substance you seize to put up your dwellings; [[3:10|and Jerusalem|et Jerusalem]], that is, the city itself, you build [[3:10|with iniquity|in iniquitate]], that is, out of things unlawfully gained, which you extort from your subjects, and with them you repair the ruins of the city.

paras.t: Principes ejus in muneribus judicabant, id est, propter dona dabant injustas sententias ; vel si juste judicabant, magis adspexerunt ad commodum temporale quam ad bonum spirituale, vendebantque sententiam, nec stipendio sui laboris erant recta intentione contenti. Et sacerdotes ejus in mercede docebant populum, id est, propter lucrum directe, spirituale pro temporali exhibentes : quum tamen ex officio haberent instruere plebem gratis, ad Dei honorem et animarum salutem; temporalia non quærentes, nisi secundario tanquam stipendium vitæ. Et prophetæ ejus in pecunia divinabant, id est, pseudo propter nummos mendosa vaticinia protulerunt. Propter quod dicitur in Isaia : Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributionem ; et in Jeremia, A propheta usque ad sacerdotem cuncti faciunt dolum.
paras.en: [[3:11|Her princes have judged for bribes|Principes ejus in muneribus judicabant]], that is, for gifts they gave unjust sentences; or, if they judged justly, they looked more to temporal advantage than to spiritual good, and sold their sentence, and were not content, with a right intention, with the wage of their labour. [[3:11|and her priests have taught for hire|Et sacerdotes ejus in mercede docebant]] the people, that is, directly for gain, offering the spiritual for the temporal: whereas by their office they were bound to instruct the people freely, for the honour of God and the salvation of souls, not seeking temporal things except secondarily, as a living wage. [[3:11|and her prophets divined for money|Et prophetæ ejus in pecunia divinabant]], that is, the false ones uttered lying oracles for coin. Wherefore it is said in Isaias: [[Is 1:23|they all love bribes, they run after rewards|Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributionem]]; and in Jeremias: [[Jer 6:13|from the prophet even to the priest, all are guilty of deceit|A propheta usque ad sacerdotem cuncti faciunt dolum]].

paras.t: Et super Dominum requiescebant, id est, divinæ auctoritati innitebantur; vel potius se inniti simulabant, quia ut eis a populo crederetur et copia rerum daretur, jactabant se ministros ac nuntios Dei. Vel, Super Dominum requiescebant, id est, de ejus bonitate præsumentes, dixerunt quietem, non impugnationem, esse futuram. Dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum? id est imo Deus vere in nobis est : quum tamen Salomon dicat, Longe est Dominus ab impiis. Non venient super nos mala pœnæ, id est, hostibus non trademur, nec capiemur, sed a Deo tanquam populus ejus protegemur.
paras.en: [[3:11|and they leaned upon the Lord|Et super Dominum requiescebant]], that is, they relied on God's authority; or rather they pretended to rely on it, since, so that the people might believe them and give them plenty of goods, they boasted that they were ministers and messengers of God. Or, [[3:11|they leaned upon the Lord|Super Dominum requiescebant]] [*requiescebant*, literally "they rested"], that is, presuming on his goodness, they said that there would be rest, not attack. [[3:11|saying: Is not the Lord in the midst of us?|Dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum?]] that is, nay, God is truly among us: whereas Solomon says: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]. [[3:11|no evil shall come among us|Non venient super nos mala]] (the evils of punishment), that is, we shall not be handed over to our enemies, nor taken, but shall be protected by God as his people.

paras.t: Propter hoc, id est propter præscripta peccata, Sion, id est illa pars Jerusalem in qua fuit templum atque palatium, quasi ager arabitur, id est, in solitudinem redigetur, ita ut possit arari, ædificiis destructis, habitatoribusque occisis; et Jerusalem quasi acervus lapidum erit, id est, penitus dejicetur; et mons templi, id est mons Sion, in quo steterat templum, erit et convertetur in excelsa silvarum, id est, fruteta et arbores altæ crescent in eo. Quæ omnia impleta sunt tempore Babylonicæ captivitatis, quæ septuaginta annis duravit. Quoniam tamen præmemorata facinora erant in populo Judæorum tempore Christi, quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio docet, redarguendo sacerdotes, Scribas ac Pharisæos de simulatione et hypocrisi, de superstitione et ambitione, præsertim de avaritia et pauperum devoratione ; ideo aliqui referunt ista ad primum Christi adventum, et captivitatem Judæorum a Romanis inflictam : præcipue, quoniam bona primitivæ Ecclesiæ diripientes principes sacerdotum ac judices, ædificabant Sion in sanguinibus, et in Jerusalem sanguinem Christi discipulorumque ejus fuderunt.
paras.en: [[3:12|Therefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because of the sins described above, [[3:12|Sion|Sion]], that is, that part of Jerusalem in which stood the temple and the palace, [[3:12|shall be ploughed as a field|quasi ager arabitur]], that is, shall be brought to a wilderness, so that it can be ploughed, its buildings destroyed and its inhabitants slain; [[3:12|and Jerusalem shall be as a heap of stones|et Jerusalem quasi acervus lapidum erit]], that is, shall be utterly thrown down; [[3:12|and the mountain of the temple|et mons templi]], that is, mount Sion, on which the temple had stood, shall be and shall be turned into [[3:12|the high places of the forests|in excelsa silvarum]], that is, thickets and tall trees shall grow on it. All of which was fulfilled at the time of the Babylonian captivity, which lasted seventy years. Since, however, the crimes recounted above were found in the Jewish people in the time of Christ, as Christ teaches in the Gospel, rebuking the priests, Scribes and Pharisees for pretence and hypocrisy, for superstition and ambition, and above all for avarice and devouring the poor, some therefore refer these words to the first coming of Christ and the captivity inflicted on the Jews by the Romans: chiefly because the chief priests and judges, plundering the goods of the primitive Church[[Heb 10:34||]], did [[3:10|build up Sion with blood|ædificabant Sion in sanguinibus]], and in Jerusalem shed the blood of Christ and of his disciples.

paras.t: Denique hujus prophetiæ atque Michææ istius mentionem efficit Jeremias. Quum enim sacerdotes et fallaces vellent Jeremiam occidere, quia Jerusalem dixit jam capiendam, surrexerunt quidam de senioribus, et dixerunt ad omnem cœtum populi : Michæas de Morasthi fuit propheta in diebus Ezechiæ regis Juda, et ait ad omnem populum : Hæc dicit Dominus : Sion quasi ager arabitur, et Jerusalem in acervum lapidum erit, et mons domus Domini in excelsa silvarum. Numquid morte condemnavit eum Ezechias et omnis Juda? Numquid non timuerunt et deprecati sunt Dominum, et pœnituit eum mali quod locutus fuerat contra eos? Hæc verba tam prolixe nunc allegavi, quia secundum allegantes hæc verba, præfatos videlicet seniores quorum allegationem Jeremias confirmare videtur, prophetia Michææ de destructione Jerusalem dicta fuit ad litteram pro tempore Ezechiæ, tanquam tunc adimplenda. Et secundum hoc, fuisset prophetia comminationis; postea tamen impleta fuit, ut dictum est.
paras.en: Lastly, Jeremias makes mention of this prophecy and of this Micheas. For when the priests and the deceivers wanted to kill Jeremias because he said that Jerusalem was soon to be taken, certain of the elders rose up, and [[Jer 26:17|they spoke to all the assembly of the people|dixerunt ad omnem cœtum populi]]: [[Jer 26:18|Micheas of Morasthi was a prophet in the days of Ezechias king of Juda|Michæas de Morasthi fuit propheta in diebus Ezechiæ regis Juda]], [[Jer 26:18|and he spoke to all the people|et ait ad omnem populum]]: [[Jer 26:18|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[Jer 26:18|Sion shall be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem shall be a heap of stones|Sion quasi ager arabitur, et Jerusalem in acervum lapidum erit]], [[Jer 26:18|and the mountain of the house|et mons domus]] of the Lord [[Jer 26:18|the high places of woods|in excelsa silvarum]]. [[Jer 26:19|Did Ezechias king of Juda, and all Juda, condemn him to death?|Numquid morte condemnavit eum Ezechias et omnis Juda?]] [[Jer 26:19|did they not fear the Lord, and beseech the face of the Lord|Numquid non timuerunt et deprecati sunt Dominum]], [[Jer 26:19|and the Lord repented of the evil that he had spoken against them?|et pœnituit eum mali quod locutus fuerat contra eos?]] I have now cited these words at such length because, according to those who cited them, namely the elders mentioned, whose citation Jeremias seems to confirm, the prophecy of Micheas about the destruction of Jerusalem was spoken, in the letter, of the time of Ezechias, as to be fulfilled then. And on this view it would have been a prophecy of threatening [that is, a prophecy of what will happen unless men repent, as distinct from a prophecy of what God has fixed]; yet it was fulfilled afterwards, as has been said.

paras.t: INSUPER, secundum tropologicum intellectum, prælatis, sacerdotibus, doctoribus atque principibus Ecclesiæ dicitur : Audite, principes domus Jacob, id est Christianorum, qui sunt templum et domus Dei (de qua dicit Apostolus Timotheo : Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei), et judices domus Israel, id est militantis Ecclesiæ, Deum fide conspicientis. Qui abominamini judicium, et omnia recta pervertitis. Hoc non omnibus, sed indignis atque nocentibus competit : qui in judicando sequuntur amorem et odium, non rationem et æquitatem; nec dignantur redargui, sed dicunt implicite illud Sapientiæ, Sit autem fortitudo nostra lex justitiæ.
paras.en: Further, according to the tropological sense [that is, the moral sense], it is said to the prelates, priests, doctors and princes of the Church: [[3:9|Hear this, ye princes of the house of Jacob|Audite, principes domus Jacob]], that is, of Christians, who are the temple and house of God (of which the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 3:15|that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God|Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei]]), [[3:9|and ye judges of the house of Israel|et judices domus Israel]], that is, of the Church militant, which beholds God by faith [*Israel* being taken as "seeing God"]. [[3:9|you that abhor judgment and pervert all that is right|Qui abominamini judicium, et omnia recta pervertitis]]. This fits not all, but the unworthy and harmful: who in judging follow love and hatred, not reason and equity; and who do not deign to be rebuked, but implicitly say that saying of Wisdom: [[Wis 2:11|But let our strength be the law of justice|Sit autem fortitudo nostra lex justitiæ]] [the words of the wicked in Wisdom: let our might be our rule of right].

paras.t: Qui ædificatis Sion, id est Ecclesiam, in sanguinibus, sacras Scripturas depravando, in cathedra pestilentiæ residendo, indignos ordinando, pusillos scandalizando ; et de eleemosynis pauperum, de patrimonio Christi pretiosas structuras levando. Et hoc est ædificare Jerusalem in peccatis.
paras.en: [[3:10|You that build up Sion|Qui ædificatis Sion]], that is, the Church, [[3:10|with blood|in sanguinibus]]: by corrupting the sacred Scriptures, by sitting [[Ps 1:1|in the chair of pestilence|in cathedra pestilentiæ]], by ordaining the unworthy, by scandalizing the little ones, and by raising costly buildings out of the alms of the poor, out of the patrimony of Christ. And this is to build Jerusalem in sins.

paras.t: Postremo, quomodo principes in muneribus judicent, sacerdotes quoque in mercede doceant, et fallaces quidam ac superstitiosi divinent, non est meæ parvitatis describere, quum (proh dolor!) ista nunc ad oculum pateant : dum omnes quæ sua sunt quæruntur, et temporalia spiritualibus præferunt; et hi qui alios ad salutarem timorem inducere obligantur, se ipsos ac alios vana promissione et periculosissima securitate decipiunt, dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum? Non venient super nos mala.
paras.en: Lastly, how princes judge [[3:11|for bribes|in muneribus]], priests too teach [[3:11|for hire|in mercede]], and certain deceivers and superstitious men divine, it is not for my littleness to describe, since (alas!) these things now lie open to the eye: while [[Phil 2:21|all seek the things that are their own|omnes quæ sua sunt quæruntur]], and prefer temporal things to spiritual; and those who are bound to lead others to a wholesome fear deceive themselves and others by vain promise and most perilous security, [[3:11|saying: Is not the Lord in the midst of us?|dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum?]] [[3:11|no evil shall come among us|Non venient super nos mala]].

paras.t: Propter hoc Sion quasi ager aratur, quia status Ecclesiæ hinc decrescit, et corda fidelium a dæmonibus arantur, ac pessimo semine seminantur. Jerusalem quoque quasi acervus lapidum est, dum caritate frigescente, dura atque lapidea fiunt fidelium corda. Et mons templi vertitur in excelsa silvarum, dum virtuosi et contemplativi labuntur, in superbiam eriguntur, et mundi dignitatibus atque opibus gaudent. Quod præcipue referri potest ad quosdam specie tenus religiosos, regulam suam non observantes, et ad sæcularia adspirantes.
paras.en: [[3:12|Therefore|Propter hoc]] [[3:12|Sion|Sion]] is ploughed [[3:12|as a field|quasi ager]], because the state of the Church is thereby in decline, and the hearts of the faithful are ploughed by demons and sown with the worst of seed. [[3:12|Jerusalem|Jerusalem]] also is [[3:12|as a heap of stones|quasi acervus lapidum]], while, as charity grows cold, the hearts of the faithful become hard and stony. [[3:12|and the mountain of the temple|Et mons templi]] is turned into [[3:12|the high places of the forests|in excelsa silvarum]], while the virtuous and contemplative fall away, are lifted up in pride, and take delight in the world's honours and riches. This may be referred especially to certain men who are religious in appearance only, who do not keep their rule and aspire to worldly things.

paras.t: Dicit autem Glossa circa hunc locum : Non debent ministri Ecclesiæ officia sua administrare propter pecuniam : non tamen prohibentur, quod ex officio debetur, accipere ad necessitatem, non ad luxuriam.
paras.en: Now the Gloss says on this place: The ministers of the Church ought not to discharge their offices for money; yet they are not forbidden to take what is due by reason of their office, for necessity, not for luxury.

4.title: Elucidatio capituli quarti: Et erit in novissimo dierum mons domus Domini, etc.
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the house of the Lord, etc.

paras.t: Descripta Judaicæ plebis ultione, subjungitur ejusdem consolatio, de proximo adimplenda per Christum. Et erit in novissimo dierum, id est in ultima mundi ætate, quæ a Præcursore incepit : de qua dicit Joannes, Novissima hora est; et Paulus, Nos, inquit, sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt; mons domus Domini, id est mons Sion, in quo templum erat constructum : de quo in fine præcedentis capituli dicebatur, quod esset in excelsa silvarum ; præparatus, id est sublimiter honoratus, in vertice montium, non per locorum mutationem aut corporalem erectionem, sed per divinorum miraculorum excellentiam : quoniam ipsemet Christus in hoc monte conversatus est, prædicavit, ultimam Cœnam fecit, corpus suum et sanguinem consecravit, ad discipulos clausis januis introivit, Spiritum Sanctum misit, multa quoque fecit prodigia in templo sito in monte isto. Idcirco mons iste sublimatus est ultra montem Sinai et Thabor, vel quemlibet alium : præsertim ob Christi corporalem in eo præsentiam, propter quam, ut in Aggæo dicitur, major fuit gloria secundi templi quam primi. Et sublimis erit super colles, id est montes minores, in quibus tamen aliqua eminentia opera facta sunt. Et fluent ad eum populi : id est, conversi ad fidem, locum hunc ex devotione visitabunt, propter opera Christi in eo patrata, et quoniam ibi congregata fuit et Spiritum Sanctum recepit primitiva Ecclesia. Et properabunt ad eum gentes multæ, id est gentiles conversi, et dicent, se mutuo cohortando : Venite, ascendamus ad montem Domini. Consueverunt enim ex gentilitate conversi, omnia loca in quibus Christus conversatus fuit ac passus, devotissime ac frequenter invisere. Et ad domum Dei Jacob, id est Ecclesiam in Jerusalem congregatam.
paras.en: The vengeance on the Jewish people having been described, their consolation is now added, soon to be fulfilled through Christ. [[4:1|And it shall come to pass in the last days|Et erit in novissimo dierum]], that is, in the last age of the world, which began with the Forerunner; of which John says, [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]]; and Paul: We, he says, are they [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]]; [[4:1|the mountain of the house of the Lord|mons domus Domini]], that is, Mount Sion, on which the temple had been built: of which it was said at the end of the preceding chapter that it would be [[Mich 3:12|as the high places of the forests|in excelsa silvarum]]; [[4:1|shall be prepared|præparatus]], that is, highly honoured, [[4:1|in the top of the mountains|in vertice montium]]: not by any change of place or bodily raising up, but by the excellence of divine miracles. For Christ himself lived on this mountain and preached there[[Matt 26:55||]], held the Last Supper and consecrated his body and blood[[Luke 22:7||]], came in to the disciples when the doors were shut[[John 20:26||]], sent the Holy Ghost[[Acts 2:1||]], and also wrought many wonders in the temple that stood on this mountain[[Matt 21:14||]]. Therefore this mountain was exalted beyond Mount Sinai and Thabor, or any other: above all because of the bodily presence of Christ in it, on account of which, as is said in Aggeus, the glory of the second temple was greater than that of the first[[Agg 2:10||]]. [[4:1|and high above the hills|Et sublimis erit super colles]], that is, the lesser mountains, on which nevertheless some eminent works were done. [[4:1|and people shall flow to it|Et fluent ad eum populi]]: that is, those converted to the faith will visit this place out of devotion, because of the works of Christ wrought in it, and because there the primitive Church was gathered and received the Holy Ghost[[Acts 2:1||]]. [[4:2|And many nations shall come in haste|Et properabunt ad eum gentes multæ]] [the Latin adds *ad eum*, "to it"], that is, the converted Gentiles, [[4:2|and say|et dicent]], exhorting one another: [[4:2|Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord|Venite, ascendamus ad montem Domini]]. For those converted from the Gentiles were wont to visit, most devoutly and often, all the places where Christ lived and suffered. [[4:2|and to the house of the God of Jacob|Et ad domum Dei Jacob]], that is, the Church gathered in Jerusalem.

paras.t: Secundo, locus iste exponitur secundum Hieronymum, intelligendo per montem, Christum, Sanctum Sanctorum, in omni gratia eminentem secundum formam assumptam, qui præparatus, id est factus seu declaratus est, in vertice montium, id est omnibus Sanctis esse sublimior. Propter quod ait Baptista : Qui post me venit, ante me factus est, id est mihi prælatus. Et sublimis est super colles. Dedit enim illi Pater nomen quod est super omne nomen; et sine mensura Spiritum contulit ei. Et fluent ad eum populi : id est, tam ex Judaismo quam ex gentilitate conversi, per fidem, dilectionem et obedientiam accesserunt ad Christum, sicut ad caput, quatenus de plenitudine ejus accipiant, dicente Apostolo : Accedamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus; et Psalmista, Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini.
paras.en: Secondly, this place is expounded according to Jerome, understanding by the mountain Christ, the Holy of Holies, eminent in all grace according to the form he took, who [[4:1|shall be prepared|præparatus]], that is, was made or declared, [[4:1|in the top of the mountains|in vertice montium]], that is, to be higher than all the Saints. Wherefore the Baptist says: [[John 1:30|After me there cometh a man, who is preferred before me|Qui post me venit, ante me factus est]][[John 1:15||]], that is, set above me. [[4:1|and high above the hills|Et sublimis est super colles]]. For the Father gave him [[Phil 2:9|a name which is above all names|nomen quod est super omne nomen]], and bestowed the Spirit on him without measure[[John 3:34||]]. [[4:1|and people shall flow to it|Et fluent ad eum populi]]: that is, those converted both from Judaism and from the Gentiles came to Christ through faith, love and obedience, as to the head, so that they might receive [[John 1:16|of his fulness|de plenitudine ejus]], as the Apostle says: [[Heb 4:16|Let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace|Accedamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus]] [Denis reads *gratiæ ejus*, "of his grace"]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini]].

paras.t: Tertio exponitur passus hic, intelligendo per montem domus Domini, militantem Christi Ecclesiam : quæ præparata est in vertice montium, quoniam major et excellentior fuit gratia data Ecclesiæ Christi, quam Synagogæ, vel congregationi quæ fuit ante legem. Propter quod tempus evangelicæ legis, seu novi Testamenti, per excellentiam appellatum est tempus gratiæ. Paulus quoque de se et coapostolis suis testatur : Nos ipsi primitias Spiritus habentes. Denique ad Ecclesiam omnes electi a principio evangelicæ prædicationis confluxerunt, quoniam extra illam nemo salvatur.
paras.en: Thirdly, this passage is expounded by understanding by [[4:1|the mountain of the house of the Lord|montem domus Domini]] the Church of Christ militant, which is prepared [[4:1|in the top of the mountains|in vertice montium]], since greater and more excellent was the grace given to the Church of Christ than to the Synagogue, or to the congregation that was before the law. For which reason the time of the evangelical law, or of the New Testament, has been called by pre-eminence the time of grace. Paul too testifies of himself and his fellow apostles: [[Rom 8:23|ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit|Nos ipsi primitias Spiritus habentes]]. Lastly, all the elect from the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel have flowed together into the Church, since outside her no one is saved.

paras.t: Et docebit nos Christus de viis suis, id est evangelica documenta atque præcepta, quibus itur ad regnum cœleste. Hæc docuit Christus per Apostolos et adjutores ac successores eorum, per illuminationem quoque occultam et angelicam subministrationem. Et ibimus, credendo, sperando, amando, et bene agendo, adversa quoque æquanimiter tolerando, in semitis ejus, id est consiliis et doctrinis, sequendo vestigia Salvatoris. Viæ enim ejus, viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ ejus pacificæ. Ipse etiam est via ac janua. Quia de Sion egredietur lex : id est, Evangelium Christi primo ab Apostolis publice et aperte prædicabitur in templo sito in monte Sion ; et deinde promulgabitur ad omnia climata orbis ; et verbum Domini, id est prædicatio Evangelii, de Jerusalem procedet ad alia loca. Quum enim in die Pentecostes recepissent Apostoli Spiritum Sanctum, mox ingressi sunt templum, Christi Evangelium constantissime prædicantes, quod postmodum in toto mundo prædicaverunt. Unde eis dixerat Christus : Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ.
paras.en: [[4:2|and he will teach us|Et docebit nos]], namely Christ, [[4:2|of his ways|de viis suis]], that is, the evangelical teachings and precepts by which one goes to the heavenly kingdom. These Christ taught through the Apostles and their helpers and successors, and also through hidden illumination and the ministry of the angels. [[4:2|and we will walk|Et ibimus]], by believing, hoping, loving and doing well, and also by bearing adversity with an even mind, [[4:2|in his paths|in semitis ejus]], that is, in his counsels and teachings, following the footsteps of the Saviour. For [[Prov 3:17|Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable|Viæ enim ejus, viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ ejus pacificæ]] [in Proverbs this is said of Wisdom]. He himself is also the way[[John 14:6||]] and the door[[John 10:9||]]. [[4:2|for the law shall go forth out of Sion|Quia de Sion egredietur lex]]: that is, the Gospel of Christ will first be preached by the Apostles publicly and openly in the temple standing on Mount Sion, and then proclaimed to every region of the world; [[4:2|and the word of the Lord|et verbum Domini]], that is, the preaching of the Gospel, will proceed [[4:2|out of Jerusalem|de Jerusalem]] to other places. For when the Apostles had received the Holy Ghost on the day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:4||]], they at once entered the temple, preaching the Gospel of Christ most steadfastly, which they afterwards preached in the whole world. Hence Christ had said to them: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]].

paras.t: Et judicabit, id est, discernet Christus, inter populos multos, quosdam vocando ad fidem et gratiam, quosdam autem derelinquendo; et corripiet gentes fortes usque in longinquum. Omnium enim gentium vitia per discipulorum suorum prædicationem redarguit. Christus quoque proprio ore, conversando inter homines, corripuit eos. Denique duplex est judicium, scilicet discretionis, quo inter electos et reprobos Christus secernit; et remunerationis, quo singulis quod merentur retribuit. Christus autem in primo suo adventu non fecit in sæculo isto judicium remunerationis seu damnationis. Propter quod ait apud Joannem : Non misit Deus Filium suum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum; et apud Lucam, Filius hominis non venit animas perdere, sed salvare. Istud autem judicium faciet in secundo suo adventu generaliter ; facitque illud quotidie particulariter in decedentibus a sæculo isto. Porro in primo suo adventu fecit judicium discretionis : de quo ait in Joanne, Nunc judicium est mundi. Fecit et tunc judicium justæ increpationis. Propter quod scriptum est in Isaia : Judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ. Jeremias quoque ait : Faciet judicium et justitiam in terra. Et concident gladios suos in vomeres, et hastas suas in ligones : id est, tanta pax erit in Christi adventu et circa evangelicæ prædicationis exordium, quod arma bellica in instrumenta agriculturæ vertentur. Tunc enim omnia regna mundi sub uno erant principe obedientia, scilicet sub Romano imperatore, ad cujus imperium descriptus est universus orbis, ut patet in Luca. Unde in Psalmo cantatur : Arcum conteret et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni. Non sumet gens adversus gentem gladium, id est, una natio non præliabitur contra aliam, quoniam omnes subditæ erunt Romano imperio; et non discent ultra belligerare, id est, non erit eis necessitas exercendi se ad modum pugnandi, quum ubique sit pax.
paras.en: [[4:3|And he shall judge|Et judicabit]], that is, Christ will discern, [[4:3|among many people|inter populos multos]], calling some to faith and grace, and leaving others; [[4:3|and rebuke strong nations afar off|et corripiet gentes fortes usque in longinquum]]. For he reproved the vices of all nations through the preaching of his disciples. Christ also rebuked them with his own mouth, while he lived among men. Further, judgment is twofold: that of discernment, by which Christ separates the elect from the reprobate; and that of recompense, by which he renders to each what he deserves. Now Christ in his first coming did not exercise in this world the judgment of recompense or of damnation. Wherefore he says in John: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|Non misit Deus Filium suum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]]; and in Luke: [[Luke 9:56|The Son of man came not to destroy souls, but to save|Filius hominis non venit animas perdere, sed salvare]]. That judgment he will exercise generally at his second coming, and he exercises it daily in particular upon those who depart from this world. But in his first coming he exercised the judgment of discernment, of which he says in John: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]. He exercised then also the judgment of just reproof. For which reason it is written in Isaias: [[Is 11:4|he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity the meek of the earth|Judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ]]. Jeremias also says: [[Jer 23:5|shall execute judgment and justice in the earth|Faciet judicium et justitiam in terra]]. [[4:3|and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into spades|Et concident gladios suos in vomeres, et hastas suas in ligones]]: that is, so great will be the peace at the coming of Christ and about the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel, that the weapons of war will be turned into tools of husbandry. For then all the kingdoms of the world were in obedience under one prince, namely under the Roman emperor, at whose command the whole world was enrolled, as is plain in Luke[[Luke 2:1||]]. Hence it is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 45:10|He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: and the shield he shall burn in the fire|Arcum conteret et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni]]. [[4:3|nation shall not take sword against nation|Non sumet gens adversus gentem gladium]], that is, one nation will not fight against another, since all will be subject to the Roman empire; [[4:3|neither shall they learn war anymore|et non discent ultra belligerare]], that is, they will have no need to train themselves in the manner of fighting, since there is peace everywhere.

paras.t: Hæc autem pro tanto dicuntur, quia tunc erat insolita inauditaque pax in toto mundo : quum tamen ante fuerint multa atque gravissima prælia. Et quoniam pax illa ultra consuetum notabiliter diu duravit, nunc dicitur, Non discent ultra belligerare : sicut communiter de negotio ultra solitum durante dicimus, Istud nunquam finietur, quum aliquando infra diem vel horam finiatur. Unde in Genesi scriptum est, quod Lia, nato Juda, parere cessavit : et tamen post pauca legitur peperisse adhuc duos filios et filiam unam. Simili modo habetur quarto Regum, quod Syri non venerunt ultra in terram Israel : et nihilo minus statim scribuntur redisse in illam.
paras.en: Now these things are said for this reason, that there was then an unwonted and unheard-of peace in the whole world, although before there had been many and most grievous wars. And because that peace lasted a remarkably long time beyond what was usual, it is said here: [[4:3|neither shall they learn war anymore|Non discent ultra belligerare]]; just as we commonly say of some business that lasts beyond the usual: This will never end, when sometimes it ends within the day or the hour. So it is written in Genesis that Lia, when Juda was born, left bearing[[Gen 29:35||]]; and yet a little after we read that she bore two more sons[[Gen 30:17||]][[Gen 30:19||]] and a daughter[[Gen 30:21||]]. In like manner it is said in the fourth book of Kings that the Syrians came no more into the land of Israel[[4 Kings 6:23||]]; and nevertheless they are written straight away to have come back into it[[4 Kings 6:24||]].

paras.t: Totum autem capitulum istud usque ad verbum sequens habetur in Isaia, pene sub eadem forma verborum : quod ibi prolixius, prout Dominus dedit, exposui.
paras.en: All of this chapter up to the following words is found in Isaias in almost the same form of words[[Is 2:2||]] [the margin gives Is. ii, 2–4]; and there I have expounded it at greater length, as the Lord gave.

paras.t: Et sedebit vir subtus vineam suam et subtus ficum suam : id est, tanta erit securitas, ut homines sine formidine sedeant etiam in agris ac vineis sub suis arbustis. Solet autem per talem modum loquendi, in veteri Testamento, magna pax et opulentia designari. In primo autem Christi adventu fuit in Judæa pax magna et copia rerum. Unde in Jeremia legitur : In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter. Propter quod subditur : et non erit qui exterreat. Romani enim sub magno rigore prohibuerunt violentiam fieri; nec judicibus a se constitutis parcebant, quando manifestam alicui fecerunt injuriam.
paras.en: [[4:4|And every man shall sit under his vine, and under his fig tree|Et sedebit vir subtus vineam suam et subtus ficum suam]]: that is, so great will be the security that men will sit without fear even in the fields and vineyards under their own trees. Now by this manner of speaking great peace and plenty are wont to be signified in the Old Testament. And at the first coming of Christ there was great peace in Judea, and abundance of goods. Hence we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:6|In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently|In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter]]. For which reason it is added: [[4:4|and there shall be none to make them afraid|et non erit qui exterreat]] [Denis reads *exterreat*; the edition notes the Vulgate's *deterreat*]. For the Romans forbade violence with great severity, and did not spare even the judges they had appointed when these had done anyone open wrong.

paras.t: Possunt præterea omnia ista specialiter accipi de diversis nationibus ad fidem conversis, quæ licet olim discordassent, tamen fide Christi suscepta, maximam mutuo dilectionem habebant, et per caritatem servierunt in invicem. Omnia vero hæc fient, quia os Domini exercituum locutum est, id est, intellectus divinus ista per Prophetas prædixit, cujus verbum irritum esse non valet.
paras.en: All these things may moreover be taken in a special way of the various nations converted to the faith, which, though once at discord, yet once they had received the faith of Christ had the greatest love for one another, and by charity served one another[[Gal 5:13||]]. And all these things will come about [[4:4|for the mouth of the Lord of hosts hath spoken|quia os Domini exercituum locutum est]], that is, the divine mind foretold these things through the Prophets, and its word cannot be made void.

paras.t: Quia omnes populi ambulabunt, unusquisque in nomine dei sui, id est, infideles in ritibus deorum suorum conversabuntur. Non enim omnium est fides; nec idololatria fuit per Apostolos penitus exstirpata, quum usque ad tempus Constantini Magni Roma coluerit idola. Nos autem ambulabimus in nomine Domini Dei nostri, id est, in Deo vero, et secundum voluntatem ac legem ipsius vivemus, in æternum et ultra, id est perseveranter omnino : non quod ultra seu post æternitatem sit duratio aliqua, sed ista dicuntur ad ampliorem certitudinem faciendam, vel ad clariorem expressionem. Porro quod ait, Nos autem ambulabimus, accipi potest de primitiva Ecclesia ex Judaismo conversa, vel de populo christiano communiter, qui est Israel secundum spiritum.
paras.en: [[4:5|For all people will walk every one in the name of his god|Quia omnes populi ambulabunt, unusquisque in nomine dei sui]], that is, the unbelievers will live in the rites of their gods. For [[2 Thess 3:2|all men have not faith|Non enim omnium est fides]]; nor was idolatry wholly rooted out by the Apostles, since Rome worshipped idols until the time of Constantine the Great. [[4:5|but we will walk in the name of the Lord, our God|Nos autem ambulabimus in nomine Domini Dei nostri]], that is, we will live in the true God and according to his will and law, [[4:5|for ever and ever|in æternum et ultra]] [literally "for ever and beyond"], that is, with utter perseverance: not that there is any duration beyond or after eternity, but these words are said to give greater certainty, or for a clearer expression. Further, what he says, [[4:5|we will walk|Nos autem ambulabimus]], may be taken of the primitive Church converted from Judaism, or of the Christian people in general, which is Israel according to the spirit.

paras.t: In die illa, dicit Dominus, id est tempore evangelicæ prædicationis et gratiæ. De qua die loquitur Isaias : In die illa erit germen Domini, id est Christus Filius Dei, in magnificentia et gloria; itemque Apostolus, Ecce nunc dies salutis; et iterum, Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit. Congregabo claudicantem, id est plebem Judaicam in via Dei nutantem : cujus pes scandalizabatur et scandalizabat frequenter; quæ tempore Christi per varia vitia indirecte transivit, juxta illud in Psalmo, Claudicaverunt a semitis suis. Quibus dici potuit illud Eliæ : Usquequo claudicatis in duas partes? Et eam quam ejeceram, id est Synagogam quam subinde ejeci de terra sua et peccare permisi, cui et interdum dedi libellum repudii, colligam per fidem et caritatem intra ovile Ecclesiæ, ut omnes sint unum mysticum corpus Christi ; et quam afflixeram, id est dictam Synagogam, quam per Assyrios, Chaldæos ac alias nationes punivi, congregabo spirituali collectione per gratiam.
paras.en: [[4:6|In that day, saith the Lord|In die illa, dicit Dominus]], that is, in the time of the preaching of the Gospel and of grace. Of which day Isaias speaks: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord|In die illa erit germen Domini]], that is, Christ the Son of God, [[Is 4:2|in magnificence and glory|in magnificentia et gloria]]; and likewise the Apostle: [[2 Cor 6:2|behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc dies salutis]]; and again: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed And the day is at hand|Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit]]. [[4:6|I will gather up her that halteth|Congregabo claudicantem]], that is, the Jewish people wavering in the way of God, whose foot often stumbled and caused others to stumble; who in the time of Christ went crookedly through various vices, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 17:46|have halted from their paths|Claudicaverunt a semitis suis]]. To them could be said that word of Elias: [[3 Kings 18:21|How long do you halt between two sides?|Usquequo claudicatis in duas partes?]] [[4:6|and her that I had cast out|Et eam quam ejeceram]], that is, the Synagogue, which from time to time I cast out of her land and let sin, and to whom at times I even gave a bill of divorce, [[4:6|I will gather up|colligam]] through faith and charity within the fold of the Church, that all may be one mystical body of Christ; [[4:6|and her whom I had afflicted|et quam afflixeram]], that is, the said Synagogue, which I punished by the Assyrians, the Chaldeans and other nations, I will gather by a spiritual gathering through grace.

paras.t: Et ne quis instet et dicat, hæc de Judæis exponi non posse, quoniam pauci illorum conversi sunt, subditur : Et ponam claudicantem in reliquias : id est, ex præinducta Judaica plebe non omnes, sed quosdam, comparatione aliorum perpaucos, salvabo. De quibus fert Isaias : Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus; et Apostolus, Reliquiæ per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt; et denuo, Non repulit Deus plebem suam, quam præscivit. Et eam quæ laboraverat, id est gentem Hebræam præfatam, quæ prædictis modis fuit afflicta et onere legis gravata, quod neque nos, neque patres nostri, ait Petrus, portare potuimus (specialiter accipi potest de Christi Apostolis et primis credentibus, quibus dicit : Vos estis qui permansistis mecum in tentationibus meis), ponam in gentem robustam : primo, quoniam innumerabiles convertent ad fidem, sicque multos in Christo filios generabunt, in quibus impletum est illud Isaiæ : Minimus erit in mille, et parvulus in gentem fortissimam ; secundo, quoniam ipsi Spiritu Sancto recepto fortissimi erant in Christo, et insuperabilem patientiam habuerunt, ita ut irent gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati, dicerentque principibus sacerdotum : Obedire oportet Deo magis quam hominibus. Nonne robustissimi erant, de quibus unus illorum locutus est, Certus sum quia neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus, neque virtutes, neque instantia, neque futura, neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei, quæ est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro? Ideo scriptum est de eis in Psalmo : Quoniam dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt. Quanta autem fuerit primitivæ Ecclesiæ in Jerusalem fortitudo, patet in Actibus Apostolorum. Et regnabit Dominus Christus super eos, id est in cordibus eorum, in monte Sion, id est in Ecclesia speculante cœlestia, quæ in monte prædicto Spiritum Sanctum recepit in primis credentibus. De qua ad Hebræos legitur : Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis; atque in Psalmo, Diligit Dominus portas Sion. Ex hoc nunc et usque in æternum, id est in præsenti vita inchoative per fidem et gratiam, in futuro quoque sæculo sine fine per beatificam revelationem.
paras.en: And lest anyone should press the point and say that these things cannot be expounded of the Jews, since few of them were converted, it is added: [[4:7|And I will make her that halted, a remnant|Et ponam claudicantem in reliquias]]: that is, of the Jewish people spoken of before I will save not all, but some, very few in comparison with the rest. Of whom Isaias says: [[Is 1:9|Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus]]; and the Apostle: [[Rom 11:5|there is a remnant saved according to the election of grace|Reliquiæ per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt]]; and again: [[Rom 11:2|God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew|Non repulit Deus plebem suam, quam præscivit]]. [[4:7|and her that had been afflicted|Et eam quæ laboraverat]] [*laboraverat*: "had laboured"], that is, the Hebrew nation already spoken of, which was afflicted in the ways described and weighed down by the burden of the law, which [[Acts 15:10|neither our fathers nor we|neque nos, neque patres nostri]], says Peter, [[Acts 15:10|have been able to bear|portare potuimus]] (this may be taken specially of the Apostles of Christ and the first believers, to whom he says: [[Luke 22:28|you are they who have continued with me in my temptations|Vos estis qui permansistis mecum in tentationibus meis]]), I will make her [[4:7|a mighty nation|ponam in gentem robustam]]: first, because they will convert countless people to the faith, and so beget many sons in Christ, in whom was fulfilled that word of Isaias: [[Is 60:22|The least shall become a thousand, and a little one a most strong nation|Minimus erit in mille, et parvulus in gentem fortissimam]]; secondly, because once they had received the Holy Ghost they were most strong in Christ, and had an invincible patience, so that they [[Acts 5:41|went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus|irent gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati]], and said to the chief priests: [[Acts 5:29|We ought to obey God rather than men|Obedire oportet Deo magis quam hominibus]]. Were they not most mighty, of whom one of them said: [[Rom 8:38|I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come|Certus sum quia neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus, neque virtutes, neque instantia, neque futura]], [[Rom 8:39|nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord|neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei, quæ est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro?]]? Therefore it is written of them in the Psalm: [[Ps 46:10|for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted|Quoniam dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt]]. And how great was the strength of the primitive Church in Jerusalem is plain in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 2:1||]] [the margin gives Acts ii–v]. [[4:7|and the Lord will reign|Et regnabit Dominus]], namely Christ, [[4:7|over them|super eos]], that is, in their hearts, [[4:7|in Mount Sion|in monte Sion]], that is, in the Church that contemplates heavenly things, which on the said mountain received the Holy Ghost in the first believers. Of which we read in Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 86:2|The Lord loveth the gates of Sion|Diligit Dominus portas Sion]]. [[4:7|from this time now and forever|Ex hoc nunc et usque in æternum]], that is, in the present life in its beginning through faith and grace, and in the world to come without end through the beatific revelation.

paras.t: Præterea, quidam exponunt hunc locum de gentilitate conversa, quæ ante suam conversionem claudicavit per idolorum culturam, eratque relicta a Deo, et in via perditionis usque lassitudinem laborabat. De qua loquitur Isaias : Lætabitur deserta et invia. Hanc autem per Apostolorum prædicationem atque miracula intra Ecclesiam congregavit. Nec omnes credentes hujusmodi salvat, sed quosdam velut reliquias, quoniam pauci electi.
paras.en: Moreover, some expound this place of the converted Gentiles, who before their conversion halted through the worship of idols, and were forsaken by God, and laboured in the way of perdition even to weariness. Of them Isaias speaks: [[Is 35:1|The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad|Lætabitur deserta et invia]]. These he gathered into the Church through the preaching and miracles of the Apostles. Nor does he save all such believers, but some, as a remnant, since there are but [[Matt 20:16|few chosen|pauci electi]].

paras.t: Et tu, turris gregis nebulosa, id est, templum Jerusalem : de quo apud Isaiam inducitur, quod Dominus ædificavit turrim in medio ejus, videlicet in Synagoga, quæ ibi vinea appellatur. Dicitur autem turris gregis, id est populi Judæorum, qui fuit grex Dei, juxta illud, Nos autem populus ejus, et oves pascuæ ejus; vel, quia in eo greges animalium offerebantur. Dicitur insuper nebulosa, vel propter vitia sacerdotum ac populi, vel propter imminentem destructionem, vel propter fumum nebulosum ex incensione hostiarum surgentem. Filiæ Sion, id est populi Judæorum. Usque ad te veniet; et veniet potestas prima, id est Christus, qui est virtus et sapientia Patris, qui cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto est una, æterna, prima ac infinita potestas : qui est regnum filiæ Jerusalem, id est rex Judaicæ plebis. De quo Isaias prædixit : Dominus rex noster, Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, ipse veniet et salvabit nos. Christus autem oblatus et præsentatus fuit in templo a Matre virginea, et frequenter prædicavit in eo. Propter quod a Malachia fuit prædictum : Statim veniet ad templum sanctum suum Dominator, quem vos quæritis, etc.; et in Psalmo, Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam in medio templi tui.
paras.en: [[4:8|And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock|Et tu, turris gregis nebulosa]], that is, the temple of Jerusalem: of which it is set forth in Isaias that the Lord [[Is 5:2|built a tower in the midst thereof|ædificavit turrim in medio ejus]], namely in the Synagogue, which is there called a vineyard[[Is 5:1||]]. It is called the tower of the flock, that is, of the Jewish people, who were the flock of God, according to that saying: [[Ps 94:7|we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand|Nos autem populus ejus, et oves pascuæ ejus]] [the margin gives Ps. xcv, 7, "according to the old version": the old Roman Psalter reads at Ps 94:7, as Denis does, "we are his people and the sheep of his pasture", the words that stand in the Vulgate at Ps 99:3]; or because flocks of animals were offered in it. It is called cloudy, moreover, either because of the vices of the priests and the people, or because of its coming destruction, or because of the cloudy smoke rising from the burning of the victims. [[4:8|Of the daughter of Sion|Filiæ Sion]], that is, of the Jewish people. [[4:8|unto thee shall it come: yea the first power shall come|Usque ad te veniet; et veniet potestas prima]], that is, Christ, who is the power and wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], who with the Father and the Holy Ghost is the one, eternal, first and infinite power: who is [[4:8|the kingdom to the daughter of Jerusalem|regnum filiæ Jerusalem]], that is, the king of the Jewish people. Of whom Isaias foretold: [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our king|Dominus rex noster]], [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our judge|Dominus judex noster]], [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our lawgiver|Dominus legifer noster]], he will come, and [[Is 33:22|he will save us|salvabit nos]]. Now Christ was offered and presented in the temple by His virgin Mother[[Luke 2:22||]], and He often preached in it[[Matt 26:55||]]. For this reason it was foretold by Malachias: [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord|Statim]] [[Mal 3:1|shall come to his temple|veniet ad templum sanctum suum Dominator]] [Denis reads "his holy temple"], [[Mal 3:1|whom you seek|quem vos quæritis]], etc.; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 47:10|We have received thy mercy, O God, in the midst of thy temple.|Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam in medio templi tui]]

paras.t: Nunc quare mœrore contraheris? id est, quum tanta consolatio tibi præstanda sit, et tanta promissio facta, o popule Sion, cur tam gravi tristitia contabescis, vel ex dilatione adventus Messiæ, vel propter persecutiones quas pateris? Numquid rex non est tibi? id est, imo Regem omnipotentem immortalemque habes, qui tandem tua assumpta natura te visitabit, et nunc te defendere lætificareque potest. Aut consiliarius tuus periit, id est Deus qui tibi per Prophetas verba consolatoria nuntiat, intusque exhilarat? Vel per consiliarium, intelligit Propheta se ipsum ac alios vates, qui populum instruebant, remediaque salutis pandebant. Christus quoque est magni consilii Angelus. Quia comprehendit te dolor sicut parturientem, ita quod in adversis non recurris ad divinum auxilium, nec in spe futurorum bonorum respiras. Possuntque hæc specialiter accipi de justis, qui Christi adventum optabant ardenter.
paras.en: [[4:9|Now, why art thou drawn together with grief?|Nunc quare mœrore contraheris?]] that is, since so great a consolation is to be granted thee, and so great a promise has been made, O people of Sion, why dost thou pine away in so heavy a sadness, whether from the delay of the Messias's coming, or because of the persecutions thou sufferest? [[4:9|Hast thou no king in thee|Numquid rex non est tibi]]? that is, nay, thou hast an almighty and immortal King, who at length, having taken thy nature, will visit thee, and even now can defend thee and make thee glad. [[4:9|or is thy counselor perished|Aut consiliarius tuus periit]], that is, God, who announces words of consolation to thee through the Prophets, and gladdens thee within? Or by the counsellor the Prophet means himself and the other seers, who instructed the people and laid open the remedies of salvation. Christ too is the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [so the Septuagint at Is 9:6, as the margin notes; the Vulgate there has "Counsellor"]. [[4:9|because sorrow hath taken thee as a woman in labour|Quia comprehendit te dolor sicut parturientem]], so that in adversity thou dost not run back to the divine help, nor breathe again in the hope of good things to come. And these words can be taken especially of the just, who longed ardently for Christ's coming.

paras.t: Dole et satage, filia Sion, quasi parturiens, id est, stude ut dolores tibi instantes æquanimiter feras. Et merito dolere potes, quia nunc egredieris de civitate Jerusalem capta, et habitabis in regione Sennaar seu Chaldæa septuaginta annis, et venies usque ad Babylonem civitatem metropolim Chaldæorum. Ibi liberaberis tempore Cyri regis de captivitate, ibi redimet te Dominus de manu inimicorum tuorum, reducendo te in propriam terram per Zorobabel, Esdram, et Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum. De hoc scriptum est plenius in libro primo Esdræ.
paras.en: [[4:10|Be in pain and labour, O daughter of Sion, as a woman that bringeth forth|Dole et satage, filia Sion, quasi parturiens]], that is, strive to bear with an even mind the pains that hang over thee. And well mayest thou grieve, [[4:10|for now shalt thou go out of the city|quia nunc egredieris de civitate]] of Jerusalem when it is taken, [[4:10|and shalt dwell in the country|et habitabis in regione]] of Sennaar, or Chaldea, for seventy years, [[4:10|and shalt come even to Babylon|et venies usque ad Babylonem]], the chief city of the Chaldeans. [[4:10|there thou shalt be delivered|Ibi liberaberis]] from captivity in the time of king Cyrus, [[4:10|there the Lord will redeem thee out of the hand of thy enemies|ibi redimet te Dominus de manu inimicorum tuorum]], by bringing thee back into thine own land through Zorobabel, Esdras, and Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest. Of this it is written more fully in the first book of Esdras[[1 Esd 1:1||]] [the margin gives I Esdr. i, ii, vii, viii].

paras.t: Et nunc, tempore meo, regnante piissimo Ezechia, congregatæ sunt super te gentes multæ, quæ dicunt : Lapidetur, et adspiciat in Sion oculus noster. Quod intelligi potest de Sennacherib rege Assyriorum et populo ejus, qui venit, et occupavit omnes urbes Juda; voluitque morte durissima, quæ per lapidationem exprimitur, necare habitatores Jerusalem, qui se ad resistentiam præparaverunt. Voluerunt quoque Assyrii in Sion adspicere, id est templum, palatium, et cetera habitacula scrutari et spoliare.
paras.en: [[4:11|And now|Et nunc]], in my time, under the reign of the most devout Ezechias, [[4:11|many nations are gathered together against thee, and they say: Let her be stoned: and let our eye look upon Sion|congregatæ sunt super te gentes multæ, quæ dicunt : Lapidetur, et adspiciat in Sion oculus noster]]. This can be understood of Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, and his people, who came and seized all the cities of Juda[[4 Kings 18:13||]]; and he wished to put to a most cruel death, which is expressed by the stoning, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, who had prepared themselves to resist. The Assyrians wished also to look upon Sion, that is, to search out and despoil the temple, the palace and the other dwellings.

paras.t: Ipsi autem non cognoverunt cogitationes Domini, id est, quod Deus voluit populum suum per illos purgare, et castigatum seu disciplinatum salvare. Illi namque propriis viribus suas victorias adscripserunt, et populum inde non corrigere, sed conterere nitebantur. Et non intellexerunt consilium ejus, id est sapientiam divinæ dispensationis, qua Deus omnipotens corrigit electos per reprobos, sicut per virgam : quo facto, reprobos æternaliter damnat, quemadmodum virga, disciplinato puero, in ignem projicitur. Hinc per Isaiam Dominus loquitur : Væ Assur, virga furoris mei et baculus ipse est ; ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur, sed ad conterendum cor ejus erit. Generaliter quoque transgressores et impii non agnoscunt cogitationem Dei, neque attendunt consilium ejus, qualiter humanum genus dispenset atque remuneret, terribilisque consistat in consiliis super filios hominum. Propter quod scriptum est in libro Sapientiæ : Quis hominum poterit scire consilium Dei ? aut quis poterit cogitare quid velit Deus? Et : Sensum tuum, Domine, quis sciet, nisi tu dederis sapientiam, et miseris spiritum tuum de cœlis ? Quia congregavit eos, id est adversarios populi sui, scilicet gentes præfatas, quasi fœnum areæ, id est in unum fascem, ut simul dispereant et damnentur, seu incendantur : quemadmodum angelus Dei percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia hominum, quorum corpora fuerunt incinerata atque combusta.
paras.en: [[4:12|But they have not known the thoughts of the Lord|Ipsi autem non cognoverunt cogitationes Domini]], that is, that God willed to purge His people through them, and to save it once chastised or disciplined. For they ascribed their victories to their own strength, and strove thereby not to correct the people but to crush it. [[4:12|and have not understood his counsel|Et non intellexerunt consilium ejus]], that is, the wisdom of the divine dispensation, by which almighty God corrects the elect through the reprobate, as through a rod: and when this is done, He damns the reprobate eternally, just as the rod, once the boy has been disciplined, is thrown into the fire. Hence the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 10:5|Woe to the Assyrian, he is the rod and the staff of my anger|Væ Assur, virga furoris mei et baculus ipse est]]; [[Is 10:7|But he shall not take it so|ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur]], [[Is 10:7|but his heart shall be set to destroy|sed ad conterendum cor ejus erit]]. In general too, transgressors and the wicked do not acknowledge the thought of God, nor heed His counsel, how He orders and rewards the human race, and stands [[Ps 65:5|terrible in his counsels over the sons of men|terribilisque consistat in consiliis super filios hominum]]. For this reason it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 9:13|who among men is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can think what the will of God is?|Quis hominum poterit scire consilium Dei ? aut quis poterit cogitare quid velit Deus?]] And: [[Wis 9:17|who shall know thy thought, except thou give wisdom, and send thy holy Spirit from above|Sensum tuum, Domine, quis sciet, nisi tu dederis sapientiam, et miseris spiritum tuum de cœlis]]? [[4:12|because he hath gathered them together|Quia congregavit eos]], that is, the adversaries of His people, namely the nations aforesaid, [[4:12|as the hay of the floor|quasi fœnum areæ]], that is, into one bundle, that they may perish and be damned, or burned, together: just as the angel of God [[4 Kings 19:35|slew in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand|percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia]] men, whose bodies were burnt to ashes and consumed.

paras.t: Surge et tritura, filia Sion, id est tu, popule Judæorum, post reditum a Chaldæa seu Babylonica captivitate, disperge, vexa, occide adversarios tuos gentiles; quia cornu tuum ponam ferreum, id est, potestatem victoriosam seu principem fortissimum tibi præstabo, et ungulas tuas ponam æreas, id est, manus tibi dabo victrices, aliorum laceratrices, quemadmodum ferrum et æs cetera domant atque confringunt. Et comminues populos multos, et interficies Domino rapinas eorum, id est, prædam pecorum offeres Deo, et ad gloriam ejus rapinam diripies. Sic enim in libro Numerorum et Josue legitur præda Deo consecrata in toto vel in parte. Et fortitudinem eorum, id est majores et potentiores interficies, Domino universæ terræ : qui pessimos voluit trucidari ; qui etiam Saulem et Achab redarguit, quoniam regibus morte dignis Agag et Benadad pepercerunt.
paras.en: [[4:13|Arise, and tread, O daughter of Sion|Surge et tritura, filia Sion]], that is, thou, O people of the Jews, after the return from Chaldea or the Babylonian captivity, scatter, harass, slay thy Gentile adversaries; [[4:13|for I will make thy horn iron|quia cornu tuum ponam ferreum]], that is, I will give thee a victorious power or a most mighty prince, [[4:13|and thy hoofs I will make brass|et ungulas tuas ponam æreas]], that is, I will give thee hands that conquer and tear others, as iron and brass subdue and break all else. [[4:13|and thou shalt beat in pieces many peoples|Et comminues populos multos]], [[4:13|and shalt immolate the spoils of them to the Lord|et interficies Domino rapinas eorum]], that is, thou shalt offer the booty of cattle to God, and shalt take the plunder for His glory. For so we read in the book of Numbers[[Num 31:37||]] and in Josue[[Jos 6:24||]] of booty consecrated to God, in whole or in part [the margin gives Num. xxxi, 37–42]. [[4:13|and their strength|Et fortitudinem eorum]], that is, the greater and more powerful of them thou shalt slay [[4:13|to the Lord of the whole earth|Domino universæ terræ]]: who willed that the worst should be slaughtered; who also rebuked Saul[[1 Kings 15:16||]] and Achab[[3 Kings 20:42||]] because they spared Agag and Benadad, kings worthy of death [the margin gives I Reg. xv, 16 and following; III Reg. xx, 42].

paras.t: Videtur autem quibusdam, quod ista non sint in populo Judaico impleta post reditum a Chaldæa, nec tanta fuerit virtus eorum. Sed si historiam Machabæorum recolimus, videtur utique tempore Judæ et fratrum ejus impletum. Unde secundo libro Machabæorum legitur, quod Judas efficiebatur intolerabilis gentibus, et non paucas hominum strages dabat, civitates et castella succendens. Denique et primo libro Machabæorum legitur : Et surrexit Judas ; et adjuvabant eum omnes fratres ejus, et præliabantur prælium Israel cum lætitia. Et dilatavit gloriam populo suo, et induit se loricam sicut gigas, et protegebat castra gladio suo. Similis factus est leoni in operibus suis, et sicut catulus leonis rugiens in venatione. Et persecutus est iniquos, perscrutans eos ; et qui conturbabant populum suum, succendit flammis ; et repulsi sunt inimici præ timore ejus, et omnes operarii iniquitatis conturbati sunt ; et directa est salus in manu ejus. Et exacerbabat reges multos, et lætificabat Jacob in operibus suis. Et perambulavit civitates Juda, et perdidit impios ex eis, et avertit iram ab Israel. Et nominatus est usque ad novissimum terræ, et congregavit pereuntes. Multaque alia in libris Machabæorum conscripta sunt, ex quibus patet hæc ad litteram esse impleta. Inter hæc unum est, quod semel in Antiochia tria millia Judæorum interfecerunt centum millia aliorum.
paras.en: Now it seems to some that these things were not fulfilled in the Jewish people after the return from Chaldea, and that their might was never so great. But if we call to mind the history of the Machabees, it does seem to have been fulfilled in the time of Judas and his brethren. Hence we read in the second book of Machabees that Judas [[2 Mach 8:5|could not be withstood by the heathens|efficiebatur intolerabilis gentibus]], and [[2 Mach 8:6|made no small slaughter|non paucas hominum strages dabat]] of men, setting fire to cities and castles. And again in the first book of Machabees we read: And Judas [[1 Mach 3:1|rose up|Et surrexit Judas]]; [[1 Mach 3:2|And all his brethren helped him|et adjuvabant eum omnes fratres ejus]], and [[1 Mach 3:2|they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel|præliabantur prælium Israel cum lætitia]]. [[1 Mach 3:3|And he got his people great honour, and put on a breastplate as a giant|Et dilatavit gloriam populo suo, et induit se loricam sicut gigas]], [[1 Mach 3:3|and protected the camp with his sword|et protegebat castra gladio suo]]. [[1 Mach 3:4|In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion's whelp roaring for his prey.|Similis factus est leoni in operibus suis, et sicut catulus leonis rugiens in venatione]] [[1 Mach 3:5|And he pursued the wicked and sought them out, and them that troubled his people he burnt with fire:|Et persecutus est iniquos, perscrutans eos ; et qui conturbabant populum suum, succendit flammis]] [[1 Mach 3:6|And his enemies were driven away for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled: and salvation prospered in his hand.|et repulsi sunt inimici præ timore ejus, et omnes operarii iniquitatis conturbati sunt ; et directa est salus in manu ejus]] [[1 Mach 3:7|And he grieved many kings, and made Jacob glad with his works|Et exacerbabat reges multos, et lætificabat Jacob in operibus suis]]. [[1 Mach 3:8|And he went through the cities of Juda, and destroyed the wicked out of them, and turned away wrath from Israel.|Et perambulavit civitates Juda, et perdidit impios ex eis, et avertit iram ab Israel]] [[1 Mach 3:9|And he was renowned even to the utmost part of the earth, and he gathered them that were perishing.|Et nominatus est usque ad novissimum terræ, et congregavit pereuntes]] And many other things are written in the books of Machabees, from which it is clear that these words were fulfilled to the letter. Among them is this: that once at Antioch three thousand Jews[[1 Mach 11:44||]] slew a hundred thousand others[[1 Mach 11:48||]] [the margin gives I Mach. xi, 44–48].

paras.t: Porro, moraliter cohortari se debent Christiani, dicentes : Venite, ascendamus ad montem Domini, et ad domum Dei Jacob, id est, ecclesiam jugiter visitemus, et divinis obsequiis præsentialiter interesse curemus; et docebit nos Dominus de viis suis : ibi enim prædicatio fit verbi Dei, et instructio salutaris proponitur. Deus quoque tales per occultum instinctum informat, et angeli sancti illuminant eos. Et concident gladios suos in vomeres. Hoc quotidie agitur, dum contentiosi, iracundi, impatientes convertuntur ad pacem et mansuetudinem Christi, et verba pungitiva cessant proferre. De hujuscemodi siquidem gladio fertur in Psalmo : Gladius in labiis ipsorum; itemque, Filii hominum, dentes eorum arma et sagittæ, et lingua eorum gladius acutus.
paras.en: Further, in the moral sense Christians ought to exhort one another, saying: [[4:2|Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob|Venite, ascendamus ad montem Domini, et ad domum Dei Jacob]], that is, let us visit the church constantly, and take care to be present in person at the divine offices; [[4:2|and he will teach us of his ways|et docebit nos Dominus de viis suis]]: for there the word of God is preached, and saving instruction is set forth. God also forms such people by a hidden prompting, and the holy angels enlighten them. [[4:3|they shall beat their swords into ploughshares|Et concident gladios suos in vomeres]]. This is done every day, when the quarrelsome, the wrathful and the impatient are turned to the peace and meekness of Christ, and cease to utter stinging words. For of such a sword it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 58:8|a sword is in their lips|Gladius in labiis ipsorum]]; and again: [[Ps 56:5|The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword|Filii hominum, dentes eorum arma et sagittæ, et lingua eorum gladius acutus]].

paras.t: In die illa, dicit Dominus, congregabo claudicantem, id est animam vagam, instabilem, oberrantem, et eam quam ejeceram, id est, a qua ad tempus gratiam subtraxi aut suspendi, et quam afflixeram tentationibus, persecutionibus atque languoribus. Christus enim calamum conquassatum non conterit, et linum fumigans non exstinguit, sed reparat, juxta illud in Psalmo : Dominus erigit elisos. Talibus igitur animabus sæpe dat Christus divinorum charismatum affluentiam magnam, ut ubi abundavit iniquitas, abundet et gratia. Tuncque claudicans in reliquias ponitur, id est inter electos et virtuosos, ut faciat rectos gressus pedibus suis; et quæ laboravit, robusta efficitur.
paras.en: [[4:6|In that day, saith the Lord, I will gather up her that halteth|In die illa, dicit Dominus, congregabo claudicantem]], that is, the wandering, unstable, straying soul, [[4:6|and her that I had cast out|et eam quam ejeceram]], that is, from whom for a time I withdrew or held back grace, [[4:6|and her whom I had afflicted|et quam afflixeram]] with temptations, persecutions and infirmities. For Christ [[Is 42:3|The bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench|calamum conquassatum non conterit, et linum fumigans non exstinguit]], but restores them, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 145:8|The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down|Dominus erigit elisos]]. To such souls, then, Christ often gives a great abundance of divine gifts, so that where iniquity abounded, grace too may abound[[Rom 5:20||]]. And then she that halted is made [[4:7|a remnant|in reliquias]], that is, she is set among the elect and the virtuous, that she may make straight steps with her feet[[Heb 12:13||]]; and she that had laboured is made strong.

paras.t: Insuper Ecclesiæ, vel unicuique afflicto, mœsto, tentatoque dicitur verbum dulce, bonum ac consolatorium : Nunc quare mœrore contraheris? quum non sint condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis; et si compatimur, conregnabimus; omneque gaudium æstimandum sit, quum in diversas tentationes inciderimus. Numquid rex non est tibi, scilicet Filius Dei, qui te valet eripere? Aut consiliarius tuus periit, qui evangelica dedit consilia, et in omni adversitate docet esse gaudendum? Beati, inquit, eritis, quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me. Gaudete et exsultate in illa hora, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Quia comprehendit te dolor sicut parturientem, id est, quasi non esset futura consolatio danda his qui nunc diversis tribulationibus exercentur.
paras.en: Moreover, to the Church, or to every one who is afflicted, sorrowful and tempted, a sweet, good and consoling word is spoken: [[4:9|Now, why art thou drawn together with grief?|Nunc quare mœrore contraheris?]] since [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|non sint condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis]]; and [[Rom 8:17|if we suffer with him|si compatimur]], [[2 Tim 2:12|we shall also reign with him|conregnabimus]]; and all should be counted joy when we fall into divers temptations[[Jas 1:2||]]. [[4:9|Hast thou no king in thee|Numquid rex non est tibi]], namely the Son of God, who is able to rescue thee? [[4:9|or is thy counselor perished|Aut consiliarius tuus periit]], who gave the counsels of the Gospel, and teaches that we must rejoice in every adversity? [[Matt 5:11|Blessed are ye|Beati]], he says, [[Matt 5:11|when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly, for my sake|eritis, quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me]]. [[Matt 5:12|Be glad and rejoice|Gaudete et exsultate]] in that hour, [[Matt 5:12|for your reward is very great in heaven|quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]]. [[4:9|because sorrow hath taken thee as a woman in labour|Quia comprehendit te dolor sicut parturientem]], that is, as though no consolation were to be given in the future to those who are now tried by divers tribulations.

paras.t: Dole pro tuis et proximorum peccatis, et satage, id est, viriliter age quæ Dei sunt : quemadmodum Salomon docet : Quodcumque potest manus tua, instanter operare, quia nec opus, nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos; filia Sion, id est, anima speculativa, seu persona aut congregatio ecclesiastica in specula Domini constituta, quasi parturiens, id est in magnis adversitatibus posita. Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Quia nunc egredieris de civitate, id est, exsulabis, de propriis locis expulsa, et habitabis in regione dissimilitudinis, vel inter iniquos; et venies usque ad Babylonem, id est confusionem magnam tentationum et persecutionum, in tantum ut forte quandoque a principe Babylonis, id est diabolo, captiveris in consensum peccati, et vinculis vitiorum adstringaris, Deo permittente te cadere, quatenus propria fragilitate experta, profundius humilieris et cautior fias. Babylon autem interpretatur confusio. Et in sæculo isto confusa sunt omnia : quoniam mundus totus in maligno positus est; et omne quod est in mundo, est concupiscentia carnis, aut concupiscentia oculorum, aut superbia vitæ. Ibi liberaberis. Non enim permittit nos Deus tentari supra id quod possumus, sed facit cum tentatione proventum. Et electos suos eripit Christus finaliter, sicut in Evangelio dicit de ovibus suis, quod nemo rapiet eas de manu sua et Patris sui, nec peribunt in sempiternum : quia Ego, inquit, vitam æternam do eis. Ibi redimet te Dominus de manu inimicorum tuorum visibilium et invisibilium : dicente Psalmista, Et adjuvabit eos Dominus, et liberabit eos, et eruet eos a peccatoribus, et salvabit eos, quia speraverunt in eo.
paras.en: [[4:10|Be in pain|Dole]] for thy own sins and thy neighbours', [[4:10|and labour|et satage]], that is, do manfully the things that are God's: as Solomon teaches: [[Eccles 9:10|Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, do it earnestly: for neither work, nor reason, nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell|Quodcumque potest manus tua, instanter operare, quia nec opus, nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos]]; [[4:10|O daughter of Sion|filia Sion]], that is, the contemplative soul [Latin *speculativa*, from *specula*, a watch-tower; Sion was taken to mean "watch-tower"], or a churchman or religious community set in the Lord's watch-tower, [[4:10|as a woman that bringeth forth|quasi parturiens]], that is, set in great adversities. For [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur]]. [[4:10|for now shalt thou go out of the city|Quia nunc egredieris de civitate]], that is, thou shalt be an exile, driven out of thine own places, [[4:10|and shalt dwell in the country|et habitabis in regione]] of unlikeness [the "region of unlikeness" of Augustine's Confessions: the state of the soul fallen away from its likeness to God], or among the wicked; [[4:10|and shalt come even to Babylon|et venies usque ad Babylonem]], that is, to a great confusion of temptations and persecutions, so much so that perhaps at times thou wilt be taken captive by the prince of Babylon, that is, the devil, into consent to sin, and bound with the chains of vices, God permitting thee to fall, so that, having learned thine own frailty, thou mayest be more deeply humbled and become more cautious. For Babylon is interpreted confusion. And in this world all things are confused: for [[1 John 5:19|the whole world is seated in wickedness|mundus totus in maligno positus est]]; and [[1 John 2:16|all that is in the world is the concupiscence of the flesh and the concupiscence of the eyes and the pride of life|omne quod est in mundo, est concupiscentia carnis, aut concupiscentia oculorum, aut superbia vitæ]]. [[4:10|there thou shalt be delivered|Ibi liberaberis]]. For God does not suffer us to be tempted above that which we are able, but makes with the temptation issue [that is, a way out][[1 Cor 10:13||]]. And Christ at the last rescues His elect, as He says in the Gospel of His sheep that no one shall snatch them out of His hand and His Father's[[John 10:29||]], and they shall not perish for ever: for [[John 10:28|I|Ego]], he says, [[John 10:28|give them life everlasting|vitam æternam do eis]]. [[4:10|there the Lord will redeem thee out of the hand of thy enemies|Ibi redimet te Dominus de manu inimicorum tuorum]], visible and invisible; as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 36:40|And the Lord will help them and deliver them: and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them because they have hoped in him.|Et adjuvabit eos Dominus, et liberabit eos, et eruet eos a peccatoribus, et salvabit eos, quia speraverunt in eo]]

paras.t: Et nunc congregatæ sunt super te gentes multæ, adversarii Ecclesiæ diaboli, homines iniqui, sævi, et reprobi. Quæ dicunt : Lapidetur Ecclesia seu persona ecclesiastica, ita ut obruatur adversis, et a statu æquitatis labatur, et adspiciat in Sion oculus noster, id est, calamitatem et oppressionem justorum cum lætitia intueamur. Ipsi autem non cognoverunt cogitationes Domini, qui cogitavit persecutionem patientibus dare coronam vitæ, si usque ad mortem consistant fideles, persecutoribus vero pœnam gehennæ.
paras.en: [[4:11|And now many nations are gathered together against thee|Et nunc congregatæ sunt super te gentes multæ]], the devils, adversaries of the Church, and wicked, savage and reprobate men, [[4:11|and they say: Let her be stoned|Quæ dicunt : Lapidetur]], the Church or a churchman, so that she may be overwhelmed by adversities and slip from the state of righteousness, [[4:11|and let our eye look upon Sion|et adspiciat in Sion oculus noster]], that is, let us gaze with gladness on the calamity and oppression of the just. [[4:12|But they have not known the thoughts of the Lord|Ipsi autem non cognoverunt cogitationes Domini]], who purposed to give to those who suffer persecution [[Apoc 2:10|the crown of life|coronam vitæ]], if they remain faithful unto death, but to the persecutors the punishment of hell.

paras.t: Surge et tritura, filia Sion, id est, adversarios tuos Christi virtute vince et ventila : quemadmodum ait fortis pugnator, Comminuam eos ut pulverem ante faciem venti ; quia cornu tuum ponam ferreum, ut omnia possis in eo qui te confortat. Potest quoque in bono intelligi, ut dicatur eos triturare, quorum colla subdit Christo ac fidei. Et comminues populos multos, vitia exstirpando ab eis, atque ad veram eos contritionem trahendo. Sicque comminuti sunt parvi et humiles in oculis suis. Et interficies Domino rapinas eorum, id est, Christo consecrabis, et divinis obsequiis applicabis divitias eorum qui convertuntur, et fortitudinem eorum Domino universæ terræ, ut totis viribus Christo ministrent, qui loquitur : Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra.
paras.en: [[4:13|Arise, and tread, O daughter of Sion|Surge et tritura, filia Sion]], that is, conquer and winnow thy adversaries by the power of Christ: as the strong warrior says: [[Ps 17:43|I shall beat them as small as the dust before the wind|Comminuam eos ut pulverem ante faciem venti]]; [[4:13|for I will make thy horn iron|quia cornu tuum ponam ferreum]], so that thou canst do all things in him who strengthens thee[[Phil 4:13||]]. It can also be understood in a good sense, so that she is said to tread those whose necks she brings under the yoke of Christ and of the faith. [[4:13|and thou shalt beat in pieces many peoples|Et comminues populos multos]], by rooting out vices from them and drawing them to true contrition. And so, beaten in pieces, they become little and humble in their own eyes [*comminuti*, "beaten small", plays on *contritio*, "contrition", literally a crushing]. [[4:13|and shalt immolate the spoils of them to the Lord|Et interficies Domino rapinas eorum]], that is, thou shalt consecrate to Christ and devote to the divine service the riches of those who are converted, [[4:13|and their strength|et fortitudinem eorum]] [[4:13|to the Lord of the whole earth|Domino universæ terræ]], so that they may serve with all their strength Christ, who says: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]].

paras.t: Postremo capitulum istud, ab illo loco : Dole et satage, filia Sion, a diversis valde diversimode explanatur ad litteram; sed propter prolixitatem vitandam omitto, et quia præinducta expositio videtur conformior textui. Judæi autem, secundum consuetudinem suæ cæcitatis, præstolantur ista implenda in adventu sui Messiæ, ita quod tunc Romano imperio prævalebunt, cunctisque gentibus imperabunt.
