paras.en: Lastly, this chapter, from the place [[4:10|Be in pain and labour, O daughter of Sion|Dole et satage, filia Sion]] on, is explained in the literal sense by different writers in very different ways; but I leave these out to avoid length, and because the exposition given above seems more in keeping with the text. The Jews, however, after the custom of their blindness, await the fulfilment of these things at the coming of their Messias, in such wise that they will then prevail over the Roman empire and rule over all nations.

5.title: Expositio capituli quinti: Nunc vastaberis, filia latronis.
5.title_en: Exposition of the fifth chapter: Now shalt thou be laid waste, O daughter of the robber.

paras.t: In fine præcedentis capituli multa prospera Deus promisit Synagogæ, seu plebi Judaicæ. Jam vero comminatur eidem. Nunc vastaberis, id est, ab hostibus capieris, filia latronis, id est Synagoga, quæ propter tua peccata es filia diaboli latronis pravissimi, qui animam strangulat. Effuderunt enim Judæi in templo sanguinem innocentem, et subjectos ac simplices multipliciter deceperunt. Unde Salvator quoque ait in Evangelio : Domus mea domus orationis vocabitur, vos autem fecistis illam speluncam latronum. Obsidionem posuerunt inimici nostri super nos, id est contra Judæos, civitates Juda obsidendo. In virga percutient maxillam judicis Israel, id est, superiores ac judices Judæorum in faciem cædent, viliterque tractabunt ut alios.
paras.en: At the end of the preceding chapter God promised many prosperous things to the Synagogue, or the Jewish people. Now, however, he threatens it. [[5:1|Now shalt thou be laid waste|Nunc vastaberis]], that is, thou shalt be taken by enemies, [[5:1|O daughter of the robber|filia latronis]], that is, O Synagogue, who for thy sins art the daughter of the devil, that most wicked robber who strangles the soul. For the Jews [[Ps 105:38|shed innocent blood|sanguinem innocentem]] in the temple, and deceived their subjects and the simple in many ways. Hence the Saviour too says in the Gospel: [[Matt 21:13|My house shall be called the house of prayer; but you have made it a den of thieves|Domus mea domus orationis vocabitur, vos autem fecistis illam speluncam latronum]] [*latronum*, “of thieves”, is the same word as *latronis*, “of the robber”, in this verse]. Our enemies [[5:1|have laid siege against us|Obsidionem posuerunt inimici nostri super nos]] [Denis's text adds *inimici nostri*, “our enemies”], that is, against the Jews, by besieging the cities of Juda. [[5:1|With a rod shall they strike the cheek of the judge of Israel|In virga percutient maxillam judicis Israel]], that is, they will strike the superiors and judges of the Jews in the face, and treat them as basely as the rest.

paras.t: Quidam referunt ista ad Babylonicam captivitatem, in qua Sedecias rex, sacerdotes ac principes ejus, a Chaldæis contemptibiliter cæsi tractatique sunt. — Alii vero referunt ad vastitatem Judæorum a Romanis, in qua gravissime sunt oppressi, et sacerdotes jubente Tito occisi. Et ita exponit Hieronymus.
paras.en: Some refer these words to the Babylonian captivity, in which King Sedecias[[4 Kings 25:7||]] and his priests and princes[[4 Kings 25:18||]][[4 Kings 25:21||]] were beaten and treated with contempt by the Chaldeans. Others, however, refer them to the laying waste of the Jews by the Romans, in which they were most grievously oppressed, and the priests were slain at the command of Titus. And so Jerome explains it.

paras.t: Unde quod ait Propheta, Obsidionem posuerunt super nos, exponit in persona Dei Patris, loquentis de se et Filio ac Spiritu Sancto. Contra quos posuerunt Judæi obsidionem, Filium Dei persequendo, in Spiritum Sanctum blasphemando, et Patrem mendacem faciendo. Qui enim non credit in Filium, mendacem facit Patrem, secundum Joannem. Et Christus ait : Nunc autem oderunt et me et Patrem meum gratis. In virga quoque seu aspero ictu percusserunt maxillam judicis Israel, id est Christi, cui Pater dedit omne judicium. Qui in Evangelio loquitur Judæis : Multa habeo de vobis loqui et judicare ; et, Amodo videbitis Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli. Hujus maxillas dulcissimas percusserunt manibus incestis atque sacrilegis in nocte illa, potestati tenebrarum concessa, quemadmodum Lucas asserit : Viri qui tenebant illum, illudebant ei, cædentes eum, et percusserunt faciem ejus. Minister quoque pontificis dedit ei alapam, dicens : Sic respondes pontifici? Quod et ministri Pilati, procurantibus Judæis, fecerunt, dum plectentes coronam de spinis, imposuerunt capiti ejus. Et veniebant, et dabant ei alapas. Quod et Sibylla prædixisse cognoscitur.
paras.en: Hence what the Prophet says, [[5:1|they have laid siege against us|Obsidionem posuerunt super nos]], he explains in the person of God the Father, speaking of himself and of the Son and the Holy Ghost. Against them the Jews laid siege, by persecuting the Son of God, by blaspheming against the Holy Ghost, and by making the Father a liar. For [[1 John 5:10|he that believeth not the Son maketh him a liar|Qui enim non credit in Filium, mendacem facit Patrem]] [Denis's wording: “he that believeth not in the Son maketh the Father a liar”], according to John. And Christ says: But now they have [[John 15:24|hated both me and my Father|oderunt et me et Patrem meum]] without cause [*gratis*, “without cause”, comes from the next verse, John 15:25]. [[5:1|With a rod|In virga]] too, or with a harsh blow, they struck [[5:1|the cheek of the judge of Israel|maxillam judicis Israel]], that is, of Christ, to whom the Father [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment|dedit omne judicium]]; who in the Gospel says to the Jews: [[John 8:26|Many things I have to speak and to judge of you|Multa habeo de vobis loqui et judicare]]; and: [[Matt 26:64|Hereafter you shall see the Son of man|Amodo videbitis Filium hominis]] [[Matt 26:64|coming in the clouds of heaven|venientem in nubibus cœli]]. His most sweet cheeks they struck with unchaste and sacrilegious hands on that night, given over to the power of darkness, as Luke declares: [[Luke 22:63|The men that held him mocked him and struck him|Viri qui tenebant illum, illudebant ei, cædentes eum]], [[Luke 22:64|and smote his face|et percusserunt faciem ejus]]. The servant of the high priest too [[John 18:22|gave Jesus a blow, saying: Answerest thou the high priest so?|dedit ei alapam, dicens : Sic respondes pontifici?]] And Pilate's servants did the same, at the instigation of the Jews, when they, [[John 19:2|platting a crown of thorns, put it upon his head|plectentes coronam de spinis, imposuerunt capiti ejus]]. [[John 19:3|And they came to him|Et veniebant]], [[John 19:3|and they gave him blows|et dabant ei alapas]]. And the Sibyl is known to have foretold this too.

paras.t: Consequenter tractatur de Judice isto, de loco nativitatis ejus, et duplici natura ac generatione ipsius. Et tu, Bethlehem Ephrata, id est, civitas binomia. Dicta est enim Bethlehem et Ephrata, juxta illud Genesis : Mortua est Rachel, et sepulta in via Ephrata : hæc est Bethlehem. Parvulus es, id est modicus locus, seu viculus, in millibus Juda, id est comparatione aliorum locorum tribus Juda. Vel est sensus, quod populus Bethlehem parvus fuit respectu millium populorum aliarum urbium Juda.
paras.en: Next he treats of this Judge: of the place of his birth, and of his twofold nature and generation. [[5:2|And thou Bethlehem Ephrata|Et tu, Bethlehem Ephrata]], that is, a city with two names. For it was called both Bethlehem and Ephrata, according to that of Genesis: [[Gen 35:19|Rachel died, and was buried in the highway that leadeth to Ephrata, this is Bethlehem|Mortua est Rachel, et sepulta in via Ephrata : hæc est Bethlehem]]. [[5:2|Art a little one|Parvulus es]], that is, a small place, or hamlet, [[5:2|among the thousands of Juda|in millibus Juda]], that is, in comparison with the other places of the tribe of Juda. Or the sense is that the people of Bethlehem was small in respect of the thousands of people of the other cities of Juda.

paras.t: Verum Matthæus scripturam istam sic allegat : Et tu, Bethleem terra Juda, nequaquam minima es in principibus Juda. Sicque in verbis contrarietas sonat. Unde Hieronymus dicit, Matthæum verba hæc allegasse, non sicut noverat esse scripta, sed sicut sacerdotes et Scribæ allegabant respondendo Herodi, ut ostenderet S. Matthæus errorem illorum negligentiamque in lectione Scripturarum. Alii vero dicunt, Matthæum magis respexisse ad mentem et sensum prophetiæ, quam ad formam verborum. Michæas namque intendit monstrare eminentiam Bethlehem per hoc, quod Christus in ea natus est : idcirco Matthæus sic ait, Nequaquam minima es. De hoc latius dixi super Matthæum.
paras.en: But Matthew cites this scripture thus: [[Matt 2:6|And thou Bethlehem the land of Juda art not the least among the princes of Juda|Et tu, Bethleem terra Juda, nequaquam minima es in principibus Juda]]. And so the words sound contradictory. Hence Jerome says that Matthew cited these words not as he knew them to be written, but as the priests and scribes cited them in answering Herod, so that St Matthew might show their error and their negligence in reading the Scriptures. Others, however, say that Matthew looked to the mind and sense of the prophecy rather than to the form of the words. For Micheas means to show the eminence of Bethlehem by this, that Christ was born in it: therefore Matthew says thus, [[Matt 2:6|art not the least|Nequaquam minima es]]. I have spoken of this more fully on Matthew.

paras.t: Ex te mihi egredietur, id est, ad honorem et gloriam meam nascetur, qui sit dominator in Israel, id est rex Messias natus ex semine David, qui fuit de Bethlehem Juda, in qua Christus natus est de beatissima Virgine. De hoc dominatore Israel dictum est in Osee : Servient David regi suo ; et item in Isaia, Super solium David, et super regnum ejus sedebit. De quo Gabriel dixit gloriosæ ac benedictæ Mariæ : Et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum. Hoc ergo de humana ac temporali Christi generatione sit dictum.
paras.en: [[5:2|Out of thee shall he come forth unto me|Ex te mihi egredietur]], that is, shall be born to my honour and glory, [[5:2|that is to be the ruler in Israel|qui sit dominator in Israel]], that is, the King Messias, born of the seed of David, who was of Bethlehem Juda, in which Christ was born of the most blessed Virgin. Of this ruler of Israel it is said in Osee: [[Jer 30:9|They shall serve|Servient]] [[Jer 30:9|David their king|David regi suo]] [the margin gives Osee iii, 5, which has “and David, their king”; Denis's words are those of Jer 30:9]; and again in Isaias: [[Is 9:7|He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom|Super solium David, et super regnum ejus sedebit]]. Of whom Gabriel said to the glorious and blessed Mary: [[Luke 1:32|And he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Et regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]]. Let this, then, be said of the human and temporal generation of Christ.

paras.t: De cujus generatione divina ac sempiterna subjungitur : et egressus ejus, id est generatio a Patre, est ab initio, id est ab æterno et ante sæcula universa. In principio enim erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, qui ait in Psalmo : Ex utero ante luciferum genui te. A diebus æternitatis, id est ab ipso momento seu nunc æternitatis, quæ omne tempus includit. Æternaliter nempe et invariabiliter Filius generatur a Patre. Estque egressio ista immanens, non foris transiens, quum genitus consubstantialis sit generanti. Denique quod generatio Filii, egressus dicatur, constat ex hoc quod Filius ait in Joanne : Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum. De hac generatione loquitur Christus, æterna sapientia Patris, in Proverbiis : Nondum erant abyssi, et ego jam concepta eram ; ante colles ego parturiebam. In Ecclesiastico quoque : Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam.
paras.en: Of his divine and everlasting generation it is added: [[5:2|and his going forth|et egressus ejus]], that is, his generation from the Father, [[5:2|is from the beginning|est ab initio]], that is, from eternity and before all ages. For [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word: and the Word was with God|In principio enim erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum]], who says in the Psalm: [[Ps 109:3|From the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]]. [[5:2|From the days of eternity|A diebus æternitatis]], that is, from the very moment or *now* of eternity, which includes all time. For the Son is begotten of the Father eternally and unchangeably. And this going forth is immanent [that is, it remains within God], not passing outward, since the one begotten is consubstantial with the one begetting. Finally, that the generation of the Son is called a going forth is clear from this, that the Son says in John: [[John 16:28|I came forth from the Father and am come into the world|Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum]]. Of this generation Christ, the eternal wisdom of the Father, speaks in Proverbs: [[Prov 8:24|The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived|Nondum erant abyssi, et ego jam concepta eram]]; [[Prov 8:25|before the hills, I was brought forth|ante colles ego parturiebam]]. In Ecclesiasticus too: [[Ecclus 24:5|I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures|Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam]].

paras.t: Propter hoc, id est, quoniam Christus ab æterno est, et omnium temporum Dominus ac moderator omnipotens, per quem reges regnant, qui transfert regna atque constituit ; vel, Propter hoc, id est, quia in Bethlehem natus est, scilicet ob incarnationis suæ mysterium et honorem ; dabit eos, id est, Judæos in terra promissionis regnare ac habitare permittere, usque ad tempus in quo parturiens pariet, id est, gentilitas diu sterilis multos in Christo filios procreabit (quemadmodum Isaias prædixit : Quia multi filii desertæ, magis quam ejus quæ habet virum), hoc est, usque ad tempus divulgationis seu publicationis evangelicæ legis. Permisit itaque Salvator Judæos in terra hac per quadraginta circiter annos post suam passionem, dans illis locum et tempus pœnitendi, quia ex illo populo humanam assumpsit naturam. Et infra hoc tempus fuit ubique divulgatum Evangelium Christi. Quo facto, et illis obstinatis, venit Romanorum exercitus, et captos destruxit. Vel per parturientem intelligi potest primitiva Ecclesia, quæ non sine labore ac multiplici persecutione gentiles in Christo regeneravit.
paras.en: [[5:3|Therefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because Christ is from eternity, and the Lord and almighty ruler of all times, by whom kings reign, who [[Dan 2:21|taketh away kingdoms, and establisheth them|transfert regna atque constituit]]; or, [[5:3|Therefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because he was born in Bethlehem, namely on account of the mystery and honour of his incarnation, [[5:3|will he give them|dabit eos]], that is, he will let the Jews reign and dwell in the land of promise [Denis takes *dabit eos*, “he will give them”, as “he will grant them their land”; the Douay-Rheims reads “will he give them up”], [[5:3|even till the time wherein she that travaileth shall bring forth|usque ad tempus in quo parturiens pariet]], that is, the Gentile world, long barren, shall bring forth many children in Christ (as Isaias foretold: [[Is 54:1|for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband|Quia multi filii desertæ, magis quam ejus quæ habet virum]]); that is, until the time of the spreading abroad or publishing of the law of the Gospel. And so the Saviour let the Jews stay in this land for about forty years after his passion, giving them place and time for repentance, because he took human nature from that people. And within this time the Gospel of Christ was spread abroad everywhere. When this was done, and they remained obstinate, the army of the Romans came, took them and destroyed them. Or by her that travaileth may be understood the early Church, which not without toil and manifold persecution regenerated the Gentiles in Christ.

paras.t: Reliquiæ fratrum ejus, id est electi Judæorum fratrum Christi, qui de eorum natus est populo. Unde non confunditur fratres eos vocare, dicens : Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis. Et post resurrectionem ait ad Magdalenam : Vade, et dic fratribus meis. Convertentur ad filios Israel, id est ad fidem duodecim Patriarcharum, qui erant filii Jacob, alio nomine Israel dicti. Judæi enim per Apostolorum doctrinam et signa conversi, id crediderunt factum per Jesum, quod Patriarchæ crediderunt fiendum per Christum. Vel, filii Israel sunt Apostoli filii Christi, qui est verissimus Israelita, quoniam non obscure per fidem, sed clare per speciem jugiter vidit Deum. Ad horum autem filiorum Israel fidem et conversationem, conversa sunt millia illa Judæorum, de quibus scriptum est in Actibus Apostolorum. Potest insuper accipi de Judæis qui in fine sæculi convertentur, prædicante Elia, qui convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres. Per hoc enim quod convertet Judæos tunc existentes ad fidem caritatemque Christi, faciet eos unanimes seu concordes Patriarchis et ceteris Sanctis qui erant sub lege. Sicque corda filiorum ad patres, et corda patrum convertentur ad filios.
paras.en: [[5:3|The remnant of his brethren|Reliquiæ fratrum ejus]], that is, the elect of the Jews, the brethren of Christ, who was born of their people. Hence [[Heb 2:11|he is not ashamed to call them brethren, saying|non confunditur fratres eos vocare, dicens]]: [[Heb 2:12|I will declare thy name to my brethren|Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis]]. And after the resurrection he says to Magdalen: [[John 20:17|go to my brethren and say to them|Vade, et dic fratribus meis]]. [[5:3|Shall be converted to the children of Israel|Convertentur ad filios Israel]], that is, to the faith of the twelve Patriarchs, who were the sons of Jacob, called by another name Israel. For the Jews, converted by the teaching and signs of the Apostles, believed that to have been done by Jesus which the Patriarchs believed was to be done by Christ. Or, the children of Israel are the Apostles, the sons of Christ, who is the truest Israelite, since he always saw God, not darkly by faith but clearly by sight [*Israel* was commonly interpreted “a man seeing God”]. And to the faith and way of life of these children of Israel were converted those thousands of Jews of whom it is written in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 4:4||]]. It can also be taken of the Jews who will be converted at the end of the world through the preaching of Elias, who [[Mal 4:6|shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers|convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres]]. For by converting the Jews then living to the faith and charity of Christ, he will make them of one mind and in concord with the Patriarchs and the other Saints who were under the law. And so the hearts of the children will be turned to the fathers, and the hearts of the fathers to the children.

paras.t: Et stabit ipse Christus, qui secundum deitatem stabilis invariabilisque consistit. Secundum humanitatem quoque Verbo unitam, stetit confirmatus in bono et omni virtute immobilis ac perfectus ; corporaliter etiam stetit turbas docendo, ut dicit Lucas et Joannes. Et pascet scientia et doctrina, exemplari vita, et aliis modis, in fortitudine Domini, id est in potentia totius superbenedictæ Trinitatis, in sublimitate nominis Domini Dei sui, id est in majestate Dei Patris, vel Trinitatis. Pater enim, seu quælibet divina Persona, est Deus Christi secundum naturam assumptam. Secundum quod ait : Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, Deum meum et Deum vestrum. Et Apostolus ait : Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Vel per sublimitatem nominis Dei, intelliguntur miracula illa altissima, quæ alius nemo fecit, nisi Christus : de quibus fatetur, Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater, testimonium perhibent de me. Sic itaque Christus pavit Judæos per se ipsum, deinde per Apostolos, per quos et gentiles pavit sive convertit. Unde scriptum est : Omnes mirabantur in verbis gratiæ quæ procedebant de ore ejus. Erat enim docens sicut potestatem habens, non sicut Scribæ et Pharisæi. Hinc loquitur Isaias : Sicut pastor gregem suum pascet, in brachio suo congregabit agnos, et in sinu suo levabit. Ipse nempe est pastor bonus, qui proprias oves vocat nominatim, et ante eas vadit ; dicitque, Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos ; et rursus, Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, et bibat.
paras.en: [[5:4|And he shall stand|Et stabit]], Christ himself, who according to his godhead stands firm and unchanging. According to the manhood united to the Word, too, he stood confirmed in good, immovable and perfect in every virtue; in body also he stood teaching the crowds, as Luke and John say[[Luke 6:17||]][[John 7:37||]]. [[5:4|And feed|Et pascet]] by knowledge and teaching, by the example of his life, and in other ways, [[5:4|in the strength of the Lord|in fortitudine Domini]], that is, in the power of the whole superblessed Trinity, [[5:4|in the height of the name of the Lord, his God|in sublimitate nominis Domini Dei sui]], that is, in the majesty of God the Father, or of the Trinity. For the Father, or any divine Person, is the God of Christ according to the nature assumed. According to which he says: [[John 20:17|I ascend to my Father and to your Father, to my God and to your God|Ascendo ad Patrem meum et Patrem vestrum, Deum meum et Deum vestrum]]. And the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 1:3|The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. Or by the height of the name of God are understood those most lofty miracles which no one else did but Christ, of which he declares: [[John 5:36|The works which the Father hath given me|Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater]] [[John 5:36|give testimony of me|testimonium perhibent de me]]. Thus Christ fed the Jews by himself, and then by the Apostles, by whom he also fed, or converted, the Gentiles. Hence it is written: All [[Luke 4:22|wondered at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth|mirabantur in verbis gratiæ quæ procedebant de ore ejus]]. [[Matt 7:29|For he was teaching them as one having power, and not as the scribes and Pharisees.|Erat enim docens sicut potestatem habens, non sicut Scribæ et Pharisæi]] Hence Isaias says: [[Is 40:11|He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather together the lambs with his arm, and shall take them up in his bosom|Sicut pastor gregem suum pascet, in brachio suo congregabit agnos, et in sinu suo levabit]]. For he is [[John 10:11|the good shepherd|pastor bonus]], who [[John 10:3|calleth his own sheep by name|proprias oves vocat nominatim]], and [[John 10:4|goeth before them|ante eas vadit]]; and he says: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you.|Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]] And again: [[John 7:37|If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink|Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, et bibat]].

paras.t: Et convertentur ad Christum gentiles : quemadmodum apud Danielem legitur, Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei; et in Psalmo, Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ; quia nunc magnificabitur usque ad terminos terræ : id est, Christus per totum mundum cognoscetur, et excellentia ejus omnibus innotescet ; sicque in cordibus credentium exaltabitur, atque ab eis magnifice honorabitur. Pro hac magnificatione Christus oravit, dicens : Pater, venit hora; clarifica Filium tuum. De hoc multa dicuntur in libro Psalmorum, ut est illud, Dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ ; et, Adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium ; et, Dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terrarum. Unde et Isaias inducit : A finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi.
paras.en: [[5:4|And they shall be converted|Et convertentur]] to Christ, namely the Gentiles: as is read in Daniel, [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 21:28|All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord|Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ]]; [[5:4|for now shall he be magnified even to the ends of the earth|quia nunc magnificabitur usque ad terminos terræ]]: that is, Christ will be known throughout the whole world, and his excellence will become known to all; and so he will be exalted in the hearts of believers, and magnificently honoured by them. For this magnifying Christ prayed, saying: Father, [[John 17:1|the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|venit hora; clarifica Filium tuum]]. Of this many things are said in the book of Psalms, as is that: [[Ps 2:8|I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession|Dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ]]; and: [[Ps 21:28|And all the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore in his sight|Adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium]]; and: [[Ps 71:8|And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.|Dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terrarum]] Hence Isaias too brings in: [[Is 24:16|From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one|A finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi]].

paras.t: Quæ autem sequuntur, intricata sunt valde, et difficultatibus plena. Et erit iste, scilicet Christus, pax, id est reconciliator et protector noster, et pacis internæ seu veræ quietis causa. De quo dicit Apostolus : Ipse est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum. Assyrius quum venerit in terram nostram, et quando calcaverit in domibus nostris. Locus iste usque ad illud, Et erunt reliquiæ Jacob, diversimode explanatur.
paras.en: What follows, however, is very involved and full of difficulties. [[5:5|And this man shall be|Et erit iste]], namely Christ, [[5:5|our peace|pax]], that is, our reconciler and protector, and the cause of inward peace, or true rest. Of whom the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:14|He is our peace, who hath made both one|Ipse est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]]. [[5:5|When the Assyrian shall come into our land, and when he shall set his foot in our houses|Assyrius quum venerit in terram nostram, et quando calcaverit in domibus nostris]]. This passage, as far as [[5:7|And the remnant of Jacob shall be|Et erunt reliquiæ Jacob]], is explained in different ways.

paras.t: Hieronymus namque, Beda et Glossa exponunt sic : Quum Assyrius, id est diabolus arguens et in perditionem dirigens (Assyrius enim dirigens seu arguens interpretatur), venerit in terram nostram, id est in carnem, illam tentando, inflammando, seu tribulando : quemadmodum Paulo datus fuit stimulus carnis, angelus Satanæ: qui percussit Job ulcere pessimo, a planta usque ad verticem; et quando calcaverit in domibus nostris, id est corporibus, quæ sunt animarum nostrarum domus seu habitacula : quæ calcat diabolus, subjiciendo ea malis pœnæ aut culpæ, quando videlicet exhibemus membra nostra arma iniquitatis peccato. Vel domus nostræ, sunt congregationes fidelium, quæ a dæmonibus exercentur, sed Christo protegente, pacem victoriamque sortiuntur. Et suscitabimus super eum, id est adversus Assyrium seu diabolum, ego Pater et Filius et Spiritus, septem pastores, id est Patriarchas ac Sanctos veteris legis : in qua sabbatum seu septima dies celebris fuit, præsertim quum per septem (qui est numerus perfectionis) universitas designetur. Unde in Apocalypsi habetur : Et a septem spiritibus, qui in conspectu throni ejus sunt. Tobiæ quoque Raphael protestatur : Ego sum unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Deum. Et octo primates homines, id est Sanctos novi Testamenti, in quibus octo beatitudines commendantur. Et octavus dominicæ resurrectionis dies, secundum Bedam, celebriter agitur. Omnes isti contra diabolum pugnaverunt, et adhuc nobis contra illum pugnantibus auxiliantur.
paras.en: For Jerome, Bede and the Gloss explain it thus: [[5:5|When the Assyrian|Quum Assyrius]], that is, the devil, who accuses and directs into perdition (for *Assyrian* is interpreted “directing” or “accusing”), [[5:5|shall come into our land|venerit in terram nostram]], that is, into the flesh, tempting, inflaming or afflicting it: as Paul was given [[2 Cor 12:7|a sting of my flesh, an angel of Satan|stimulus carnis, angelus Satanæ]], he who [[Job 2:7|struck Job with a very grievous ulcer, from the sole of the foot even to the top of his head|percussit Job ulcere pessimo, a planta usque ad verticem]]; [[5:5|and when he shall set his foot in our houses|et quando calcaverit in domibus nostris]], that is, in our bodies, which are the houses or dwellings of our souls: these the devil treads upon, subjecting them to the evils of punishment or of guilt, when, that is, we yield our members [[Rom 6:13|as instruments of iniquity unto sin|arma iniquitatis peccato]]. Or our houses are the congregations of the faithful, which are harassed by the demons, but, with Christ protecting them, obtain peace and victory. [[5:5|And we shall raise against him|Et suscitabimus super eum]], that is, against the Assyrian or devil, I, the Father, and the Son, and the Spirit, [[5:5|seven shepherds|septem pastores]], that is, the Patriarchs and Saints of the old law, in which the sabbath, or seventh day, was solemnly kept; above all since by seven (which is the number of perfection) the whole is signified. Hence it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:4|And from the seven spirits which are before his throne|Et a septem spiritibus, qui in conspectu throni ejus sunt]]. In Tobias too Raphael declares: I am [[Tob 12:15|one of the seven, who stand before the Lord|unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Deum]]. [[5:5|And eight principal men|Et octo primates homines]], that is, the Saints of the new Testament, in whom the eight beatitudes are commended. And the eighth day, that of the Lord's resurrection, is solemnly kept, according to Bede. All these fought against the devil, and still help us as we fight against him.

paras.t: Propter quod subditur : Et pascent terram Assur, id est regnum diaboli, seu dæmones tentatores, in gladio oris sui, seu verbi Dei (quoniam teste Apostolo, gladius spiritus est verbum Dei), hoc est, virtute orationis vel prædicationis; dæmonum potestatem dejicient. Et terram Nemrod. Qui per Assur, ille et per Nemrod designatur, videlicet dæmon, qui ut fulgur ruit de cœlo, et animarum robustus venator est : quemadmodum Nemrod, qui interpretatur tentatio descendens, fuit fortis venator coram Domino. Hujus itaque terram pascent in lanceis suis, id est verbis acutissimis et penetrativis. Vivus est enim sermo Dei et efficax, et penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti. Vel lanceæ sunt virtutes seu spiritualia arma, quibus perforatur diabolus. Et liberabit Christus ab Assur, id est tentatione diaboli, quum venerit diabolus in terram nostram : secundum sensum nunc positum (animam autem intrare non potest); et quum calcaverit in terminis nostris, id est, Ecclesiam impugnaverit.
paras.en: Hence it is added: [[5:6|And they shall feed the land of Assyria|Et pascent terram Assur]], that is, the kingdom of the devil, or the tempting demons, [[5:6|with the sword|in gladio]] of their mouth [Denis's text adds *oris sui*, “of their mouth”], or of the word of God (since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[Eph 6:17|the sword of the Spirit|gladius spiritus]] is [[Eph 6:17|the word of God|verbum Dei]]), that is, by the power of prayer or of preaching: they will cast down the power of the demons. [[5:6|And the land of Nemrod|Et terram Nemrod]]. He who is signified by Assur is signified by Nemrod too, namely the demon, who [[Luke 10:18|like lightning|ut fulgur]] fell [[Luke 10:18|from heaven|de cœlo]], and is a mighty hunter of souls: as Nemrod, which is interpreted *temptation descending*, [[Gen 10:9|was a stout hunter before the Lord|fuit fortis venator coram Domino]]. His land, then, they shall feed [[5:6|with the spears thereof|in lanceis suis]] [Denis reads *suis*, “their”; a note in the edition gives *ejus*, “thereof”, the Vulgate's word], that is, with most sharp and piercing words. [[Heb 4:12|For the word of God is living and effectual and more piercing than any two edged sword|Vivus est enim sermo Dei et efficax, et penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti]]. Or the spears are the virtues or spiritual arms by which the devil is pierced through. [[5:6|And he shall deliver us|Et liberabit]], namely Christ, [[5:6|from the Assyrian|ab Assur]], that is, from the temptation of the devil, [[5:6|when he shall come into our land|quum venerit diabolus in terram nostram]] (the devil, that is), according to the sense now given (for the soul he cannot enter); [[5:6|and when he shall tread in our borders|et quum calcaverit in terminis nostris]], that is, shall attack the Church.

paras.t: Verum expositio ista videtur ad mysticum confugere intellectum. Unde alii litteralius ita exponunt : Et erit iste Christus pax nostra, quum, id est postquam, Assyrius, id est rex et exercitus Assyriorum, venerit in terram nostram, et quando calcaverit, id est, postquam incesserit, in domibus nostris. Tempore enim Ezechiæ, Assyrii civitates, vicos et castella Judææ ingressi sunt, et suæ voluntati ad tempus subjecerunt. Et suscitabimus, nos Deus Trinitas, qui alibi diximus : Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram; vel, nos Prophetæ, suscitando annuntiabimus; super eum, id est contra regnum Assyriorum, septem pastores, id est septem duces Medorum atque Persarum, de quorum consilio cuncta egerunt reges illorum, ut legitur in libro Esther : illi enim septem videbant faciem regis, et primi post eum sedebant. Qui Deo movente, Cyro ac Dario dederunt consilium invadendi regnum Chaldæorum ac Assyriorum, quorum regnum tunc subditum erat Chaldæis. Et octo primates homines, id est directores bellatorum : erantque in exercitu Persarum ac Medorum marescalli; et impugnaverunt Assyrios.
paras.en: But this explanation seems to take refuge in the mystical sense. Hence others explain it more literally thus: [[5:5|And this man shall be|Et erit iste]], Christ, [[5:5|our peace|pax nostra]], [[5:5|when|quum]], that is, after, [[5:5|the Assyrian|Assyrius]], that is, the king and army of the Assyrians, [[5:5|shall come into our land, and when he shall set his foot|venerit in terram nostram, et quando calcaverit]], that is, after he has marched, [[5:5|in our houses|in domibus nostris]]. For in the time of Ezechias the Assyrians entered the cities, villages and castles of Judea[[4 Kings 18:13||]], and for a time subjected them to their will. [[5:5|And we shall raise|Et suscitabimus]]: we, God the Trinity, who said elsewhere: [[Gen 1:26|Let us make man to our image and likeness|Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram]]; or, we Prophets, shall raise up by announcing it; [[5:5|against him|super eum]], that is, against the kingdom of the Assyrians, [[5:5|seven shepherds|septem pastores]], that is, the seven chiefs of the Medes and Persians, by whose counsel their kings did all things[[Esth 1:13||]], as is read in the book of Esther: for they were the seven [[Esth 1:14|who saw the face of the king, and were used to sit first after him|videbant faciem regis, et primi post eum sedebant]]. These, at God's prompting, gave Cyrus and Darius the counsel to invade the kingdom of the Chaldeans and of the Assyrians, whose kingdom was then subject to the Chaldeans. [[5:5|And eight principal men|Et octo primates homines]], that is, leaders of the warriors: for there were marshals in the army of the Persians and Medes; and they attacked the Assyrians.

paras.t: Et pascent terram Assur in gladio, id est, Assyrios gladio devorabunt, et terram Nemrod, id est Babylonem et Chaldæam, in qua Nemrod primo regnavit, juxta illud Genesis : Fuit autem principium regni ejus Babylon, et Arach, et Achad, et Chalanne in terra Sennaar; in lanceis ejus, occidendo Chaldæos. Et liberabit Christus Judæos ab Assur, quum venerit in terram nostram, id est, postquam Assyrii Judæam introierunt, et quum calcaverit in terminis nostris, mittendo nuntios usque Jerusalem, scilicet Rabsacen et alios multos. Siquidem post illud tempus destructum fuit regnum Assyriorum : sicque impediti erant reverti in terram Judææ.
paras.en: [[5:6|And they shall feed the land of Assyria with the sword|Et pascent terram Assur in gladio]], that is, they shall devour the Assyrians with the sword, [[5:6|and the land of Nemrod|et terram Nemrod]], that is, Babylon and Chaldea, in which Nemrod first reigned, according to that of Genesis: [[Gen 10:10|And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, and Arach, and Achad, and Chalanne in the land of Sennaar|Fuit autem principium regni ejus Babylon, et Arach, et Achad, et Chalanne in terra Sennaar]]; [[5:6|with the spears thereof|in lanceis ejus]], by slaying the Chaldeans. [[5:6|And he shall deliver|Et liberabit]], namely Christ, the Jews [[5:6|from the Assyrian|ab Assur]], [[5:6|when he shall come into our land|quum venerit in terram nostram]], that is, after the Assyrians had entered Judea, [[5:6|and when he shall tread in our borders|et quum calcaverit in terminis nostris]], by sending messengers as far as Jerusalem, namely Rabsaces and many others. For after that time the kingdom of the Assyrians was destroyed, and so they were prevented from returning into the land of Judea.

paras.t: Et erunt reliquiæ Jacob, id est electi Judæi in Christum credentes, puta Apostoli, discipulique eorum ex Judaismo conversi, in medio populorum multorum, id est inter diversas gentium nationes : sicut Joannes in Asia, Thomas in India, Bartholomæus in Armenia; quasi ros a Domino, id est, corda gentilium semine verbi cœlestis irrigantes et fecundantes, atque libidinis ignem vitiorumque flammam in eis infrigidantes aut exstirpantes; et quasi stillæ, id est guttæ aquarum, super herbam quæ non exspectat virum, id est, humano auxilio non irrigatur, et non præstolatur filios hominum, ut illorum studio crescat sive fructificet, sed divina providentia hoc totum agitur. Homo enim non potest unum capillum facere album et nigrum. Et quamvis materiam præbet, et activa passivaque applicet, Dei tamen est incrementum præstare, et fructum concedere.
paras.en: [[5:7|And the remnant of Jacob shall be|Et erunt reliquiæ Jacob]], that is, the elect Jews who believe in Christ, for instance the Apostles and their disciples converted from Judaism, [[5:7|in the midst of many peoples|in medio populorum multorum]], that is, among the different nations of the Gentiles: as John in Asia, Thomas in India, Bartholomew in Armenia; [[5:7|as a dew from the Lord|quasi ros a Domino]], that is, watering and making fruitful the hearts of the Gentiles with the seed of the heavenly word, and cooling or rooting out in them the fire of lust and the flame of vices; [[5:7|and as drops|et quasi stillæ]], that is, drops of water, [[5:7|upon the grass, which waiteth not for man|super herbam quæ non exspectat virum]], that is, it is not watered by human help, [[5:7|nor tarrieth for the children of men|et non præstolatur filios hominum]], that it may grow or bear fruit by their effort; but all this is done by divine providence. For man cannot [[Matt 5:36|make one hair white or black|unum capillum facere album et nigrum]]. And although he supplies the matter, and brings the active and passive causes together, yet it is God's to give the increase and to grant the fruit.

paras.t: Et erunt reliquiæ Jacob in gentibus in medio populorum multorum, quibus evangelicam legem proponent, quasi leo in jumentis silvarum, et quasi catulus leonis in gregibus pecorum, id est fortes et insuperabiles, habentes potestatem ligandi atque solvendi : quibus et Christus promisit, Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere omnes adversarii vestri. Quemadmodum ergo leo fortior est jumentis quæ versantur in silva, et catulus leonis fortior pecoribus, quoniam prædam quam volunt, tollunt ac devorant; ita Apostoli, nullo potente impedire, prædam hominum ex ore diaboli rapuerunt, et Christo incorporaverunt. Qui leo quum transierit, quærens prædam, et conculcaverit bestiam, et ceperit eam, non est qui eruat de ore leonis, quum sit fortissimus bestiarum. Sic transeuntibus Apostolis de gente in gentem, et conculcantibus gentilitatem, Christo eam subdendo, et capientibus intra rete suum multitudinem gentium conversarum, nullus potuit conversos ab Apostolorum doctrina avertere. De hac reliquiarum Israel dispersione et fructificatione in gentibus, multa dicuntur in Isaia, scilicet: Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine; et illud, Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt.
paras.en: [[5:8|And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles, in the midst of many peoples|Et erunt reliquiæ Jacob in gentibus in medio populorum multorum]], to whom they shall set forth the law of the Gospel, [[5:8|as a lion among the beasts of the forests, and as a young lion among the flocks of sheep|quasi leo in jumentis silvarum, et quasi catulus leonis in gregibus pecorum]], that is, strong and unconquerable, having the power of binding and loosing[[Matt 18:18||]]: to whom Christ also promised: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere omnes adversarii vestri]]. As, then, the lion is stronger than the beasts that dwell in the forest, and the young lion stronger than the flocks, since they carry off and devour what prey they will; so the Apostles, with none able to hinder them, snatched a prey of men from the mouth of the devil, and incorporated them into Christ. [[5:8|Who|Qui]] (the lion) [[5:8|when he shall go through|quum transierit]], seeking prey, [[5:8|and tread down|et conculcaverit]] the beast, [[5:8|and take|et ceperit eam]] it, [[5:8|there is none to deliver|non est qui eruat]] it from the mouth of the lion, since he is the strongest of beasts. So, as the Apostles passed from nation to nation, and trod down the Gentile world, subjecting it to Christ, and took within their net a multitude of converted Gentiles, no one could turn the converts away from the teaching of the Apostles. Of this dispersion and fruitfulness of the remnant of Israel among the Gentiles many things are said in Isaias, namely: [[Is 27:6|Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed|Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine]]; and that: [[Is 42:12|They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands.|Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt]]

paras.t: Et exaltabitur manus, id est potestas tua, o Christe, vel Ecclesia, super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui peribunt, id est, æternaliter damnabuntur. Invisibiles enim hostes subjecit Christus discipulis suis, dicendo : Infirmos curate, mortuos suscitate, dæmones ejicite; et, Dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit. Judæi quoque increduli et tyranni, persequentes olim Ecclesiam, perierunt. Rursus, postquam Romanum imperium fidem Christi suscepit, exaltata est manus Ecclesiæ, etiam in præsenti, supra æmulos suos. De quo Christo loquitur Isaias : Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei.
paras.en: [[5:9|Thy hand shall be lifted up|Et exaltabitur manus]], that is, thy power, O Christ, or O Church, [[5:9|over thy enemies|super hostes tuos]], [[5:9|and all thy enemies shall be cut off|et omnes inimici tui peribunt]] [Denis reads *peribunt*, “shall perish”, where the Vulgate has *interibunt*], that is, shall be damned eternally. For Christ subjected his invisible enemies to his disciples, saying: [[Matt 10:8|Heal the sick, raise the dead|Infirmos curate, mortuos suscitate]], [[Matt 10:8|cast out devils|dæmones ejicite]]; and: [[Luke 10:19|I have given you power to tread|Dedi vobis potestatem calcandi]] [[Luke 10:19|upon all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall hurt you|super omnem virtutem inimici, et nihil vobis nocebit]]. The unbelieving Jews too, and the tyrants who once persecuted the Church, perished. Again, after the Roman empire received the faith of Christ, the hand of the Church was lifted up, even in the present life, over her rivals. Of this Christ Isaias says: [[Is 45:25|They shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded|Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei]].

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, quum Apostoli prædicaverint ubique Evangelium Christi, dicit Dominus : Auferam equos tuos, o Synagoga, de medio tui, et disperdam quadrigas tuas; et perdam civitates terræ tuæ, et destruam omnes munitiones tuas, id est fortalitia, et auferam maleficia de manu tua. Videntur hæc accipi posse de destructione Judæorum a Romanis. Sed obstat quod subditur : Et divinationes non erunt in te; et perire faciam sculptilia tua, et statuas tuas de medio tui, et non adorabis ultra opera manuum tuarum; et evellam lucos tuos de medio tui, et conteram civitates tuas. Judæi enim pro tunc idola non colebant. Unde qui ista ad captivitatem prædictam cupit referre, dicere potest quod idola, statuæ et luci dicuntur Judæorum istorum, in quantum patres eorum ab antiquo talia coluerunt. Vel per idola, statuas et lucos, metaphorice intelliguntur bona creata caduca, quibus inordinatissime afficiebantur, et velut idola coluerunt, præponendo talia Deo, quemadmodum Apostolus nominat avaritiam idolorum culturam. Deus enim avari, est aurum; gulosi, venter; luxuriosi, venus. De hujuscemodi idolis ait Joannes : Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris. Hieronymus quoque exponit ista omnia satis spiritualiter, intelligendo per equos, motus lascivos; per quadrigas, vanitatis vehicula, quibus de peccato in peccatum deducimur; per civitates, congregationes iniquas; per munitiones, divitias sæculi, pompam mundi, eloquentiam frivolam; per maleficia, deceptiones et nocumenta; per divinationes, propriæ doctrinæ præsumptionem; per sculptilia autem et statuas, superstitiosa, vana, conficta et deceptoria documenta.
paras.en: [[5:10|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit in die illa]], when the Apostles have preached the Gospel of Christ everywhere, [[5:10|saith the Lord, that I will take away thy horses|dicit Dominus : Auferam equos tuos]], O Synagogue, [[5:10|out of the midst of thee, and will destroy thy chariots|de medio tui, et disperdam quadrigas tuas]]; [[5:11|and I will destroy the cities of thy land, and will throw down all thy strong holds|et perdam civitates terræ tuæ, et destruam omnes munitiones tuas]], that is, fortresses, [[5:11|and I will take away sorceries out of thy hand|et auferam maleficia de manu tua]]. These things seem able to be taken of the destruction of the Jews by the Romans. But against this stands what is added: [[5:11|And there shall be no divinations in thee|Et divinationes non erunt in te]]; [[5:12|and I will destroy thy graven things, and thy statues, out of the midst of thee: and thou shalt no more adore the works of thy hands|et perire faciam sculptilia tua, et statuas tuas de medio tui, et non adorabis ultra opera manuum tuarum]]; [[5:13|And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: and will crush thy cities.|et evellam lucos tuos de medio tui, et conteram civitates tuas]] For the Jews at that time did not worship idols. Hence one who wishes to refer these words to the captivity just mentioned may say that the idols, statues and groves are called those of these Jews inasmuch as their fathers of old worshipped such things. Or by idols, statues and groves are understood metaphorically the perishable created goods to which they were most inordinately attached, and which they worshipped as idols, setting such things before God; as the Apostle calls avarice the worship of idols[[Eph 5:5||]][[Col 3:5||]]. For the god of the avaricious man is gold; of the glutton, his belly; of the lustful, Venus. Of idols of this kind John says: [[1 John 5:21|Little children, keep yourselves from idols|Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris]]. Jerome too explains all these things in a quite spiritual way, understanding by the horses, wanton motions; by the chariots, the vehicles of vanity, by which we are carried from sin to sin; by the cities, wicked assemblies; by the strong holds, the riches of the world, the pomp of the world, frivolous eloquence; by the sorceries, deceptions and harms; by the divinations, presumption in one's own teaching; and by the graven things and statues, superstitious, vain, made-up and deceitful teachings.

paras.t: Et faciam in furore et indignatione mea, id est in rigorosa ac vindicativa æquitate mea, et in zelo justitiæ meæ vitia detestante, ultionem in omnibus gentibus quæ non audierunt, id est, doctrinam Apostolorum et fidem catholicam non receperunt, quoniam æternam pœnam habebunt. Punitio Dei in sæculo isto, quantum ad electos, quamvis dura appareat, est tamen medicinalis, nec ex furore, sed misericordia Dei infligitur, qui paternaliter corripit in præsenti, ne durius puniat in futuro. Punitio autem gehennæ, recte ex furore Dei infligi asseritur, non quod in Deo sit passionis affectio, sed propter similitudinem operis.
paras.en: [[5:14|And I will execute|Et faciam]] [[5:14|in wrath, and in indignation|in furore et indignatione mea]], that is, in my rigorous and avenging equity, and in the zeal of my justice which detests vices, [[5:14|vengeance|ultionem]] [[5:14|among all the nations that have not given ear|in omnibus gentibus quæ non audierunt]], that is, that have not received the teaching of the Apostles and the catholic faith; for they shall have eternal punishment. God's punishment in this world, as regards the elect, however hard it may appear, is nevertheless medicinal, and is inflicted not out of wrath but out of the mercy of God, who chastises like a father in the present so as not to punish more severely in the future. But the punishment of hell is rightly said to be inflicted out of the wrath of God: not that there is the affection of a passion in God, but because of the likeness of the work [that is, God's punishing is called wrath because it does what an angry man does, not because God feels anger].

paras.t: Postremo, ut refert Hieronymus, carneus Israel ita exponit præhabita, quod in adventu Messiæ, Assyrii et Chaldæi ac ceteræ nationes subjicientur Judæis, et ipsi Judæi, qui tunc fuerint inter gentes dispersi, benedicentur et confortabuntur a Deo, in tantum quod nemo eis resistere poterit. Sed sanguinarii erunt atque crudeles, occidendo eos inter quos oppressi fuerunt : sicque exaltabitur manus eorum super adversarios. Verum, ut probat Hieronymus, huic eorum vanissimæ expositioni repugnat quod subditur, nuncque expositum est, scilicet : In die illa, dicit Dominus, auferam equos tuos de medio tui, etc. Quomodo enim tunc auferentur ab eis idola et statuæ ac luci, quum in omni captivitate ista idololatriam vehementissime detestentur? Quomodo etiam tunc urbes eorum destruentur, quum in terra habitent aliorum? Et utique si ordo textus rite pensetur, innotescet quam tenebrosus sit error illorum.
paras.en: Lastly, as Jerome relates, Israel according to the flesh explains what has gone before thus: that at the coming of the Messias the Assyrians and Chaldeans and the other nations will be subjected to the Jews, and the Jews themselves who are then scattered among the Gentiles will be blessed and strengthened by God, so much that no one will be able to resist them. But they will be bloodthirsty and cruel, slaying those among whom they were oppressed: and so their hand will be lifted up over their adversaries. But, as Jerome proves, against this most empty explanation of theirs stands what follows, and has now been explained, namely: [[5:10|in that day, saith the Lord, that I will take away thy horses out of the midst of thee|In die illa, dicit Dominus, auferam equos tuos de medio tui]], etc. For how will idols and statues and groves be taken from them then, when in all this captivity they most vehemently detest idolatry? And how will their cities then be destroyed, when they dwell in the land of others? And indeed, if the order of the text is rightly weighed, it will be plain how dark their error is.

paras.t: Mystice, quod in principio hujus capituli dictum est, Nunc vastaberis, filia latronis, intelligi potest de ecclesia malignantium, quæ quum sit Deo rebellis, obsidionem ponit quodammodo contra eum. Et dum Christo tantam contumeliam facit, ejusque contemnit vicarios, quasi in virga percutit maxillam judicis Israel, scilicet Christi seu ejus vicarii. Omnis quoque bonus diligensque prælatus, prædicator seu doctor, stare debet in via perfectionis et firmitate virtutis, et pascere audientes vel subditos verbo, vita, ac precibus, in fortitudine Domini, non propriis viribus, sed adjutorio Dei totaliter, jugiter, atque humiliter innitendo, nec a cœpto opere bono ignaviter desistendo.
paras.en: Mystically, what was said at the beginning of this chapter, [[5:1|Now shalt thou be laid waste, O daughter of the robber|Nunc vastaberis, filia latronis]], may be understood of the church of the malignant, which, since it is rebellious against God, in a manner lays siege against him. And while it does Christ such great insult and despises his vicars, it strikes as it were [[5:1|with a rod|in virga]] [[5:1|the cheek of the judge of Israel|maxillam judicis Israel]], namely of Christ or of his vicar. Every good and diligent prelate too, preacher or teacher, ought to stand in the way of perfection and in firmness of virtue, and to feed his hearers or subjects by word, by life and by prayers, [[5:4|in the strength of the Lord|in fortitudine Domini]], not by his own powers, but leaning wholly, constantly and humbly on the help of God, and not slothfully giving up a good work once begun.

6.title: Elucidatio capituli sexti: Audite quæ Dominus loquitur.
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Hear ye what the Lord saith.

paras.t: OSTENDITUR demum præsenti capitulo multiplex Israeliticæ plebis ingratitudo, multiformis quoque beneficentia Dei ad populum, quatenus opposita juxta se posita, clarius innotescant.
paras.en: Lastly, the present chapter shows the manifold ingratitude of the Israelite people, and also the manifold beneficence of God towards the people, so that the opposites, set side by side, may be the more clearly seen.

paras.t: Ait ergo sanctus Michæas : Audite quæ Dominus loquitur ad me per angelum, per me quoque ad populum. Beati enim qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud. Surge tu, Michæa, a quiete ad actum, ab interioribus ad exteriora ; contende judicio adversus montes, id est, contra sacerdotes et Scribas seu principes disputa et conquire, ut veritas pateat ; et audiant colles, id est, qui inferioris gradus, potestatis, seu ordinis sunt, vocem tuam, id est verba quibus probabis beneficentiam Dei, et ingratitudinem populi. Audiant montes jam dicti judicium Domini, id est sententiam justæ increpationis contra eos, et quid de eis sentiat Deus, et fortia fundamenta terræ, id est Pharisæi, et qui aliis religiosiores videntur, atque columnæ aliorum dicuntur, sustentando eos per gratiam sibi concessam, quemadmodum ait Apostolus : Debemus nos firmiores, imbecillitatem aliorum portare, et non nobis placere.
paras.en: So holy Micheas says: [[6:1|Hear ye what the Lord saith|Audite quæ Dominus loquitur]] to me through an angel, and through me to the people. For [[Luke 11:28|blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it|Beati enim qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud]]. [[6:1|Arise|Surge]] thou, Micheas, from rest to action, from inward things to outward; [[6:1|contend thou in judgment against the mountains|contende judicio adversus montes]], that is, dispute and contend against the priests and Scribes or princes, that the truth may be laid open; [[6:1|and let the hills hear|et audiant colles]], that is, those who are of lower rank, power or order, [[6:1|thy voice|vocem tuam]], that is, the words by which thou shalt prove the beneficence of God and the ingratitude of the people. [[6:2|Let the mountains hear|Audiant montes]] already spoken of [[6:2|the judgment of the Lord|judicium Domini]], that is, the sentence of just rebuke against them, and what God thinks of them, [[6:2|and the strong foundations of the earth|et fortia fundamenta terræ]], that is, the Pharisees and those who seem more religious than others and are called the pillars of others[[Gal 2:9||]], since they bear them up by the grace granted to them, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 15:1|we that are stronger ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not to please ourselves|Debemus nos firmiores, imbecillitatem aliorum portare, et non nobis placere]] [Denis's wording is "we that are stronger ought to bear the weakness of others, and not to please ourselves"].

paras.t: Quia judicium Domini cum populo suo, id est, rationabilem discussionem et justam declarationem vult facere Deus cum populo Judæorum, probando per exhibitionem beneficiorum suorum, ingratitudinem atque malitiam populi, ne videatur per potentiam eos opprimere, sed omnibus elucescat quam juste illi damnentur. Unde dictum est in Osee : Judicium Domino cum habitatoribus terræ. Et cum Israel dijudicabitur, id est, justus esse probabitur, justusque ab omnibus agnoscetur, qui audierint contentionem Dei contra Israeliticam plebem, videlicet declarationem beneficiorum divinorum et maleficiorum populi ejus. Sic quoque loquitur per Ezechielem : Judicabor vobiscum facie ad faciem. Et Psalmista : Justificeris, inquit, in sermonibus tuis et vincas quum judicaris. Et in Isaia : Judicate inter me et vineam meam. Per rationem ergo, non per potestatem dumtaxat, vult Dominus prævalere ; datque licentiam disputandi adversus se, secundum quod alibi loquitur : Narra, si quid habes, ut justificeris.
paras.en: [[6:2|for the Lord will enter into judgment with his people|Quia judicium Domini cum populo suo]]: that is, God wills to make a reasoned examination and a just declaration with the people of the Jews, proving the ingratitude and malice of the people by setting forth his benefits, lest he seem to crush them by might, and so that it may shine out to all how justly they are condemned. Hence it is said in Osee: [[Osee 4:1|the Lord shall enter into judgment with the inhabitants of the land|Judicium Domino cum habitatoribus terræ]]. [[6:2|and he will plead against Israel|Et cum Israel dijudicabitur]] [*dijudicabitur*, literally "he will be judged"], that is, he will be proved just, and will be acknowledged as just by all who hear God's contention against the Israelite people, namely the declaration of the divine benefits and of the misdeeds of his people. So too he speaks through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 20:35|there will I plead with you face to face|Judicabor vobiscum facie ad faciem]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 50:6|that thou mayst be justified|Justificeris]], he says, [[Ps 50:6|in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged|in sermonibus tuis et vincas quum judicaris]] [the margin gives Ps. l, 5; the words are in Ps 50:6]. And in Isaias: [[Is 5:3|judge between me and my vineyard|Judicate inter me et vineam meam]]. It is by reason, then, and not by power alone, that the Lord wills to prevail; and he gives leave to dispute against him, as he says elsewhere: [[Is 43:26|tell if thou hast any thing to justify thyself|Narra, si quid habes, ut justificeris]].

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur ratio Dei contra ingratos, videlicet commemoratio beneficiorum ipsius. Popule meus, id est, gens Judæorum, quam præ ceteris elegi, multisque beneficiis decoravi. Isti tamen ingrati, non fuerunt populus Dei per prædestinationem finalisque gratiæ electionem secundum veritatem. Sed nominati sunt populus Dei, propter patres, et propter gratiam quam Deus præbuit eis, quamvis abjecerint illam. Simili modo vocantur filii regni, Christo dicente : Filii regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores. Quid feci tibi ? id est, quid forefeci ? quid mali intuli ? quid feci quod facere non debui ? Aut quid molestus fui tibi, inordinate seu contra justitiam ? Responde mihi ad hæc. Non enim fuit eis Deus molestus, irrationabiliter aggravando, quamvis contra perversam impiorum voluntatem aliqua faciat, quibus gravantur. Hinc Dominus per Isaiam testatur : Quid debui ultra facere vineæ meæ, et non feci ? Et in Deuteronomio asserit Moyses huic plebi : Portavit te Dominus Deus tuus, sicut portare solet homo parvulum filium suum. Denique quod tibi molestus non fui, hinc liquet : Quia eduxi te de terra Ægypti, et liberavi te de domo servientium, id est de Ægypto et habitaculo ejus, ubi durissima servitute luti ac lateris premebaris, et Pharaoni urbes tabernaculorum ædificabas ; et misi ante faciem tuam Moysen ducem, doctorem, seu legislatorem, et amicum meum, et Aaron fratrem ejus pontificem, et Mariam sororem illorum, prophetissam, quæ specialiter præerat feminis.
paras.en: Next is set down God's case against the ungrateful, namely the recalling of his benefits. [[6:3|O my people|Popule meus]], that is, nation of the Jews, which I chose before the rest and adorned with many benefits. Yet these ungrateful men were not in truth the people of God by predestination and the election of final grace. But they were named the people of God for the sake of the fathers, and because of the grace which God gave them, though they cast it away. In like manner they are called children of the kingdom, as Christ says: [[Matt 8:12|the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into the exterior darkness|Filii regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores]]. [[6:3|what have I done to thee|Quid feci tibi]]? that is, what wrong have I done? what evil have I brought on thee? what have I done that I ought not to have done? [[6:3|or in what have I molested thee|Aut quid molestus fui tibi]], unduly or against justice? [[6:3|answer thou me|Responde mihi]] on these things. For God was not burdensome to them by oppressing them without reason, although he does some things against the perverse will of the wicked by which they are burdened. Hence the Lord testifies through Isaias: [[Is 5:4|What is there that I ought to do more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it?|Quid debui ultra facere vineæ meæ, et non feci]] And in Deuteronomy Moses declares to this people: [[Deut 1:31|the Lord thy God hath carried thee, as a man is wont to carry his little son|Portavit te Dominus Deus tuus, sicut portare solet homo parvulum filium suum]]. Lastly, that I have not been burdensome to thee is plain from this: [[6:4|For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt|Quia eduxi te de terra Ægypti]], [[6:4|and delivered thee out of the house of slaves|et liberavi te de domo servientium]], that is, from Egypt and its dwelling-place, where thou wast weighed down by the hardest bondage of clay and brick[[Ex 1:14||]], and didst build cities of tabernacles for Pharao[[Ex 1:11||]]; [[6:4|and I sent before thy face Moses|et misi ante faciem tuam Moysen]], as leader, teacher or lawgiver, and my friend, [[6:4|and Aaron|et Aaron]] his brother, as high priest, [[6:4|and Mary|et Mariam]] their sister, a prophetess, who had charge of the women in particular.

paras.t: Popule meus, memento, quæso : qui præcipere possum, sed dulciter loquor, ut te ad veritatis recognitionem inducam : quid cogitaverit contra te Balac rex Moab, qui cogitavit te abigere, dejicere, et per fraudulenta consilia Balaam seu maledictionem illius occidere ; et quid responderit ei Balaam filius Beor. Multa enim bona dixit de populo Israel, et beneficia Dei præstita ei commemoravit. In quo patet, quanta bona fecit Dominus Israeli. Denique tribus vicibus quasi invitus benedixit Judæis, inter cetera dicens : Ad benedicendum adductus sum ; benedictionem prohibere non valeo. Dominus Deus ejus cum illo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo. Dominus Deus eduxit illum de Ægypto, cujus fortitudo est sicut rhinocerotis. De Setim usque ad Galgalam, id est, Balaam lustrans oculis exercitum Israel, qui protendebatur a loco qui dicitur Setim, usque ad Jordanem, juxta quem, ex opposito tamen, est Galgala. Est autem Setim locus in eremo plenus arboribus, ubi filii Israel peccaverunt cum filiabus Madian et idolo Phogor. Hieronymus tamen dicit, quod Balac congregavit ibi exercitum contra filios Israel : quod intelligi potest, quia circa hunc locum hoc fecit. In Numerorum enim libro aperte habetur, quod Israel morabatur eo tempore in Setim ; et paulo ante asseritur, quod Balac duxit Balaam in verticem montis Phogor. Vel iste est sensus, secundum Hebræos : Memento, etc., ut dictum est, de Setim usque ad Galgalam, id est mea beneficia tibi impensa, et tua iniqua opera contra me facta, ab eo tempore quo patres tui peccaverunt in Setim, usque ad tempus quo Saul unctus est in Galgala. Hæc autem recordari te quæso, et prædicto jam modo te per Balaam benedixi, ut cognosceres justitiam Domini, id est, quam juste increperis a Deo ; vel fidelitatem Dei in adimplendo promissa, qui tibi misericorditer fecit et vere implevit, sicut sanctissimis patriarchis Abraham, Isaac et Jacob spopondit.
paras.en: [[6:5|O my people, remember, I pray thee|Popule meus, memento, quæso]]: I who could command, yet speak gently, that I may lead thee to acknowledge the truth: [[6:5|what Balach, the king of Moab, purposed|quid cogitaverit contra te Balac rex Moab]] against thee, he who purposed to drive thee off, to cast thee down, and to destroy thee through the crafty counsels of Balaam or through his curse[[Num 22:6||]] [the margin gives Num. xxii–xxiv, the whole story]; [[6:5|and what Balaam, the son of Beor, answered him|et quid responderit ei Balaam filius Beor]]. For he said many good things of the people of Israel, and recounted the benefits God had bestowed on them. In this it is plain how great were the good things the Lord did for Israel. In fact, three times, as though against his will, he blessed the Jews, saying among other things: [[Num 23:20|I was brought to bless, the blessing I am not able to hinder.|Ad benedicendum adductus sum ; benedictionem prohibere non valeo]] [[Num 23:21|The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king in him|Dominus Deus ejus cum illo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo]]. [[Num 23:22|God hath brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like to the rhinoceros.|Dominus Deus eduxit illum de Ægypto, cujus fortitudo est sicut rhinocerotis]] [[6:5|from Setim to Galgal|De Setim usque ad Galgalam]]: that is, Balaam surveying with his eyes the army of Israel, which stretched from the place called Setim as far as the Jordan, beside which, though on the opposite side, is Galgal. Now Setim is a place in the desert full of trees, where the children of Israel sinned with the daughters of Madian and with the idol Phogor[[Num 25:1||]][[Num 25:3||]] [Num 25:1 has "the daughters of Moab"; the Madianite woman comes at 25:6]. Jerome, however, says that Balach gathered an army there against the children of Israel: which can be understood in the sense that he did this near that place. For in the book of Numbers it is plainly stated that [[Num 25:1|Israel at that time abode in Settim|Israel morabatur eo tempore in Setim]]; and a little before it is said that Balach brought Balaam to the top of mount Phogor[[Num 23:28||]]. Or this is the sense, according to the Hebrews: [[6:5|remember|Memento]], etc., as was said, [[6:5|from Setim to Galgal|de Setim usque ad Galgalam]]: that is, my benefits bestowed on thee and thy wicked works done against me, from the time when thy fathers sinned in Setim until the time when Saul was anointed in Galgal[[1 Kings 10:1||]][[1 Kings 11:15||]] [the margin gives II Reg. x, 1; xi, 15, that is 1 Kings (1 Samuel): Saul is anointed at 10:1 and made king in Galgal at 11:15]. These things I pray thee to remember; and in the way already said I blessed thee through Balaam, [[6:5|that thou mightest know the justice of the Lord|ut cognosceres justitiam Domini]]: that is, how justly thou art rebuked by God; or the faithfulness of God in fulfilling his promises, who mercifully did for thee and truly fulfilled what he had pledged to the most holy patriarchs Abraham[[Gen 22:17||]][[Gen 22:18||]], Isaac[[Gen 26:24||]] and Jacob[[Gen 28:13||]][[Gen 28:14||]][[Gen 28:15||]].

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta in persona plebis ad ista respondet : Quid dignum offeram Domino ? tanquam dicat : Attendo præhabita, et de cetero gratus esse desidero ; sed quid dignum offeram Deo æterno ? Curvabo genu Deo excelso ? Hoc dupliciter legitur. Primo negative, ut sit sensus : Genuflexio per se non est idonea Deum placare, quum non sit in se nisi indicium devotionis. Et oratio sine conversatione bona, non est condigna. Qui enim declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis. Secundo legitur affirmative, ut sit responsio ad verbum præcedens ; eritque sensus, quod genuflexio, oratio seu adoratio, in quantum sunt actus latriæ, et ex vera devotione procedunt, sunt digna oblatio atque placatio Dei, juxta illud in Psalmo : Immola Deo sacrificium laudis.
paras.en: Next the Prophet, in the person of the people, answers these things: [[6:6|What shall I offer to the Lord that is worthy?|Quid dignum offeram Domino]] as if to say: I consider what has gone before, and henceforth I desire to be grateful; but what worthy thing shall I offer to the eternal God? [[6:6|wherewith shall I kneel before the high God|Curvabo genu Deo excelso]]? [literally "Shall I bow the knee to the most high God?"] This is read in two ways. First negatively, so that the sense is: kneeling of itself is not fit to appease God, since in itself it is nothing but a sign of devotion. And prayer without a good life is not worthy. For [[Prov 28:9|He that turneth away his ears from hearing the law, his prayer shall be an abomination|Qui enim declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis]]. Secondly it is read affirmatively, as an answer to the words before; and the sense will be that kneeling, prayer or adoration, in so far as they are acts of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone] and proceed from true devotion, are a worthy offering to God and a means of appeasing him, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:14|Offer to God the sacrifice of praise|Immola Deo sacrificium laudis]].

paras.t: Consequenter excluditur error confidentium in legalibus hostiis. Numquid offeram ei holocautomata, quæ totaliter incendebantur ad divinæ majestatis honorem, et vitulos anniculos, qui unius sunt anni ? tanquam dicat : Per sacrificia talia non fit debitus honor Deo, neque placatur, quoniam per se non sunt accepta, videlicet ex parte operis operati, sed operis operantis, utpote ex fide et caritate devotioneque offerentis. Et juxta hunc sensum subjungitur : Numquid placari potest Dominus in millibus arietum, aut in multis millibus hircorum pinguium, id est per immolationem immolaticiorum brutorum, quantumcumque multorum ? Impossibile quippe est sanguine hircorum et vitulorum auferri peccata, secundum Apostolum. Propter quod scriptum est apud Jeremiam : Numquid carnes sanctæ auferent a te malitias tuas ? Numquid dabo primogenitum meum pro scelere meo ? quod fecit rex Moab, secundum Hieronymum. Et numquid dabo fructum ventris mei, id est quamcumque prolem meam, pro peccato animæ meæ ? Quasi dicat : Non est talis oblatio placita Deo, quum innocentis occisio non sit divinæ æquitatis placatio. Hæc dicuntur ad insinuandum quod sacrificia legis non erant de se purgativa peccati. Quod vero Moyses ait in lege per talia Deum placari, vitiaque deleri, intelligendum fuit ex parte devotionis offerentium. Sic enim dicit Psalmista : Introibo in domum tuam in holocaustis ; et : Holocausta medullata offeram tibi cum incenso arietum ; offeram tibi boves cum hircis.
paras.en: Next the error of those who trust in the victims of the Law is ruled out. [[6:6|shall I offer holocausts unto him|Numquid offeram ei holocautomata]], which were wholly burnt in honour of the divine majesty, [[6:6|and calves of a year old|et vitulos anniculos]], which are one year old? as if to say: by such sacrifices due honour is not paid to God, nor is he appeased, since they are not acceptable of themselves, that is, by the work done, but by the work of the doer [*ex opere operato … operantis*: not by the mere performance of the rite, but by the dispositions of the one who offers it], namely from the faith, charity and devotion of the offerer. And in keeping with this sense it is added: [[6:7|May the Lord be appeased with thousands of rams, or with many thousands of fat he goats?|Numquid placari potest Dominus in millibus arietum, aut in multis millibus hircorum pinguium]] that is, by the immolation of brute beasts offered in sacrifice, however many? For [[Heb 10:4|it is impossible that with the blood of oxen and goats sin should be taken away|Impossibile quippe est sanguine hircorum et vitulorum auferri peccata]], according to the Apostle. For this reason it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 11:15|shall the holy flesh take away from thee thy crimes|Numquid carnes sanctæ auferent a te malitias tuas]]? [[6:7|shall I give my firstborn for my wickedness|Numquid dabo primogenitum meum pro scelere meo]]? as the king of Moab did, according to Jerome [see 4 Kings 3:27]. And shall I give [[6:7|the fruit of my body|fructum ventris mei]], that is, any offspring of mine, [[6:7|for the sin of my soul|pro peccato animæ meæ]]? As if to say: such an offering is not pleasing to God, since the slaying of the innocent does not appease the divine justice. These things are said to suggest that the sacrifices of the Law did not of themselves cleanse from sin. And where Moses says in the Law that God is appeased by such things and that faults are blotted out, this was to be understood on the part of the devotion of those offering. For so the Psalmist says: [[Ps 65:13|I will go into thy house with burnt offerings|Introibo in domum tuam in holocaustis]]; and: [[Ps 65:15|I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: I will offer to thee bullocks with goats|Holocausta medullata offeram tibi cum incenso arietum ; offeram tibi boves cum hircis]].

paras.t: Deinde ponitur quid digne Domino offeratur. Indicabo tibi, o homo, id est, o universum genus humanum, quid sit bonum, id est Deo acceptum et meritorium, et quid Dominus requirat a te pro beneficiis suis tibi collatis, non ad suam utilitatem, sed ob tuam salutem. Utique facere judicium justum subjectis et tibimetipsi, ut propria peccata dijudices et ulciscaris, ipsamque justitiam non in habitu tantum, sed in actu etiam habeas, nec sine ratione atque consilio aliquid agas. Loquitur ergo de ordinato judicio. Est autem et inordinatum judicium, scilicet temerarium vel usurpatorium, de quo ait Salvator : Nolite judicare, et non judicabimini. De prædicto autem ordinato judicio protestatur Apostolus : Si nosmetipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur ; et rursus, Sine præjudicio nihil facies, id est prævio judicio. In Job quoque libro habetur : Judicium eligamus, et inter nos videamus quid sit melius.
paras.en: Then is set down what may worthily be offered to the Lord. [[6:8|I will shew thee, O man|Indicabo tibi, o homo]], that is, O whole human race, [[6:8|what is good|quid sit bonum]], that is, acceptable to God and meritorious, [[6:8|and what the Lord requireth of thee|et quid Dominus requirat a te]] for his benefits bestowed on thee, not for his own advantage but for thy salvation. [[6:8|Verily to do judgment|Utique facere judicium]], just judgment, towards those under thee and towards thyself, so that thou judgest and punishest thy own sins, and hast justice itself not only as a habit but also in act, and doest nothing without reason and counsel. He speaks, then, of ordered judgment. But there is also a disordered judgment, namely rash or usurped judgment, of which the Saviour says: [[Luke 6:37|Judge not: and you shall not be judged|Nolite judicare, et non judicabimini]]. But of the ordered judgment just spoken of the Apostle declares: [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged|Si nosmetipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur]]; and again: [[1 Tim 5:21|without prejudice, doing nothing|Sine præjudicio nihil facies]], that is, without judgment going before [Denis takes *præjudicium* in the sense "judgment beforehand", that is, due deliberation]. In the book of Job too it is said: [[Job 34:4|Let us choose to us judgment, and let us see among ourselves what is the best|Judicium eligamus, et inter nos videamus quid sit melius]].

paras.t: Et diligere misericordiam, spirituales et corporales eleemosynas proximis impendendo ex caritatis prompto affectu, non ex necessitate aut coactione. Hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus. Beati siquidem misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequuntur. Per fidem namque et misericordiam purgantur peccata, ut dicitur in Proverbiis. Propter quod in Tobiæ libro inducitur : Quomodo potueris, ita esto misericors ; et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere. Hinc habetur et in Zacharia : Judicium verum judicate, et misericordiam et miserationes facite unusquisque cum proximo suo. Talis fuit beatus Job, qui fatetur : Flebam super eum qui afflictus erat, et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi ; et ab infantia crevit mecum miseratio.
paras.en: [[6:8|and to love mercy|Et diligere misericordiam]], by bestowing spiritual and corporal alms on one's neighbours out of the ready affection of charity, not of necessity or constraint. For [[2 Cor 9:7|God loveth a cheerful giver|Hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus]]. And indeed, [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati siquidem misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequuntur]]. For [[Prov 15:27|By mercy and faith sins are purged away|Per fidem namque et misericordiam purgantur peccata]], as is said in Proverbs [Denis has "by faith and mercy"]. For this reason it is set down in the book of Tobias: [[Tob 4:8|According to thy ability be merciful|Quomodo potueris, ita esto misericors]]; and [[Tob 4:7|turn not away thy face from any poor person|noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere]]. Hence it is also said in Zacharias: [[Zach 7:9|Judge ye true judgment, and shew ye mercy and compassion every man to his brother|Judicium verum judicate, et misericordiam et miserationes facite unusquisque cum proximo suo]] [Denis has "with his neighbour"]. Such was blessed Job, who confesses: [[Job 30:25|I wept heretofore for him that was afflicted, and my soul had compassion on the poor|Flebam super eum qui afflictus erat, et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi]]; and [[Job 31:18|from my infancy mercy grew up with me|ab infantia crevit mecum miseratio]].

paras.t: Et sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo, id est timorate in conspectu Altissimi conversari, per diligentem mandatorum observantiam et cordis custodiam, sicut hortatur Apostolus : Cum metu, inquiens, timore et tremore vestram salutem operamini. Hinc in Deuteronomio docetur : Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite ; ne obliviscaris verborum Domini Dei tui, et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ. In Marco quoque legitur : Videte, vigilate et orate. Hoc eminenter fecit sanctus Job, dicens : Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Dominum, et pondus ejus ferre non potui.
