Vere enim si perpendimus quam horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis, quanta sit nostra fragilitas, quam arduum sit animæ nostræ negotium, et quam indesinenter adspiciamur a Deo, sollicite ambulare conabimur cum Creatore altissimo, dicentes singuli illud Job : Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest ; et anima ejus quodcumque voluit fecit : idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor. Hæc est enim laudabilis sollicitudo, quæ maxime pertinet ad prælatos : qui tanto sollicitiores esse tenentur, quanto pro pluribus reddituri sunt rationem. Propter quod dicit Apostolus ad Romanos : Qui præest, in sollicitudine. O quam compendiosum ac saluberrimum est prædictum sancti Michæ documentum, jugiter revolvendum !
paras.en: [[6:8|and to walk solicitous with thy God|Et sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo]]: that is, to live in fear in the sight of the Most High, by diligent keeping of the commandments and guarding of the heart, as the Apostle exhorts: [[Phil 2:12|with fear|Cum metu]], he says, [[Phil 2:12|and trembling work out your salvation|timore et tremore vestram salutem operamini]] [Denis's text has "with fear, dread and trembling"]. Hence it is taught in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]: [[Deut 4:9|Forget not the words|ne obliviscaris verborum]] of the Lord thy God, [[Deut 4:9|and let them not go out of thy heart all the days of thy life|et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ]]. In Mark too we read: [[Mark 13:33|Take ye heed, watch and pray|Videte, vigilate et orate]]. This holy Job did in an eminent degree, saying: [[Job 31:23|I have always feared God as waves swelling over me, and his weight I was unable to bear|Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Dominum, et pondus ejus ferre non potui]]. For truly, if we consider that [[Heb 10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God|horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis]], how great is our frailty, how hard is the business of our soul, and how unceasingly we are beheld by God, we shall strive to walk solicitously with the most high Creator, each of us saying that word of Job: [[Job 23:13|he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought: and whatsoever his soul hath desired, that hath he done|Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest ; et anima ejus quodcumque voluit fecit]]: [[Job 23:15|therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor]] [*timore sollicitor*, literally "I am made solicitous with fear", echoing *sollicitum ambulare*]. For this is the praiseworthy solicitude which belongs above all to prelates, who are bound to be the more solicitous as they are to render an account for more. For this reason the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 12:8|he that ruleth, with carefulness|Qui præest, in sollicitudine]]. O how brief and how wholesome is this teaching of holy Micheas, to be pondered without ceasing!

paras.t: Vox Domini ad civitatem clamat, id est, prædictum sermonem, vel verba sequentia Deus per me ad Synagogam profatur ; et salus, id est æterna felicitas, erit timentibus nomen tuum, o Domine, casto ac filiali timore, vel etiam initiali, qui non differt realiter, sed gradualiter a timore filiali, dummodo finaliter perseverent. Unde in Ecclesiastico habetur : Timor Domini delectabit cor, et dabit gaudium et lætitiam in longitudinem dierum. Timenti Deum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis benedicetur. In Proverbiis quoque : In timore Domini esto tota die, quia habebis spem in novissimo. Et in Isaia : Dominum exercituum ipsum sanctificate ; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester. Denique, Beatus homo qui semper est pavidus ; et, Qui sine timore est, non potest justificari ; et, Nisi te instanter tenueris in timore Dei, cito subvertetur domus tua.
paras.en: [[6:9|The voice of the Lord crieth to the city|Vox Domini ad civitatem clamat]]: that is, God through me utters to the Synagogue the discourse just given, or the words that follow; [[6:9|and salvation|et salus]], that is, eternal happiness, [[6:9|shall be to them that fear thy name|erit timentibus nomen tuum]], O Lord, with a chaste and filial fear, or even with initial fear [that is, the fear of a beginner, between servile fear of punishment and the filial fear of offending God], which differs from filial fear not really but in degree, provided they persevere to the end. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:12|The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart, and shall give joy, and gladness, and length of days.|Timor Domini delectabit cor, et dabit gaudium et lætitiam in longitudinem dierum]] [[Ecclus 1:13|With him that feareth the Lord, it shall go well in the latter end, and in the day of his death he shall be blessed.|Timenti Deum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis benedicetur]] In Proverbs also: [[Prov 23:17|be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long|In timore Domini esto tota die]]: [[Prov 23:18|Because thou shalt have hope in the latter end|quia habebis spem in novissimo]]. And in Isaias: [[Is 8:13|Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.|Dominum exercituum ipsum sanctificate ; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester]] Again: [[Prov 28:14|Blessed is the man that is always fearful|Beatus homo qui semper est pavidus]]; and: [[Ecclus 1:28|he that is without fear, cannot be justified|Qui sine timore est, non potest justificari]]; and: [[Ecclus 27:4|Unless thou hold thyself diligently in the fear of the Lord, thy house shall quickly be overthrown.|Nisi te instanter tenueris in timore Dei, cito subvertetur domus tua]]

paras.t: Consequenter arguitur populus Israel de vitio fraudis et injustitiæ. Audite, tribus, id est, popule Israel per tribus duodecim distinctus. Et quis approbabit illud ? id est, quis verbo meo consentiet atque obediet ? tanquam dicat, Perpauci. Cujus subditur causa : Adhuc ignis, id est fervens iniquitas, est in domo impii, id est in familia, imo in corde et anima hominis pravi. Quod specialiter refertur ad domum Amri patris Achab, quorum uterque pessimus fuit. De hoc igne dictum est in Osee : Omnes adulterantes quasi clibanus succensus a coquente. Thesauri iniquitatis, id est bona injuste possessa, vel copiosa iniquitas, secundum quod dictum est ab Amos : Nescierunt facere rectum, thesaurizantes iniquitatem ; et mensura minor, per quam datur alteri non tantum ut justum est, sed diminute persolvitur, iræ plena, id est magnam vindictam efflagitans, quum sit contra justitiam et mortale peccatum.
paras.en: Next the people of Israel is rebuked for the vice of fraud and injustice. [[6:9|hear O ye tribes|Audite, tribus]], that is, O people of Israel, divided into twelve tribes. [[6:9|and who shall approve it|Et quis approbabit illud]]? that is, who will consent to my word and obey it? as if to say: very few. The reason for this is added: [[6:10|As yet there is a fire|Adhuc ignis]], that is, burning iniquity, [[6:10|in the house of the wicked|in domo impii]], that is, in the household, nay, in the heart and soul of the wicked man. This refers especially to the house of Amri, the father of Achab, each of whom was most wicked[[3 Kings 16:25||]][[3 Kings 16:30||]]. Of this fire it is said in Osee: [[Osee 7:4|They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker|Omnes adulterantes quasi clibanus succensus a coquente]]. [[6:10|the treasures of iniquity|Thesauri iniquitatis]], that is, goods unjustly possessed, or abundant iniquity, according to what was said by Amos: [[Amos 3:10|they have not known to do the right thing|Nescierunt facere rectum]], [[Amos 3:10|storing up iniquity|thesaurizantes iniquitatem]]; [[6:10|and a scant measure|et mensura minor]], by which another is given not as much as is just, but is paid short, [[6:10|full of wrath|iræ plena]], that is, calling down great vengeance, since it is against justice and a mortal sin.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus ait : Numquid justificabo stateram impiam, id est fallacem, et saccelli pondera dolosa ? In quibus ponderibus divites ejus, scilicet populi Israel, et non solum egeni, qui per necessitatem inopiæ aliqualiter excusari posse videntur, repleti sunt iniquitate, id est injustis divitiis, vel multiplici gravique culpa, quoniam enormiter peccaverunt ista agendo ; et habitantes in ea, videlicet in terra Israel, vel perseverantes in ista iniquitate, loquebantur mendacium perniciosum : quod avaritiam concomitatur et fraudem ; et lingua eorum fraudulenta in ore eorum : quum tamen Isaias dicat, Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt ; et Psalmista, Virum sanguinum et dolosum abominabitur Dominus. Porro, quum Deus sit justus, et virtus ejus justitiæ sit initium, ut dicitur in libro Sapientiæ, constat vitia ista ei plurimum displicere. Propter quod ait in Levitico : Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura.
paras.en: Next the Lord says: [[6:11|Shall I justify wicked balances|Numquid justificabo stateram impiam]], that is, false ones, [[6:11|and the deceitful weights of the bag|et saccelli pondera dolosa]]? [[6:12|By which her rich men|In quibus ponderibus divites ejus]], namely of the people of Israel, and not only the needy, who seem able to be excused in some measure by the necessity of want, [[6:12|were filled with iniquity|repleti sunt iniquitate]], that is, with unjust riches, or with manifold and grievous guilt, since they sinned enormously in doing these things; [[6:12|and the inhabitants thereof|et habitantes in ea]], namely in the land of Israel, or those persevering in this iniquity, [[6:12|have spoken lies|loquebantur mendacium perniciosum]] [Denis's text adds *perniciosum*: "pernicious lies"], which go along with avarice and fraud; [[6:12|and their tongue was deceitful in their mouth|et lingua eorum fraudulenta in ore eorum]]: though Isaias says: [[Is 32:7|The vessels of the deceitful are most wicked|Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 5:7|The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor|Virum sanguinum et dolosum abominabitur Dominus]]. Moreover, since God is just, and his [[Wis 12:16|power is the beginning of justice|virtus ejus justitiæ sit initium]], as is said in the book of Wisdom, it is clear that these vices displease him exceedingly. For this reason he says in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:35|Do not any unjust thing in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure.|Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura]]

paras.t: Horum autem vitiorum debita pœna subjungitur : Et ego ergo cœpi percutere te perditione, id est captivitate et aliis plagis, super peccatis tuis : hoc est, non repente, nec statim volui vos subvertere, sed paulatim cœpi percutere, ut variis plagis ad pœnitentiam provocarem. Decem enim tribus primo partim vastatæ sunt a Phul, deinde a Theglathphalasar, postremo atque totaliter a rege Salmanasar. Tu comedes, et non saturaberis : et sic mittam famem in vos ex terræ sterilitate, seu hostium destructione vastantium terræ nascentia ; et humiliatio tua, id est dejectio, erit in medio tui, ita quod undique in propria terra ab adversariis confunderis. Et apprehendes quosdam afflictos de populo tuo a facie hostium fugientes, et non salvabis, id est, a captivitate non eripies eos ; et quos salvaveris, id est, ad tempus absconderis, in gladium dabo, ita quod ab hostibus invenientur et trucidabuntur.
paras.en: The due punishment of these vices is added: [[6:13|And I therefore began to strike thee with desolation|Et ego ergo cœpi percutere te perditione]], that is, with captivity and other plagues, [[6:13|for thy sins|super peccatis tuis]]: that is, I did not will to overthrow you suddenly or at once, but I began to strike little by little, that by various plagues I might call you to repentance. For the ten tribes were first laid waste in part by Phul[[4 Kings 15:19||]], then by Theglathphalasar[[4 Kings 15:29||]], and lastly and wholly by king Salmanasar[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. [[6:14|Thou shalt eat, but shalt not be filled|Tu comedes, et non saturaberis]]: and so I will send famine upon you through the barrenness of the land, or through the destruction wrought by enemies laying waste the produce of the land; [[6:14|and thy humiliation|et humiliatio tua]], that is, thy casting down, [[6:14|shall be in the midst of thee|erit in medio tui]], so that on every side, in thy own land, thou shalt be put to confusion by thy adversaries. [[6:14|and thou shalt take hold|Et apprehendes]] of some of thy people, afflicted and fleeing from the face of the enemy, [[6:14|but shalt not save|et non salvabis]], that is, thou shalt not rescue them from captivity; [[6:14|and those whom thou shalt save|et quos salvaveris]], that is, shalt hide for a time, [[6:14|I will give up to the sword|in gladium dabo]], so that they will be found by the enemy and slaughtered.

paras.t: Tu seminabis, et non metes : quoniam fruges diripientur ab Assyriis, vel eruca, brucho, locusta, seu rubigine destruentur, ut dictum est in Joele de populo Juda ac Israel. Tu calcabis olivam, et non ungeris oleo : vel quia oliva non erit fructifera, vel quia oleum tuum auferetur ab æmulis ; et mustum facies, et non bibes vinum, propter easdem causas.
paras.en: [[6:15|Thou shalt sow, but shalt not reap|Tu seminabis, et non metes]]: because the crops will be carried off by the Assyrians, or destroyed by the palmerworm, the bruchus, the locust or the mildew, as was said in Joel of the people of Juda and Israel[[Joel 1:4||]]. [[6:15|thou shalt tread the olives, but shalt not be anointed with oil|Tu calcabis olivam, et non ungeris oleo]]: either because the olive will bear no fruit, or because thy oil will be taken away by thy foes; [[6:15|and the new wine, but shalt not drink the wine|et mustum facies, et non bibes vinum]] [Denis has "and thou shalt make new wine"], for the same reasons.

paras.t: Quod autem ista ad decem tribus specialiter referantur, ostendit quod subditur : Et custodisti præcepta Amri regis Israel ; et omne opus domus Achab, id est instituta idololatriæ, et opera Achab atque familiæ ejus, secutus es, pessime conversando. Et ambulasti in voluptatibus eorum, id est carnalibus vitiis delectationibusque actus vitiosos concomitantibus, ut darem te in perditionem, id est captivitatem atque æternam damnationem, et habitantes in ea, id est habitatores Samariæ, in sibilum, id est derisionem, quæ flatu oris ostenditur ; et opprobrium populi mei portabis, tolerando mala pœnalia, quæ ex antiquo consuevi infligere filiis Israel, dum graviter peccaverunt. Dictio, ut, notat hoc loco sequelam, non causam : non enim idcirco peccaverunt, ut punirentur, sed culpam consecuta est pœna.
paras.en: That these things refer especially to the ten tribes is shown by what follows: [[6:16|For thou hast kept the statutes of Amri|Et custodisti præcepta Amri]], king of Israel; [[6:16|and all the works of the house of Achab|et omne opus domus Achab]], that is, the ordinances of idolatry and the works of Achab and his household, thou hast followed, living most wickedly. [[6:16|and thou hast walked according their wills|Et ambulasti in voluptatibus eorum]] [Denis reads *voluptatibus*, "pleasures", for the Vulgate's *voluntatibus*, "wills", and glosses accordingly], that is, in the carnal vices and the delights that go with vicious acts, [[6:16|that I should make thee a desolation|ut darem te in perditionem]], that is, captivity and eternal damnation, [[6:16|and the inhabitants thereof|et habitantes in ea]], that is, the dwellers in Samaria, [[6:16|a hissing|in sibilum]], that is, a mockery, which is shown by a blowing of the mouth; [[6:16|and you shall bear the reproach of my people|et opprobrium populi mei portabis]], by enduring the penal evils which from of old I have been wont to inflict on the children of Israel when they sinned grievously. The word *that* [*ut*] here denotes consequence, not cause: for they did not sin in order to be punished, but punishment followed upon guilt.

6.title: Mystica ejusdem capituli sexti expositio.
6.title_en: Mystical exposition of the same sixth chapter.

paras.t: Nunc moralitas hujus capituli breviter est tangenda. Ait itaque Dominus viro sancto ac prædicatori condigno, præsertim summo Antistiti: Surge, contende judicio adversus montes, id est negligentes prælatos, superbos vitiososque principes, illorum redarguendo peccata, et subditorum perditionem retorquendo in eos: quia enim stulte egerunt pastores, omnis grex eorum dissipatus est, ut loquitur Jeremias. Hoc fecit sapiens ille, qui ait: Præbete aures, vos qui continetis multitudines, quoniam data est vobis potestas a Deo, qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur; cito et horrende apparebit vobis, quoniam judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet. Et audiant colles, id est, qui inferioris potestatis et gradus sunt, puta vicarii, vocem tuam, id est prædicationem seu contentionem contra prælatos, quia eadem pœna imminet eis, si fuerint negligentes.
paras.en: Now the moral sense of this chapter is to be touched on briefly. The Lord therefore says to a holy man and worthy preacher, above all to the supreme Pontiff [Latin *summus Antistes*, the highest bishop, that is, the Pope]: [[6:1|Arise, contend thou in judgment against the mountains|Surge, contende judicio adversus montes]], that is, against negligent prelates and proud and vicious princes, by reproving their sins and turning the ruin of their subjects back upon them: for since [[Jer 10:21|the pastors have done foolishly|stulte egerunt pastores]], [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]], as Jeremias says. This the wise man did, who says: [[Wis 6:3|Give ear, you that rule the people|Præbete aures, vos qui continetis multitudines]], [[Wis 6:4|For power is given you by the Lord|quoniam data est vobis potestas a Deo]], [[Wis 6:4|who will examine your works: and search out your thoughts|qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur]]; [[Wis 6:6|Horribly and speedily will he appear to you: for a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule.|cito et horrende apparebit vobis, quoniam judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]] [[6:1|and let the hills hear|Et audiant colles]], that is, those who are of lower power and rank, vicars for example, [[6:1|thy voice|vocem tuam]], that is, the preaching or contention against the prelates, because the same punishment hangs over them if they are negligent.

paras.t: Audiant montes judicium Domini, qui sanguinem pereuntium requiret de manu eorum, et ait per Ezechielem: Væ pastoribus qui pascebant semetipsos; itemque per Jeremiam: Dic regi et dominatrici, Humiliamini; et fortia fundamenta terræ, id est litterati et doctores, quorum est alios sustentare. Quia judicium Domini erit cum populo suo Christiano; et cum Israel, id est Ecclesia per fidem speculante divina, dijudicabitur in die generalis judicii, quando omnibus innotescet æquitas judicii Dei contra Christifideles iniquos: quibus melius fuisset viam veritatis nescisse, quam post cognitionem reverti retrorsum.
paras.en: [[6:2|Let the mountains hear the judgment of the Lord|Audiant montes judicium Domini]], who will require the blood of those who perish at their hand[[Ezech 3:18||]][[Ezech 3:20||]], and who says through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:2|Woe to the shepherds|Væ pastoribus]] [[Ezech 34:2|that fed themselves|qui pascebant semetipsos]]; and likewise through Jeremias: [[Jer 13:18|Say to the king, and to the queen: Humble yourselves|Dic regi et dominatrici, Humiliamini]]; [[6:2|and the strong foundations of the earth|et fortia fundamenta terræ]], that is, the lettered and the doctors, whose part it is to hold others up. [[6:2|for the Lord will enter into judgment with his people|Quia judicium Domini erit cum populo suo]], the Christian people; and [[6:2|against Israel|cum Israel]], that is, the Church, which by faith beholds divine things, [[6:2|he will plead|dijudicabitur]] on the day of the general judgment, when the equity of God's judgment against wicked Christians will be made known to all: for whom [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|melius fuisset viam veritatis nescisse, quam post cognitionem reverti retrorsum]] [Denis has "the way of truth" where the Douay-Rheims has "the way of justice"].

paras.t: Popule meus, Christiane ingrate, quid feci tibi? aut quid molestus fui tibi? Responde mihi. Quia eduxi te de terra Ægypti, id est sæculari conversatione et potestate ac regno diaboli, sicut ait Apostolus: Eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam; et de domo servitutis, id est vitiis carnis, ut non sis in carne, sed in spiritu. Qui enim in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt. Vel, De domo servitutis, id est aggregatione iniquorum, juxta illud in Psalmo: Protexisti me a conventu malignantium: ubi diabolo et concupiscentiis deservitur. Hæc beneficia contulit nobis Christus meritorie in sua passione: tunc enim meruit nobis gratiam ad omnia ista. In sacramento vero Baptismi ac Pœnitentiæ tribuit ista actualiter. Aliqui autem recidivant atque ingrati sunt infinitis ac summis beneficiis Salvatoris. Et misi ante faciem tuam Moysen et Aaron, id est Christum hominem, legislatorem et sacerdotem altissimum, qui per Moysen Aaronque figuratus cognoscitur, et Mariam, quæ est advocata nostra ac mediatrix peroptima, cujus figura fuit Maria prophetes Moysis soror.
paras.en: [[6:3|O my people|Popule meus]], ungrateful Christian, [[6:3|what have I done to thee, or in what have I molested thee? answer thou me|quid feci tibi? aut quid molestus fui tibi? Responde mihi]]. [[6:4|For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt|Quia eduxi te de terra Ægypti]], that is, out of worldly life and out of the power and kingdom of the devil, as the Apostle says that Christ came to [[Gal 1:4|deliver us from this present wicked world|Eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam]]; [[6:4|and delivered thee out of the house of slaves|et de domo servitutis]], that is, from the vices of the flesh, so that thou art not in the flesh but in the spirit. For [[Rom 8:8|they who are in the flesh cannot please God|Qui enim in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt]]. Or, [[6:4|out of the house of slaves|De domo servitutis]], that is, out of the gathering of the wicked, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 63:3|Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant|Protexisti me a conventu malignantium]], where the devil and the concupiscences are served. These benefits Christ conferred on us by way of merit in his passion, for then he merited for us the grace for all of them; but in the sacraments of Baptism and Penance he bestows them in act [that is, the passion earned these graces for all, and the sacraments give them to each one]. Yet some fall back and are ungrateful for the infinite and supreme benefits of the Saviour. [[6:4|and I sent before thy face Moses, and Aaron|Et misi ante faciem tuam Moysen et Aaron]], that is, Christ as man, the lawgiver and most high priest, who is known to have been prefigured by Moses and Aaron, [[6:4|and Mary|et Mariam]], who is our advocate and most excellent mediatrix, whose figure was Mary the prophetess, the sister of Moses.

paras.t: Popule meus, memento, quæso, quid cogitaverit Balac rex Moab, id est machinationes diaboli regis impiorum, qui multis fraudibus conatur tuam impedire salutem, ne terram viventium (in qua ipse fuit) possideas. Est quoque grave diabolo, dum veri religiosi et prædicatores idonei terram suam, id est iniquos, visitant atque operiunt: metuens ne convertantur, et suo imperio subtrahantur per verba et exempla justorum, quemadmodum Balac formidavit terram suam a filiis Israel occupandam ac possidendam. Balac autem interpretatur lingens: per quem designatur diabolus, subsannationem quasi aquam bibens, et animas glutiens. Absorbet enim fluvium nec miratur, et habet fiduciam quod influat Jordanis in os ejus. Moab vero interpretatur, ex patre: per quem designantur iniqui, quibus apud Joannem loquitur Christus: Vos ex patre diabolo estis. Et Joannes in prima sua epistola: Qui facit peccatum, ex diabolo est. Et quid responderit ei Balaam, id est homines animarum corruptores, qui realiter responsum dant dæmoni, consentiendo et cooperando eidem in subversione proximorum suorum. Hi enim una cum principe suo diabolo nituntur maledicere populum prædestinatum; sed Deus convertit maledictionem in benedictionem, quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum. Debemus ergo perpendere invisibilium et visibilium hostium insidias contra nos, et quomodo auxiliante gratia Dei evadimus, qui propria potestate et industria nequaquam prævalere possemus.
paras.en: [[6:5|O my people, remember, I pray thee, what Balach, the king of Moab, purposed|Popule meus, memento, quæso, quid cogitaverit Balac rex Moab]], that is, the schemes of the devil, the king of the wicked, who by many frauds strives to hinder thy salvation, lest thou possess the land of the living (in which he himself once was). It is grievous to the devil, too, when true religious and fit preachers visit and cover his land, that is, the wicked: for he fears that they may be converted and withdrawn from his rule by the words and examples of the just, just as Balac dreaded that his land would be occupied and possessed by the children of Israel[[Num 22:2||]] [the margin gives Num. xxii, 2–6]. Now Balac is interpreted *licking*: by him is designated the devil, who [[Job 34:7|drinketh up scorning like water|subsannationem quasi aquam bibens]], and swallows souls. For [[Job 40:18|he will drink up a river, and not wonder: and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth|Absorbet enim fluvium nec miratur, et habet fiduciam quod influat Jordanis in os ejus]] [the margin gives Ibid. xl, 18, that is, Job 40:18, which is said of Behemoth]. And Moab is interpreted *from the father*: by him are designated the wicked, to whom Christ says in John: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]. And John in his first epistle: [[1 John 3:8|He that committeth sin is of the devil|Qui facit peccatum, ex diabolo est]]. [[6:5|and what|Et quid]] [[6:5|Balaam|Balaam]] [[6:5|answered him|responderit ei]], that is, men who corrupt souls, who in deed give their answer to the demon by consenting to him and working with him for the overthrow of their neighbours. For these, together with their prince the devil, strive to curse the predestined people; but God turns the curse into a blessing, since [[Rom 8:28|to them that love God all things work together unto good|diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum]]. We ought therefore to weigh the snares laid against us by our enemies, invisible and visible, and how by the help of God's grace we escape them, we who by our own power and effort could never prevail.

paras.t: Quid dignum offeram Domino? etc. Totum hoc dicitur ad insinuandum quod sine effusione sanguinis Christi, et virtute ac merito ejus, Deo placere nequimus, quamvis nos ipsos, et omnia interiora exterioraque nostra obtulerimus ei; ad innuendum quoque quod tanta sunt nobis a Christo beneficia pie exhibita, quod rependere nil condignum valemus.
paras.en: [[6:6|What shall I offer to the Lord that is worthy?|Quid dignum offeram Domino?]] etc. All this is said to suggest that without the shedding of Christ's blood, and without his power and merit, we cannot please God, even though we should offer him ourselves and all that is ours, within and without; and also to hint that the benefits Christ has lovingly shown us are so great that we can repay nothing worthy of them.

paras.t: Indicabo tibi, o homo, quid sit bonum: Utique facere judicium, et diligere misericordiam. Quilibet ergo discutiat, increpet, damnet et vindicet propria mala, disciplinando se ipsum, et multipliciter castigando corpus suum. Sitque clemens in alios, protinus indulgendo, liberaliter communicando, caritative compatiendo, quemadmodum ait Apostolus ad Ephesios: Estote invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis; et alibi, Alter alterius onera portate; et, Flete cum flentibus. Et sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo. Omnis ergo levitas et cachinnus, omnis dissolutio et scurrilitas evitentur. Hoc fecit ille sanctus eremita, qui fratrem ridere conspiciens, dixit: Coram cœlo et terra rationem reddituri sumus: et tu rides?
paras.en: [[6:8|I will shew thee, O man, what is good|Indicabo tibi, o homo, quid sit bonum]]: [[6:8|Verily to do judgment, and to love mercy|Utique facere judicium, et diligere misericordiam]]. Let each one, then, examine, rebuke, condemn and punish his own evils, disciplining himself and chastising his body in many ways. And let him be gentle towards others, forgiving at once, sharing generously, sympathizing in charity, as the Apostle says to the Ephesians: [[Eph 4:32|be ye kind one to another: merciful, forgiving one another, even as God hath forgiven you in Christ|Estote invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis]]; and elsewhere: [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]]; and: [[Rom 12:15|weep with them that weep|Flete cum flentibus]]. [[6:8|and to walk solicitous with thy God|Et sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo]]. Let all levity and loud laughter, then, all dissipation and buffoonery, be avoided. This is what that holy hermit did who, seeing a brother laugh, said: We are to render an account before heaven and earth, and dost thou laugh?

paras.t: Vox Domini, id est sacra Scriptura, et prædicatio justorum, ad civitatem clamat, id est ad Ecclesiam, quatenus mali pœniteant, boni proficiant, et universi salventur. Adhuc ignis carnalis concupiscentiæ, iræ, furoris et cupiditatis, in domo, id est corpore vel populo, impii præsidentis. Qualis enim rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea. Thesauri iniquitatis, qui sibi thesaurizat iram in die justi judicii Dei, et quasi longam restim trahit peccatum, peccatis veteribus nova adjiciens, et gloriatur in his, quasi in omnibus divitiis, imo frequenter multa mala se jactat fecisse, quæ non fecit. Et mensura minor, id est injustum judicium atque acceptio personarum, dum non facit omnibus æquum judicium, sed unum præ alio palpat, iræ plena, quia per hoc Dei iram incurrit, magnamque pœnam meretur.
paras.en: [[6:9|The voice of the Lord|Vox Domini]], that is, Holy Scripture and the preaching of the just, [[6:9|crieth to the city|ad civitatem clamat]], that is, to the Church, so that the wicked may repent, the good make progress, and all be saved. [[6:10|As yet there is a fire|Adhuc ignis]] of carnal concupiscence, of anger, rage and covetousness, [[6:10|in the house|in domo]], that is, in the body or the people, [[6:10|of the wicked|impii]] ruler. For [[Ecclus 10:2|what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Qualis enim rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea]]. [[6:10|the treasures of iniquity|Thesauri iniquitatis]]: of him who treasures up wrath for himself against the day of the just judgment of God[[Rom 2:5||]], and draws sin along like a long rope[[Is 5:18||]], adding new sins to the old, and glories in them as in all riches; nay, he often boasts of having done many evils that he has not done. [[6:10|and a scant measure|Et mensura minor]], that is, unjust judgment and respect of persons, when he does not judge equally for all but favours one before another, [[6:10|full of wrath|iræ plena]], because by this he incurs the wrath of God and merits a great punishment.

paras.t: Numquid justificabo stateram impiam, et saccelli pondera dolosa? Hoc contra Christianos qui in suis mercaturis fraudibus utuntur, sit dictum: qui sciant non dimitti peccatum, nisi restituatur ablatum. De talibus legitur in Psalmo: Verumtamen vani filii hominum, mendaces filii hominum in stateris, ut decipiant ipsi de vanitate in id ipsum. Hi diversis mendaciis polluunt linguas et animas suas. Contra quos ait Scriptura: Os quod mentitur, occidit animam.
paras.en: [[6:11|Shall I justify wicked balances, and the deceitful weights of the bag?|Numquid justificabo stateram impiam, et saccelli pondera dolosa?]] Let this be said against Christians who use frauds in their trading: let them know that the sin is not forgiven unless what was taken is restored [a saying of Augustine, Letter 153]. Of such we read in the Psalm: [[Ps 61:10|But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: that by vanity they may together deceive|Verumtamen vani filii hominum, mendaces filii hominum in stateris, ut decipiant ipsi de vanitate in id ipsum]]. These pollute their tongues and their souls with lies of many kinds. Against them Scripture says: [[Wis 1:11|the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul|Os quod mentitur, occidit animam]].

paras.t: Et ego ergo cœpi percutere te perditione, id est gratiæ subtractione. Prima enim pœna peccati mortalis, est caritatis et gratiæ seu spiritualis vitæ amissio.
paras.en: [[6:13|And I therefore began to strike thee with desolation|Et ego ergo cœpi percutere te perditione]], that is, by the withdrawal of grace. For the first punishment of mortal sin is the loss of charity and grace, that is, of the spiritual life.

paras.t: Tu comedes, et non saturaberis, id est, aliquid boni facies, et verbum Dei audies, sed fructum justitiæ, et delectationem sanctam in Deo non consequeris. Vix enim est aliquis Christianus adeo pravus, quin in aliquo sequatur ritum Ecclesiæ, et aliqua bona ex genere operetur. Et humiliatio tua in medio tui, id est, intus dæmoni atque peccatis subjiceris, vilificaris, et confusione dignus consistis. Et apprehendes aliqua opera bona de genere ex consuetudine, visitando ecclesiam, orando, seu jejunando, et non salvabis per hæc te ipsum, quum non sint meritoria, quoniam caritate privatus es, et mortuus coram Deo. Et quos salvaveris, in gladium dabo: quia si aliquid meritorie egeris, per tentationem diaboli vel propriam concupiscentiam auferetur a te. Hoc de reprobis verum est, qui ad tempus credunt, sed tempore tentationis recedunt.
paras.en: [[6:14|Thou shalt eat, but shalt not be filled|Tu comedes, et non saturaberis]], that is, thou wilt do some good and hear the word of God, but thou wilt not obtain the fruit of justice and holy delight in God. For there is hardly any Christian so depraved that he does not follow the rite of the Church in something and do some works that are good in their kind [that is, good by what they are, though done without charity they earn no merit]. [[6:14|and thy humiliation shall be in the midst of thee|Et humiliatio tua in medio tui]], that is, inwardly thou art made subject to the demon and to sins, art made vile, and standest worthy of confusion. [[6:14|and thou shalt take hold|Et apprehendes]] of some works good in their kind, out of habit, visiting the church, praying or fasting, [[6:14|but shalt not save|et non salvabis]] thyself by them, since they are not meritorious, for thou art deprived of charity and dead before God. [[6:14|and those whom thou shalt save, I will give up to the sword|Et quos salvaveris, in gladium dabo]]: because if thou hast done anything meritoriously, it will be taken from thee through the temptation of the devil or thy own concupiscence. This is true of the reprobate, who [[Luke 8:13|believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|ad tempus credunt, sed tempore tentationis recedunt]].

paras.t: Tu seminabis opera bona, et non metes vitam æternam, quia non perseveras usque in finem. Tu calcabis olivam, legendo Scripturas, et non ungeris oleo, id est, veritatis dulcedinem non gustabis; et mustum, et non bibes vinum, sequendo litteram occidentem, non spiritum vivificantem, in quo est vinum de quo Sapientia loquitur: Bibite vinum quod miscui vobis.
paras.en: [[6:15|Thou shalt sow|Tu seminabis]] good works, [[6:15|but shalt not reap|et non metes]] eternal life, because thou dost not persevere unto the end[[Matt 10:22||]]. [[6:15|thou shalt tread the olives|Tu calcabis olivam]] by reading the Scriptures, [[6:15|but shalt not be anointed with oil|et non ungeris oleo]], that is, thou shalt not taste the sweetness of truth[[1 Pet 2:3||]]; [[6:15|and the new wine, but shalt not drink the wine|et mustum, et non bibes vinum]], by following the letter that kills, not the spirit that gives life[[2 Cor 3:6||]], in which is the wine of which Wisdom speaks: [[Prov 9:5|drink the wine which I have mingled for you|Bibite vinum quod miscui vobis]].

paras.t: Et custodisti præcepta Amri, et omne opus domus Achab, id est, impiorum principum et indignorum atque carnalium prælatorum prava jussa et facta maligna secutus es. Quamvis enim obediendum est superioribus, non solum bonis, sed etiam dyscolis; non tamen nisi in licitis et honestis, non in his quæ sunt contra Deum et Ecclesiam rectamque rationem. Et ambulasti in voluptatibus (seu voluntatibus), id est in deliciis et adinventionibus eorum, quia et ideo multi applaudunt illis, ut delicate ab ipsis nutriantur, ut darem te in perditionem damnationis æternæ, et in sibilum, ita quod dæmones tibi insultabunt in pœnis, qui te jam inducunt ad vitia, juxta illud in Psalmo: Qui tribulant me, exsultabunt, si motus fuero.
paras.en: [[6:16|For thou hast kept the statutes of Amri, and all the works of the house of Achab|Et custodisti præcepta Amri, et omne opus domus Achab]], that is, thou hast followed the wicked commands and evil deeds of impious princes and of unworthy and carnal prelates. For although obedience is owed to superiors, [[1 Pet 2:18|not only to the good|non solum bonis]] [[1 Pet 2:18|but also to the froward|sed etiam dyscolis]], yet only in what is lawful and honest, not in what is against God, the Church and right reason. [[6:16|and thou hast walked|Et ambulasti]] in pleasures (or, [[6:16|according their wills|voluntatibus]]) [Denis's text reads *in voluptatibus*, "in pleasures", and gives the Vulgate's *in voluntatibus*, "in their wills", as another reading], that is, in their delights and inventions; for this is why many applaud them, that they may be delicately fed by them: [[6:16|that I should make thee a desolation|ut darem te in perditionem]] of eternal damnation, and [[6:16|a hissing|in sibilum]], in that the demons, who now lead thee into vices, will mock thee in thy torments, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 12:5|They that trouble me, will rejoice when I am moved|Qui tribulant me, exsultabunt, si motus fuero]].
